This Week’s Two Blocks (the answer to “what do I do right now?”)

You each get roughly 7-10 hours a week around the day job — call it 90 minutes on weekday mornings plus one longer weekend block. That is the real budget, so plan in 90-minute units, not in “days.” Write one commitment each on Monday; it saves automatically and stays until you change it.

Mike — this week’s 90-minute block

Default if you are unsure: whatever the Readiness Score below names as your weakest dimension. If the pipeline is empty, it is always prospects and outreach — never a new build.

Paola — this week’s 90-minute block

Default if you are unsure: score this week’s client calls, then two referral-partner touches. If a client signed this week, the handoff and 10-call test come first.

Stop-when rules, so a half-finished block is never a disaster: a build block ends when the thing you started answers or sends — not when it is perfect. An outreach block ends when the batch is sent, even if the list is shorter than planned. Write down the next single action before you close the laptop; that is what you open with next time.

Pick Your Track (do this once, then ignore the other one)

Three different calendars in this course each claim “Day 1,” and they disagree on purpose — they are two different strategies, not two descriptions of the same one. Choose by one question: do you need revenue this month, or do you have runway? Then follow only that column and treat the other one’s day numbers as if they don’t exist.

Our track: Pick one — the day counter and the Friday scorecard both adapt to it.
Track A

Sell First (21-Day Money Sprint)

Choose if: you need cash this month, or a paying client is the only thing that will keep you both motivated.

The rule: nothing gets built unless a prospect asked for it or paid for it. You sell from Day 3 with a demo, not a finished product.

Your path: the 21-Day Sprint, plus Days 1, 2, 4, 5 and 7 of the click-by-click steps page ↗ — accounts, server, Vapi agent, refine, test. That is the smallest set that actually produces a callable demo: Day 5 refines what Day 4 builds, and Day 7 tests the Day 4 webhook. Skip Days 3, 6 and 8-14 until a client is paying.

Track B

Build First (Full 15-Day Build)

Choose if: you have 2-3 months of runway and would rather walk into the first sales call with everything already working.

The cost: roughly 55-60 hours of building before you speak to a single prospect. That is the trade you are making — go in knowing it.

Your path: the click-by-click steps page, Days 1-15 in order ↗, then Module 5 for outreach.

Whichever you pick, two things start on Day 1 in both tracks because they take weeks to mature and everything else waits on them: (1) email domain warm-up, and (2) Twilio A2P 10DLC registration. Start them today even if you do nothing else. And do not blend the tracks — cherry-picking days from both is the single most common way this stalls.

Who Owns What (canonical — overrides every other role list)

Other sections of this course were written generically and hand some of these to the wrong person. This table wins. One name per row: the owner does it, the other reviews. “Both” appears only where the work genuinely cannot be split.

AreaOwnerWhy this way for you two
Prospect lists & enrichment MikeFeeds his own outreach — splitting it creates handoff lag
Cold email + audit Looms MikeHis voice is on the recordings and he answers the replies
US cold calls & demos MikeNative-English sales seat. Paola joins demos only where Spanish helps
Closing & pricing MikeOne person quotes price, always — two quoters means two ladders

Bus-factor rule. Mike being the only person who can deploy is the biggest risk you have. Every credential lives in one shared password vault from day one, and Paola does one supervised deploy per month so she can keep clients alive for a week without him.

Paola holds the go-live veto. Nothing reaches a client until she has run the 10-call test — and test #1 is always “are you a real person?” If the agent dodges, it does not go live. The person who owns the relationship decides when it is ready — this protects Mike from his own optimism.

Reduced Mode. When one of you is sick, travelling or buried at the day job: keep client delivery and demos already booked; drop prospecting, content and new builds first. Say it out loud on Friday so nobody quietly resents the imbalance.

Paola’s job before client #1 exists

Read this on any Monday where her honest answer is “nothing.” Eight of the twelve rows above need a paying client — until you have one they are not her job, and these five are. This lane sits deliberately upstream of Mike’s: she produces the evidence, he uses it. Nobody quotes a price but Mike, and nobody sells on these calls.

1 · The Live Test list (her highest-value hour)

Call 10 target businesses after hours. Log: rang out / voicemail / answered. She is not selling — she is collecting the recording Mike’s audit Loom is built on. This is the single asset the first sale rests on, and it needs no English sales seat.

2 · Referral partners, from day one

Two conversations a week. Bookkeepers and supply houses take 6-8 weeks to produce anything, so starting them at client #1 is starting them two months late.

3 · Write the SOPs now

Intake form, welcome email, kickoff agenda, the 10-call test sheet. Delivery is the readiness dimension that scores zero for everyone pre-revenue — and the only one you can fix with no prospects at all. Writing them after client #1 signs means writing them at 11pm.

4 · The Spanish list

Build a separate list of Hispanic-owned and Spanish-serving shops. On these, Paola leads the entire call — the one prospecting lane that is hers outright, and your actual edge.

5 · Dry-run the go-live. Before any client exists, run the 10-call test against Mike’s demo agent and fill in a Handoff Packet for a fake client. The first time you practise the handoff should not be the day real money is on the line.

The One Pricing Ladder (canonical — quote nothing else)

Every price anywhere in this course belongs to this ladder. The two numbers in the Monthly column are the same offer at two stages of your credibility: charge the left number until you have a written case study, then charge the right number to every new client.

TierSetupMonthly (launch → established)What's included
Founding Client (clients 1-3 only)$497$497/moCore receptionist. Deliberately cheap — you are buying testimonials and recordings, not profit. Expires after client #3.
Starter$1,500$500 → $800AI receptionist 24/7, booking, SMS confirmations, monthly report. 1,000 AI minutes included.
“Never Miss a Call” Bundle (most popular)$2,500$1,000 → $1,200Starter + lead follow-up + review automation. 1,500 minutes included.
Scale$3,500-5,000$1,500+Bundle + bilingual + outbound campaigns + dashboard + priority support. 3,000 minutes included.

Minutes, always. Never say “unlimited.” Overage is $0.35/min (your cost ~$0.13/min). Unlimited is how you lose money on the one client who advertises on the radio.

Grandfather rule. Existing clients keep their rate forever. That’s why founding clients happily give you case studies and referrals — they know what they have.

Raise the price, not the discount. Discount the setup fee if you must. Never discount the monthly — it’s the number that compounds.

The Numbers That Are Actually True (cite these, and only these)

Contractors Google your claims. Most stats circulating in the AI-receptionist world are vendor arithmetic or tiny unnamed studies — if you quote one and it collapses, you lose the room. These are the defensible ones, with who published them and when.

Use this numberSourceWhere you use it
Only 52% of home-services calls reach a person — and the longer a phone rings, the more callers give up entirelyInvoca, 2026 — analysis of 70M callsThe opening line of every audit Loom and cold email
46% of home-services phone leads convert; 41% for calls referred from ChatGPTInvoca, 2026ROI math — this is the “booking rate” input
Only 17% of HVAC pros respond to a lead within the hour — slowest of any tradeJobber, 2026 Home Service Economic ReportSpeed-to-Lead pitch (use instead of the 2007 “21x” stat)
~25% of residential contractors currently use AI, while 74% see it as an efficiency gainServiceTitan contractor survey, 2026 (n≈1,000)Market-timing slide: early, but no longer novel
~$522B US home improvement & repair spending (annualized, late 2026)Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies (LIRA)Market-size framing in proposals
~120,000 HVAC firms, ~129,000 plumbers, ~262,000 electricians in the USIBISWorld, 2026Territory math — your reachable universe
2 of 3 specialty-trade firms with employees earn under $1M/yrUS Census / SUSBWhy you target 1-8 truck shops, not enterprises

Stop using these three (they will not survive a skeptical owner): “62% of calls go unanswered” (traces to a 2024 study of 85 businesses), “every missed call costs $1,200” (vendor arithmetic, no study), and “respond in 5 minutes and you’re 21x more likely to qualify” (Oldroyd/MIT Sloan for InsideSales.com, 2007). The honest version is stronger anyway: “I called your line at 7:14pm last night. Here’s the recording.” First-party evidence beats any statistic. Best practice: never quote a number about the client’s business that you can pull from the client’s own call log instead.

The Mike + Paola 90-Day Contract

Across online-course data, self-paced material is finished by a small minority while scheduled, accountable cohorts finish at dramatically higher rates — the difference is not content, it is a date, a named partner, and a standing review. (Directional industry figures, not a controlled study.) This is that mechanism — fill it in, it saves automatically.

We commit to these weekly minimums, every week, regardless of how we feel:

150 cold emails sent (Mike) — the pipeline never goes dark, even in a delivery-heavy week

5 Missed Call Audit Looms recorded (Mike) — the highest close-rate hour you have

2 referral-partner conversations (Paola) — bookkeepers, supply houses, web shops

1 Friday scorecard filled in together (Both) — 30 minutes, non-negotiable, the whole system depends on it

The consequence clause (write it down or it isn't real): if we miss the weekly minimums two weeks in a row, we cancel and do a full reset session that Sunday.

When/Then Commitments

“I’ll do outreach this week” fails. “When I finish coffee Tuesday at 8am, I will send 25 HVAC emails” works — implementation intentions are one of the best-evidenced habit mechanisms in psychology (Gollwitzer & Sheeran meta-analysis, 94 tests). Write four. Be embarrassingly specific about the time and place.

Red two weeks running: . Per your own rule, that is next week’s only priority — everything else waits.

Behind schedule? Open this instead of pushing harder.

Most couples are behind at week 3. That is the normal shape of this, not evidence you picked wrong. Work these in order and stop at the first one that is true — do not do all five.

  1. Did the week actually happen? If the two 90-minute blocks did not get done, nothing else on this page is the problem. Halve the commitment and protect the time before changing anything about the business.
  2. Is the pipeline empty, or is it stuck? Empty = do outreach only, drop everything else. Stuck (replies but no demos) = your audit Loom is the problem, not your volume. Re-record one and watch it back.
  3. Demos happening but nobody buying? That is the offer, not the effort. Re-read the Offer & Objection System, and specifically go find the Critical Event — no urgency, no deal this month.
  4. One of you carrying it alone? Say it out loud on Friday and switch to Reduced Mode deliberately for two weeks rather than resenting it for eight.
  5. Still nothing after 60 days of real activity? Change the trade, the city, or the offer — one variable, not all three. Log which one you changed so week 12 tells you something.

The consequence clause does not fire for being behind. It fires only for not doing the work. Missing the target while doing the minimums means the plan was wrong, and you adjust the plan — not the marriage.

FRIDAY DEBRIEF — 30 MINUTES, PHONES DOWN Each of you answers out loud, no interrupting: 1. What did I actually SHIP this week? (things that exist now, not things I worked on) 2. Where did I get stuck, and what did I avoid because it felt uncomfortable? 3. What is my ONE commitment for next week — with the day and time I'll do it? Then together, 10 minutes: 4. Read the scorecard. Any metric in the red two weeks running becomes next week's only priority. 5. Any client at risk? (quiet, complaining, usage dropping, invoice bounced) 6. Update the pipeline: who's closest to signing, and what's the exact next action + date? 7. One thing we'll STOP doing next week. There must be one. Rule: no strategy talk, no new ideas, no re-planning the business. This meeting is about what happened and what happens next. New ideas go in a parking-lot note for the monthly review.

What Is This? (The 2-Minute Explanation)

The problem we solve: When a plumber is under a sink or an HVAC tech is on a roof, they can't answer their phone. The call goes to voicemail. The customer hangs up and calls the next company on Google. That plumber just lost a $3,000-$10,000 job and doesn't even know it. This happens roughly half the time across home services (Invoca, 2026). The average home service business loses real, countable jobs every month — run the Missed-Revenue Worksheet on their own numbers rather than quoting an average from missed calls alone.

What we sell: We set up an AI phone agent that answers their business calls 24/7. It sounds like a real, friendly receptionist. It picks up in under 1 second, asks the right questions ("What's the issue? What's your address? When works for you?"), books the appointment, and sends the customer a confirmation text. The business owner gets a text notification instantly: "New appointment booked — John Smith, broken AC, Tuesday 2pm." The customer is happy, the contractor gets the job, nobody called a competitor.

What it's NOT: It's not a robot that says "Press 1 for sales." It's not a voicemail. It's a natural-sounding AI that has a real conversation. Most callers don't even realize it's AI — they just know they got helped immediately.

Why it works as a business:

  • • We charge: $500-$1,500/month per client (plus a one-time setup fee of $1,500-$5,000 depending on tier)
  • • It costs us: ~$50/month per client in software and phone costs
  • • That's an 80-90% gross margin (see the Command Center for the honest P&L). Once set up, it runs 24/7
  • • Clients stay: because it saves them real money every single month — they see the numbers in reports we send

What Mike does: Builds the AI agent, sets up the tech, handles technical issues. This is the "under the hood" work — connecting the tools, writing the scripts the AI follows, and making sure everything runs smoothly.

What Paola does: Owns everything from the signature onward — client onboarding and go-live, all client communication and monthly reports, call QA scoring, referral partners, invoicing, and every Spanish-language client and agent. She holds the go-live veto: nothing reaches a client until she has run the 10-call test. No coding needed — it is people, checklists, and clicking buttons in web apps. (Mike owns prospecting, cold outreach, demos and closing — see Who Owns What.)

Our secret weapons:

  • • Bilingual: Paola's native Spanish means we can offer AI agents that answer in English AND Spanish. 46% of US roofers and 52% of concrete workers are Hispanic. Nobody else offers a bilingual AI receptionist at our price. We charge an extra $150-$200/month for this and it costs us $0 extra.
  • • Time zone: We live in Germany, 6-9 hours ahead of the US. Our mornings are build time while America sleeps. Our afternoons (3-5pm) are their mornings (9-11am) — the perfect window for sales calls. The AI handles client calls 24/7, so we don't need to be awake at US hours.
  • • Part-time friendly: We each work 7-10 hours/week around a day job. The AI does the 24/7 work. We just build, sell, and manage.
  • • Scaling with Colombian VAs: When we grow past 12 clients and need help, Paola hires and manages Colombian virtual assistants in native Spanish. They cost $8-15/hr (vs $25-50/hr in the US) and they're on US Eastern Time naturally.

The goal — computed from the pricing ladder, not rounded up. Your first three clients are Founding Clients at $497, so month-3 MRR looks small on purpose; the setup fees are where the early cash actually is:

💡 Course Tip: The 30-Second Elevator Pitch

Practice explaining this business to someone who's never heard of AI in under 30 seconds: "We help plumbers and HVAC companies stop losing customers from missed phone calls by setting up an AI receptionist that answers 24/7, books appointments, and sends confirmations — all for less than the cost of one lost job per month." If you can say this naturally, you can sell it to anyone.

Knowledge Check Module 1 Quiz

A plumber loses a meaningful share of their booked work/year from missed calls. You charge them $1,000/month. What's the primary reason clients stay and keep paying?

Exactly! Retention = proving ROI. Monthly reports show calls answered, appointments booked, and revenue captured. The math keeps them paying.
Not quite. Clients stay because of proven ROI, not cool tech or contracts. Your monthly reports show real dollars captured from calls they would have missed.

Fast Track

The 21-Day Money Sprint: First Paying Client in 3 Weeks

The standard plan (Quick Start above) builds for two weeks, then sells, and lands a first client around Week 4–8. This sprint compresses that to 21 days by changing two things: you sell from Day 3 using channels that need zero warm-up (the phone, your network, Facebook groups), and you lead with offers that close in one call instead of the full $497/mo receptionist. Cash first, polish later.

The One Rule of the Sprint

Nothing gets built unless a prospect asked for it or paid for it. Your demo takes 2 days. Everything else — website polish, GoHighLevel, perfect branding, cold email at volume — waits until there's money in Stripe. Cold email domains warm in the background and become your engine in Week 4+; the sprint itself runs on the phone.

These businesses lose a meaningful share of their booked work per year from missed calls. You fix that problem with an AI voice agent that answers 24/7, captures leads, and books appointments.

Tax Situation: What You Need to Know

Your LLC is a US company, serving US clients, paid through US banks. You owe US taxes — that part is simple. The Germany question is more nuanced. Below we break down what the law says, what actually happens in practice, and our recommended approach.

1. What the Law Technically Says

SOFA exempts your military/government pay from German tax. NATO SOFA Article X is crystal clear on this — Mike's government salary is not taxable by Germany. Period.

Private business income is a gray area. Article X has a carve-out saying Germany can tax "any profitable enterprise other than his employment" that a SOFA member engages in. Army JAG offices and the Ramstein AFB tax guidance interpret this to mean that side business income could be subject to German taxation, because the work is physically performed in Germany.

The Gewerbeanmeldung question: Stuttgart's Spousal Employment Guide says profitable activities "generally require" trade registration. The Gewerbeamt determines if it's needed based on the type of activity.

Sources: NATO SOFA Article X, Ramstein AFB Taxation Guidance (Aug 2023), US Army Garrison Stuttgart Spousal Employment Guide, Kaiserslautern American

2. What Actually Happens (Enforcement Reality)

The Finanzamt has zero visibility into your US business. Your Wyoming LLC, US bank account, Stripe payments, and US tax filings are completely invisible to German tax authorities. There is no information-sharing mechanism between the IRS and the Finanzamt for LLC pass-through income.

Thousands of SOFA families run side businesses without registering in Germany. Etsy shops, freelance work, online coaching, MLMs, Amazon FBA, software development — the military communities are full of spouse-run and dual-income businesses operating through US entities. Enforcement against these is essentially nonexistent.

Your specific situation is especially low-risk:

  • • US LLC registered in a US state
  • • US-only clients (no German customers)
  • • US bank account and payment processing
  • • No physical presence in German commerce (no German ads, no German invoices)
  • • No German employees or contractors
  • • No German business bank account

When would risk increase? Taking German clients, opening a German business bank account, advertising in Germany, hiring German workers, or having someone report you to the Finanzamt. As long as the business stays 100% US-facing, the practical risk is very low.

3. What You Definitely Owe (US Taxes)

Self-employment tax: 15.3% (12.4% Social Security + 2.9% Medicare) on net self-employment income up to roughly $184,500 (2026 cap — verify the current year’s figure with your CPA). This applies to both Mike and Paola's share of LLC profits. This is the biggest tax bite and there is no way around it.

Federal income tax: 10-37% progressive rates. At $50K net profit each (50/50 split), your effective federal rate is approximately 12-15%. At $100K each, approximately 18-22%.

FEIE (Foreign Earned Income Exclusion): May exclude up to ~$130,000 of earned income from federal income tax — potentially zeroing out your federal liability. FEIE does NOT reduce self-employment tax. SOFA eligibility is debated among tax pros, but many SOFA families successfully claim it using the Physical Presence Test (330 days outside the US). Worth discussing with a CPA.

State taxes: If LLC is registered in Wyoming, Nevada, or South Dakota — no state income tax. Register in a no-income-tax state.

Estimated quarterly payments: The IRS expects quarterly estimated tax payments (April 15, June 15, Sept 15, Jan 15). Use Form 1040-ES.

4. Your Realistic Tax Rate

For planning purposes, here's what your tax burden looks like with the US LLC structure:

ComponentRateNotes
Self-employment tax~14.1%15.3% on 92.35% of net income (you deduct half)
Federal income tax~8-12%Effective rate after SE deduction + standard deduction. Could be $0 with FEIE.
State income tax0%Register LLC in WY/NV/SD/TX/FL.
Likely effective rate~22-25%US taxes only. Could be ~15% with FEIE.
If German taxes also apply~28-32%German tax replaces (not adds to) US federal via Foreign Tax Credit. Unlikely scenario for your setup.

We use ~23% in the P&L projections (US-only, no-income-tax state, no FEIE). If you successfully claim FEIE, your actual rate could be as low as ~15%, putting even more money in your pockets.

5. Important Filings

Form 5472: Required if the LLC has a "foreign" owner. If Paola is not a US person for tax purposes, this is mandatory. Penalty for missing it: $25,000. If she elects to file jointly with Mike as a US resident, you may not need it. Clarify this with your CPA first.

FBAR (FinCEN 114): Required if you have foreign bank accounts exceeding $10,000 combined at any point during the year. If you keep a German bank account, this likely applies.

Form 8938 (FATCA): Required if foreign financial assets exceed $200,000 (filing jointly abroad). May apply depending on your German bank balances.

6. One Rule You Cannot Break

Never use SOFA privileges for business purposes. This is the one thing that can actually get you in trouble, regardless of the German tax question:

  • • No APO/FPO address for business mail or LLC registration
  • • No USAREUR-plated vehicle for business activities
  • • No tax-free goods (PX/Commissary/VAT-form purchases) used for business
  • • No military installation facilities for private business without authorization

Violations can result in loss of SOFA privileges — which would be catastrophic. Use your US home address (virtual address via iPostal1) and keep everything completely separate.

What Happens When SOFA Ends

If Mike leaves his SOFA-covered position, you become regular German tax residents within 90 days. At that point, German taxes on the LLC become mandatory — not optional. Plan 3-6 months ahead:

  • • German income tax on worldwide income (14-45% progressive)
  • • Gewerbeanmeldung required for the LLC's activities
  • • Gewerbesteuer (trade tax, ~14-17% with €24,500 exemption)
  • • US-Germany tax treaty + Foreign Tax Credit prevent paying double
  • • Consider relocating the business or restructuring before SOFA ends
  • • Hire a Steuerberater with US-German cross-border experience early.

Our Recommended Approach

  • • Register LLC in Wyoming ($100/year, no state income tax, strong privacy, easy online).
  • • Keep everything US-based: US bank account (Mercury or Relay), US Stripe, US virtual address (iPostal1). Zero German financial footprint for the business.
  • • Set aside 25% of net profit in a separate savings account for quarterly estimated US tax payments. Adjust once your CPA calculates your actual rate.
  • • File US taxes properly. This is non-negotiable. Quarterly estimates + annual return with Schedule C/K-1.
  • • Get a CPA once revenue hits $3K+/month. Military OneSource offers free basic tax prep. For the LLC, budget $500-1,500/year for a CPA familiar with military/expat situations. They'll advise on FEIE eligibility and optimize your rate.
  • • Clarify Paola's tax status with your CPA. If she elects to file jointly with Mike as a US resident, it simplifies everything but means she files US taxes too.
  • • Don't take German clients until you've consulted a Steuerberater. US-only clients = clean separation.
  • • Revisit the German tax question if income exceeds $100K/year or if SOFA status is ending. At that scale, it's worth getting a formal opinion from a cross-border tax professional.

DBA Filing (If Your Agency Name Differs From LLC Name)

Your LLC is Colibri Code LLC. If your client-facing brand is different (e.g., “Call Colibri” or “Never Miss a Call”), you may want a DBA (“Doing Business As”) registration. This lets you open a bank account, accept payments, and sign contracts under the brand name.

Where to file: In the state where your LLC is registered. Usually through the county clerk or Secretary of State website. Cost: $10-65 depending on state.

When you need it: If you want to accept payments or open a bank account under a different name than “Colibri Code LLC.” Stripe and most banks accept LLC names, so a DBA is optional unless your brand name is very different.

When you DON’T need it: If clients pay “Colibri Code LLC” and you’re fine with that on invoices. Many agencies operate under their LLC name and just have a branded website. Stripe invoices can show any display name.

Process: Search your state’s business name database to make sure the name isn’t taken → file online or by mail → receive certificate (1-5 business days) → bring to bank to open account under DBA name.

Start with HVAC + Plumbing in Tier 1-2 cities (Miami, Houston, Dallas, San Antonio, Atlanta). Highest urgency, highest job values, closest timezone, and the largest bilingual opportunity. Once you have 5 clients, expand into electrical and roofing, then push into Tier 3 cities.

Services & Pricing: What You Sell

You sell three productized services. Fixed scope, fixed price. No custom quotes, no scope creep.

Service 1: AI Phone Agent

PRIMARY

An AI voice agent that answers every call 24/7, captures caller info, books appointments, and sends confirmations. The client's phone never goes to voicemail again.

Setup fee: $1,500-$3,000
Monthly retainer: $500-$1,000/mo
Your cost/client: ~$50-150/mo
Your margin: 80-90%

What the client gets: Dedicated phone number, custom-scripted AI agent, appointment booking, SMS confirmations, call logs dashboard, monthly performance report.

Service 2: Lead Follow-Up Automation

AI-powered SMS and email sequences that follow up with missed leads, send appointment reminders, and request Google reviews after completed jobs.

Setup fee: $500-$1,500
Monthly retainer: $300-$500/mo

Automatically request Google reviews after jobs, respond to reviews with AI, and alert the owner to negative reviews instantly.

Setup fee: $500
Monthly retainer: $200-$300/mo

The "Never Miss a Call" Bundle (All 3)

Position this as the default. Most clients will choose the bundle because it's the complete solution.

Setup fee: $2,500 (saving them $500)
Monthly retainer: $1,000/mo (saving them $200)

The math for the client: They pay $1,000/mo. They were losing $4,000-$10,000/mo from missed calls. ROI is obvious.

Premium Add-Ons

Bilingual AI Agent (English + Spanish)

HIGH MARGIN

The AI detects the caller's language automatically and responds in English or Spanish. Paola trains and quality-tests every Spanish agent script. Traditional bilingual answering services charge $300-$1,500/mo with a 20-40% surcharge — you charge a fraction.

Add-on price: +$150-$200/mo
Your extra cost: ~$0 (same Vapi agent, different prompt)
Setup: Included with any service tier
Margin on add-on: ~95%

Pitch: "52% of concrete finishers and 46% of roofers in the US are Hispanic. If your crew or their families call in Spanish and hit an English-only voicemail, you lose them. Our bilingual agent handles both — no extra staff needed."

Seasonal Campaign Blasts

AI calls past customers before peak season ("AC tune-up season is here — want to book before the rush?"). Database reactivation for dormant leads.

Per campaign: $250-$500
Your cost: ~$20-50 in Vapi/Twilio usage

Weekly AI-generated posts, photo optimization, Q&A responses, and review reply management. Uses Claude API + Canva templates.

Add-on price: +$150/mo
Your cost: ~$10/mo (API + Canva Pro share)

Pricing Psychology

Always present three options (Service 1, Service 2, Bundle). Most choose the middle or bundle. Layer add-ons after they commit to a tier — the bilingual add-on is nearly pure profit. Never charge hourly. You're selling an outcome (never miss a call), not your time.

Plain English: What Each Tool Actually Does

Vapi = the "voice" of the AI phone agent. It's the service that actually answers the phone and talks to callers. Think of it as the mouth and ears.

Twilio = the phone company. It gives you real phone numbers and sends/receives texts. Think of it as the phone line Vapi talks through.

n8n = the "brain" that connects everything. When a call ends, n8n takes the info and automatically does things with it — saves the lead, sends a text, emails the client. It's like a digital assistant that follows rules you set up. No code needed — you drag and drop boxes on screen.

Claude API / OpenAI = the intelligence behind the voice. This is what makes the AI agent actually understand what the caller is saying and respond smartly — not just play pre-recorded messages.

Supabase = a spreadsheet on steroids. It stores all your data — every call, every lead, every client. You can pull reports from it. Free for your scale.

Hetzner VPS = a rented computer that runs 24/7 in the cloud. It's where n8n lives. You'll never see it physically — you access it through your browser. $5/month.

Smartlead = an email sending tool designed for outreach. It sends your cold emails, warms up your email addresses so they don't go to spam, and tracks who opens/replies.

LLM = "Large Language Model" — the AI that understands language. Claude (Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6) and GPT-5.x are LLMs. When we say "LLM cost" we mean the cost of the AI thinking during calls.

TTS / STT = "Text to Speech" / "Speech to Text." TTS is how the AI turns its written response into a voice. STT is how it understands what the caller said. Both happen inside Vapi automatically.

Webhook = an automatic notification between tools. When a call ends in Vapi, it sends a webhook (a little data packet) to n8n saying "hey, a call just happened, here's the info." n8n then does something with it. You set this up once and it runs forever.

API key = a password that lets one tool talk to another. When Mike sets up Vapi to use Claude, he copies an API key from Anthropic into Vapi. It's how tools authenticate with each other.

Role Split: Who Does What

Your real budget is 7-10 hours a week each around the day job — the Command Center number wins. The 20-25 hr/week schedule below is the shape of the week, not the volume: run it at about a third density and protect the 3-5pm CET window above everything else. Play to each person's strengths. Every task maps to a specific time block optimized for the Germany → US timezone gap.

Mike — Tech + Build (7-10 hrs/wk real budget)

  • Set up and manage n8n, Vapi, Twilio, Supabase
  • Build the AI voice agent scripts and workflows
  • Deploy and test automations for each client
  • Handle technical troubleshooting
  • Record Loom demos showing the product working
  • Take the lead on demo calls (technical questions)
  • Morning deep work (8am-12pm CET) while US sleeps

Paola — Clients + Ops + Spanish (7-10 hrs/wk real budget)

  • Own client onboarding end to end: intake form, kickoff, go-live checklist
  • Hold the go-live veto — run the 10-call test before any client hears the agent
  • Score 10 client calls a week for quality and log what needs tuning
  • All client communication, monthly reports, and check-in calls
  • Invoicing, billing and the MRR number on the Friday scorecard (Stripe)
  • Own referral partners: bookkeepers, supply houses, web shops (2 touches/week)
  • Every Spanish-speaking client, call and agent script — your competitive edge
  • One supervised deploy per month so the business survives a week without Mike
  • Cold email, prospect lists, US cold calls, demos and closing belong to Mike — see Who Owns What.

Part-Time Weekly Schedule (Germany Time)

~8 hrs/week each — this table shows which block, not how many hours. Mondays for planning, Fridays for wrap-up. Sales calls concentrated in the afternoon overlap window.

Time (CET) US Equiv. Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri
8-12pm 2-6am ET Mike: Deep tech — build agents, fix bugs, deploy clients. Paola: Lead research, email copy, content creation.
12-2pm 6-8am ET Lunch break / personal time
3-5pm 9-11am ET Mike: Sales calls and demos. Paola: client check-ins; joins demos only for Spanish-speaking prospects. This is the golden window — East Coast & Central business hours.

Why This Works

Morning = uninterrupted build time (no US clients awake to ping you). Afternoon = focused 2-hour sales window. Two optional evenings for West Coast or overflow demos. The AI agent handles all client calls 24/7, so you don't need to be available outside these blocks.

Demo Call Tag-Team

Both of you should be on demo calls during the 3-5pm window. Mike handles "how does it work?" and Paola handles "here's what happens next / let's get you started." For Spanish-speaking prospects, Paola leads the entire conversation.

Knowledge Check Module 2 Quiz

You're pricing your AI phone agent service. A contractor asks why they should pay $1,000/mo when Dialzara charges $29/mo. What's the strongest response?

Right. Contractors aren't buying technology — they're buying a solved problem. DIY tools require setup they'll never do. You're an outsourced operations partner, not a software subscription. The price difference buys peace of mind and proven results.
Technology comparisons don't resonate with contractors, and price-matching kills your margins. The winning angle is done-for-you value: they sign up, you handle everything, and they see monthly reports proving ROI. That's worth 20x a DIY tool login they'll never use.

DAY 2 Tech Account Setup

Mike — 4-5 hours

Spin up Hetzner VPS. Go to hetzner.com/cloud. Create a CX22 server (2 vCPU, 4GB RAM, $5/mo). Choose Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. Save the IP address and root password.

Point a subdomain at the server FIRST. In your domain registrar’s DNS, add an A record: n8n.yourdomain.com → your server IP. Do this before the next step — HTTPS certificates won’t issue without it, and Vapi/Twilio webhooks refuse plain HTTP.

Install n8n with automatic HTTPS. SSH in as root and paste this whole block. It ends with a URL you can open in a browser:

# --- edit these two lines, then paste the whole block --- export N8N_HOST=n8n.yourdomain.com export N8N_EMAIL=you@yourdomain.com apt update && apt upgrade -y curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh # installs Docker + Compose v2 ufw allow OpenSSH && ufw allow 80 && ufw allow 443 && ufw --force enable mkdir -p /opt/n8n && cd /opt/n8n cat > docker-compose.yml <<YAML services: caddy: image: caddy:2 restart: unless-stopped ports: ["80:80", "443:443"] volumes: - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile - caddy_data:/data n8n: image: docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n restart: unless-stopped environment: - N8N_HOST=\${N8N_HOST} - WEBHOOK_URL=https://\${N8N_HOST}/ - N8N_PROTOCOL=https - GENERIC_TIMEZONE=America/New_York - N8N_ENFORCE_SETTINGS_FILE_PERMISSIONS=true volumes: - n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n volumes: caddy_data: n8n_data: YAML cat > Caddyfile <<CADDY ${N8N_HOST} { tls ${N8N_EMAIL} reverse_proxy n8n:5678 } CADDY printf 'N8N_HOST=%s\nN8N_EMAIL=%s\n' "$N8N_HOST" "$N8N_EMAIL" > /opt/n8n/.env docker compose up -d sleep 20 && docker compose ps # Compose auto-loads ./.env, so future up/restart/pull work in any new SSH session.
Done when: docker compose ps shows both containers “running”, and https://n8n.yourdomain.com loads the setup screen with a padlock. If the padlock is missing, DNS hasn’t propagated — wait 10 minutes and run docker compose restart caddy.

Set the n8n owner account immediately. The setup screen is public until you do — anyone who finds the URL first owns your automation server. Use a password manager, and turn on 2FA under Settings.

Create Vapi account. Sign up, add a payment method. Get your API key from the dashboard.

Create Twilio account. Sign up, verify your phone number. Buy one local phone number ($1/mo). Get your Account SID and Auth Token.

Submit A2P 10DLC registration TODAY — this is the long pole. Register your Brand and one Campaign in Twilio Console → Messaging → Regulatory Compliance. Since June 30 2026 you must supply a public Privacy Policy URL and Terms & Conditions URL or the submission hard-fails with a 400. Standard registration typically clears in days, but assume up to 2-3 weeks and plan around it. Do not send a single SMS before approval — unregistered traffic gets filtered and can damage the number. Full walkthrough

Create Anthropic account. Get API key. Add $10 in credits to start.

Create Supabase project. Name it "agency-crm". You'll set up tables later.

Create Cal.com account. Set up two event types: "15-min Demo Call" (for prospects) and "Client Appointment" (template for client booking).

Create Resend account. Verify your agency domain for sending.

Create Loom account. Test recording a 30-second video.

Paola — 3-4 hours

Create Smartlead account. Sign up for Basic plan ($39/mo). Connect your 3 cold email sending domains. Start inbox warmup immediately — this takes 14 days, so start now.

Set up sending domains in Smartlead:

  1. Go to Namecheap → each sending domain → set up MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC records (Smartlead gives you the exact records to add)
  2. Create a mailbox on each sending domain (e.g., mike@colibri-solutions.com) using a $1/mo Zoho Mail account (don't waste Google Workspace on these)
  3. Connect each mailbox to Smartlead
  4. Turn on warmup for all 3 accounts

Create Apollo.io account. Free tier. Set up your first search: Industry = "HVAC" OR "Plumbing", Employees = 1-50, Location = [your metro area], Title = "Owner" OR "President" OR "General Manager".

Export your first 200 leads from Apollo. Save as CSV. You'll upload these to Smartlead in Week 3.

Google Maps research. Search "HVAC companies near [your city]" and "plumbers near [your city]". Note the top 50 companies — their names, phone numbers, and whether they have a website. This is your manual call list.

DAYS 3-4 Learn the Stack

Mike — 8-10 hours over 2 days

n8n crash course. Watch these on the n8n YouTube channel (in order):

  1. "Getting Started with n8n" (basics of nodes, triggers, workflows)
  2. "HTTP Request node" (how to call APIs)
  3. "Webhook node" (how to receive data from external services)
  4. "AI Agent node" (how n8n handles AI-powered decisions)
  5. Search community workflows for "Vapi" or "voice agent" — clone and study them

Vapi crash course. Read the Vapi quickstart docs. Create your first test assistant. Make a test call. Understand: assistants, tools, phone numbers, and webhooks.

Connect Vapi to n8n. Create a simple workflow: Vapi webhook → n8n receives call data → logs it. This is the foundation of everything you'll build.

Paola — 4-5 hours over 2 days

Cold email crash course. Watch 2-3 YouTube videos on "cold email for agencies 2026" (channels: Alex Berman, Patrick Dang). Key concepts: open rates, reply rates, warmup, avoiding spam.

Write your cold email sequences. Draft all 3 emails in the sequence (see Scripts section below). Get them reviewed by Mike. Load them into Smartlead as a template (don't send yet — warmup still running).

Build your lead list to 500. Continue Apollo exports + Google Maps scraping. Organize in a spreadsheet: Name, Company, Email, Phone, City, Sub-niche (HVAC/Plumbing/Electrical).

Research 20 prospects deeply. Visit their websites, Google reviews, Facebook pages. Note: Do they have a "Contact Us" form or just a phone number? What are their hours? Do their Google reviews mention hard-to-reach or slow response? These become personalization hooks in your emails.

DAY 5 Build the Demo Voice Agent

Mike — 5-6 hours

Create a demo Vapi assistant for a fake HVAC company ("Comfort Pro HVAC"). Configure:

  • Greeting: "Thanks for calling Comfort Pro HVAC, this is the scheduling assistant. How can I help you today?"
  • The agent should collect: caller name, phone number, address, type of service needed (AC repair, heating, installation, maintenance), urgency level
  • If urgent: "I'll make sure a technician calls you back within 15 minutes."
  • If not urgent: offer to book an appointment (connect to Cal.com)
  • End: "Great, you're all set. You'll receive a text confirmation shortly. Is there anything else I can help with?"

Connect to Twilio phone number. Forward calls to your Twilio number to the Vapi assistant.

Build n8n post-call workflow:

  • Vapi fires webhook when call ends → n8n receives call data
  • Extract: caller name, phone, address, service type, urgency
  • Store in Supabase "leads" table
  • Send SMS confirmation to caller via Twilio
  • Send notification email to "business owner" via Resend

Test it end-to-end. Call the number from your cell phone. Pretend to be a homeowner with a broken AC. Verify: the AI agent handles the call, data arrives in Supabase, you get the notification, caller gets the SMS.

Paola — 2-3 hours

Call the demo number as different customer personas. Test edge cases: "I need someone RIGHT NOW, my pipes are bursting", "I just want a quote", "What are your hours?", "Can I speak to a real person?"

Note every issue — did the AI handle it well? Where did it stumble? Write down improvements for Mike to fix.

Continue building lead lists. Target: 500 total leads by end of Week 1.

DAYS 6-7 Polish & Record Demo

Both Together — 4-5 hours

Fix every issue found during testing. Tweak the Vapi script. Improve the AI's responses for edge cases. Make the SMS confirmation sound professional.

Record a Loom demo video (2-3 minutes). Structure:

  1. Show the phone ringing and the AI answering (screen record + audio)
  2. Show the lead appearing in the dashboard in real-time
  3. Show the SMS confirmation the caller receives
  4. Show the notification the business owner gets
  5. End with: "This runs 24/7. You never miss a call again."

Prep the sales pitch. Practice the demo call flow together. Who says what. How to handle "how much?" and "I need to think about it."

Create a simple one-page PDF proposal (use Canva or Google Docs). Include: the problem (missed calls = lost revenue), the solution (AI phone agent), what's included, pricing (the 3 tiers), and a "Ready to start?" CTA.

End of Week 1 Checkpoint

You should have: all accounts created, n8n running on your VPS, a working demo voice agent you can call, a recorded Loom demo, cold email domains warming up in Smartlead, 500+ leads in your list, and a simple agency website live. If anything is missing, Day 1 of Week 2 is your catch-up day.

Week 2: Build Follow-Up Automation + Prep Outreach

DAYS 8-9 Build Services 2 & 3

Mike — 8-10 hours over 2 days

Build the lead follow-up automation in n8n:

  • When a new lead is captured → wait 5 minutes → send SMS: "Hi [Name], thanks for calling [Business]. We've received your request for [service]. A technician will contact you shortly."
  • If no appointment booked within 2 hours → send follow-up SMS: "Hi [Name], just following up on your [service] request. Would you like to schedule a time? Reply YES and we'll set it up."
  • 24 hours before appointment → send reminder SMS
  • 1 hour after appointment time → send "How did it go?" SMS

Build the review request automation in n8n:

  • After "How did it go?" response is positive → wait 1 day → send SMS: "Glad we could help! Would you mind leaving us a quick Google review? It really helps: [Google Review Link]"
  • If negative response → immediately email the business owner: "Alert: [Customer Name] reported a negative experience. Details: [response]. Follow up recommended."

Build a simple client dashboard. Use Supabase + a basic HTML page (or a Notion embed) showing: total calls this week, leads captured, appointments booked, reviews requested. This is what you show clients in their monthly report.

Paola — 6 hours over 2 days

Finalize cold email copy. Write 3 variations of each email in the sequence (A/B/C test). Load all into Smartlead.

Build a "hot prospects" list. From your 500 leads, identify 50 with the most pain signals:

  • Google reviews mentioning "couldn't get through" or "didn't answer"
  • Websites with only a phone number (no online booking)
  • Companies with 4+ star ratings but few recent reviews (need review automation)
  • Companies that answered YOUR call when you tested — they're the ones picking up while on jobs

Write voicemail script for the phone call campaign (see Scripts section).

Join 5-10 local Facebook groups: "[City] Small Business Owners", "[City] Home Services", "Contractors of [State]", etc. Don't post anything yet — just join and observe what they talk about.

DAYS 10-11 Test Everything End-to-End

Both Together — 4-5 hours

Run the full customer journey simulation. Paola calls the demo number as a customer. Mike watches the backend. Track:

  • Does the AI answer within 2 seconds?
  • Does it capture all required info?
  • Does the lead appear in Supabase?
  • Does the caller get a confirmation SMS?
  • Does the "owner" get notified?
  • Does the follow-up sequence trigger correctly?
  • Does the review request go out after the mock appointment?

Fix every broken step. Run through again until it's flawless.

Record an updated Loom demo showing the FULL flow (voice agent + follow-up + review request). This is your sales weapon.

Practice the demo call. Role-play: one of you is the HVAC owner, the other pitches. Switch roles. Practice handling objections (see FAQ section).

DAYS 12-14 Outreach Prep & Warmup Check

Paola — Focus

Check warmup health in Smartlead. After 10-14 days of warmup, check your sender reputation. Open rates on warmup emails should be 40%+ and spam rate under 2%. If not, troubleshoot DNS records.

Upload first 200 leads to Smartlead. Create your first campaign. Set to start Day 15 (Monday of Week 3).

Prepare your phone call tracker spreadsheet. Columns: Company, Contact Name, Phone, Date Called, Result (Voicemail/Spoke/Not Interested/Demo Booked), Follow-up Date, Notes.

Write your first LinkedIn post. Something like: "I just tested calling 20 HVAC companies in [City]. 14 of them went to voicemail. That's 14 potential customers lost to whoever picks up next. We're building something to fix this." Post it.

Mike — Focus

Create a client onboarding template. A Google Doc with everything you need from a new client:

  • Business name, address, phone number
  • Services they offer (list of all service types)
  • Business hours
  • Service area (which zip codes/cities)
  • How they want leads handled (call back? text? email?)
  • Existing scheduling tool? (or will they use Cal.com)
  • Google Business Profile link (for review automation)

Build a "client clone" workflow. Make your demo setup duplicatable so when you sign a new client, you can spin up their voice agent in 2-4 hours, not 2 days. Create templates in Vapi and n8n that you just swap out business name, phone number, and services.

Set up monitoring. Create an n8n workflow that checks every 6 hours whether all active phone agents are responding. If one fails, send yourself a Slack/SMS alert.

End of Week 2 Checkpoint

You should have: a bulletproof demo, the full 3-service suite built and tested, a Loom recording ready to send, cold emails loaded in Smartlead and warmup looking healthy, 500+ leads ready to go, a cloneable setup so new client onboarding takes hours not days. You're ready to start selling.

Quick-Win Services (Revenue Before Your Full Agent is Ready)

While you’re building and testing your full AI agent (Weeks 1-4), you can already offer these simpler services. Each takes under 2 hours to set up.

1. Missed Call Text-Back (Twilio Only — No AI Needed)

$200-300/mo

When a call goes to voicemail, auto-send SMS: “Hi, we missed your call! How can we help? Reply here or we’ll call you back within 15 minutes.” No AI, no Vapi. Just call forwarding + SMS trigger. Build time: 30 minutes. Your cost: ~$5/mo in Twilio.

2. Google Business Profile Optimization

$250-500 one-time

Most contractors have unclaimed or poorly optimized GBP. Claim it, add photos, update hours, write keyword-rich description, add services, respond to reviews, add Q&A. Takes ~2 hours. Great foot-in-the-door — then upsell the AI agent. Google reports complete profiles get meaningfully more calls and direction requests than incomplete ones — cite Google’s own Business Profile guidance, not a vendor percentage.

3. Review Request Automation

$150-200/mo

After each job, auto-SMS: “Thanks for choosing [Business]! If you had a great experience, a Google review helps a lot: [link].” Build with a Google Form trigger + Twilio SMS in n8n. Build time: 45 minutes.

4. Missed Call Audit Report (Free Lead Magnet)

FREE — lead gen tool

Call a prospect’s business 5 times at different hours over a week. Document how many went to voicemail. Package as a PDF: “We called your business 5 times — here’s what your customers experience.” Devastating sales tool. Free to do, 30 minutes per prospect.

The Ladder Strategy

Start with a quick-win (low risk, easy yes). Deliver results. Upsell to the full AI agent: “You’re getting 15 text-backs per week. Imagine if those callers talked to an AI receptionist and booked appointments instead. Want to see what that looks like?”

Week 4: Close Your First Client

DAYS 22-28 Demo → Close → Onboard

The Demo Call Script (15-20 min)

Minutes 1-3: Build rapport

"Hey [Name], thanks for taking the time. Before I show you anything, tell me — how are you currently handling calls when you're out on a job?" Listen. Take notes. Mirror their frustration back to them.

Minutes 3-5: Quantify the pain

"Roughly how many calls would you say you miss in a week? And what's your average job value?" Do the math with them: "So if you're missing even 5 calls a week and your average job is $3,000, that's 5 × 52 = 260 missed calls a year. Even if only one in five would have booked, that's 52 jobs — call it $156,000 of work you never quoted. Use their real ticket, and halve it out loud so they trust the number."

Minutes 5-10: Show the demo

"Let me show you what it looks like. I'm going to call this number right now, and I want you to listen." Call the demo number on speakerphone. Let them hear the AI handle a fake customer call. Then show the dashboard where the lead appeared.

Minutes 10-12: Show the full flow

"And here's the best part — after the call, the customer automatically gets a confirmation text. And you get an instant notification with all their info. No more playing phone tag."

Minutes 12-15: Handle questions

Answer their questions honestly. Common ones: "What if the caller wants a real person?" (it can transfer), "What about my existing phone number?" (we forward, no change needed), "What if they ask something the AI can't handle?" (it takes a message and alerts you immediately).

Minutes 15-18: Present pricing

"Two options that fit you. The AI receptionist on its own is $500 a month with a one-time $1,500 setup. Most people take the full Never Miss a Call bundle — receptionist plus lead follow-up plus review requests — at $1,000 a month with a $2,500 setup, because it covers the whole customer journey instead of just the phone. Both include your monthly minutes: 1,000 on the receptionist, 1,500 on the bundle, and anything over that is 35 cents a minute so there are never surprise invoices. We have you live within a week." [For clients 1-3 only, swap this for the Founding Client offer: $497 setup + $497/mo, in exchange for a written case study and permission to use call recordings. Say that trade out loud — it is why the price is low, and it stops them expecting that rate forever.]

Minutes 18-20: Close

"Based on what you told me about missing [X] calls per week, this would pay for itself within the first week or two. Want to get started? I can send over the agreement today and have you live by [date]."

When They Say Yes

Client Onboarding (Day 1-2 after signing) — every task has one owner

Runs straight off the Handoff Packet. Paola owns the client-facing half, Mike owns the build half, and Paola signs off before it goes live.

Paola — Send Stripe invoice for the setup fee and start the recurring charge at the rung you actually sold — for clients 1-3 that is the Founding offer ($497 setup + $497/mo), otherwise Starter ($1,500 + $500/mo) or the Bundle ($2,500 + $1,000/mo). Never invent a number here: check the ladder.

Paola — Send onboarding questionnaire (the template Mike built in Week 2). Get: business name, services, hours, service area, existing phone number, Google Business link.

Mike — Buy a Twilio phone number with their area code.

Mike — Clone your demo Vapi assistant. Customize greeting, business name, services offered, and appointment availability.

Mike — Clone your n8n workflow template. Update: phone number, business name, owner email/phone for notifications, Google review link.

Paola — Set up call forwarding with the client. Work with the client to forward their after-hours calls (or all calls) to the new Twilio number. This usually means a 5-minute change in their existing phone provider.

Paola — Run the 10-call test, then test with the client on the line. She holds the go-live veto. Call together, let them hear it work with their business name. Get their approval.

Go live. Flip the switch. Send the client a "You're Live!" email with: their new phone number, a link to their dashboard, and your support contact.

What If You Haven't Closed Anyone by End of Week 4?

This is normal. Most agencies close their first client in weeks 3-6. If Week 4 ends with no client: (1) Review your email metrics — are people opening but not replying? Rewrite the body. Not opening? Rewrite subject lines. (2) Increase phone calls to 15-20/day. (3) Try a different angle — instead of cold outreach, offer 3 local businesses a free 2-week trial. Getting them to experience the product is more powerful than any pitch. (4) Don't panic. Keep the daily rhythm.

Demo Environment: Your Sales Weapon

Your demo is what closes deals. Not your pitch, not your slides — the moment a prospect hears the AI answer a real phone call in their trade’s language. Here’s how to build a demo that converts at 40%+.

What Your Demo Environment Needs

1. A Working Demo Phone Number

Set up a dedicated Twilio number connected to your best Vapi agent. This is your “showroom model.” Keep it polished. Use a local area code from your target market (e.g., 305 for Miami, 713 for Houston). Cost: $1/mo.

2. Three Pre-Built Agent Templates

Have ready-to-go agents for HVAC, Plumbing, and Electrical. When a plumber calls, you demo the plumbing agent. When an HVAC owner calls, demo the HVAC agent. 15 seconds of personalization (swap company name) makes it feel custom.

3. A Loom Demo Library

Pre-record 3 polished Loom videos (2-3 min each): one showing the AI answering a call, one showing the lead capture in action, one showing the monthly report. Send these BEFORE the demo call to warm prospects up.

4. A Simple Demo Dashboard

A web page (even a Google Sheet with charts) showing sample data: calls answered, appointments booked, response times. This makes the “monthly report” tangible. Prospect thinks: “I’d get THIS every month?”

The Live Demo Script (What Makes Them Say “Wow”)

Step 1: “I’m going to call our demo number right now. Pretend you’re a homeowner whose AC just broke at 9pm on a Friday. Watch how the AI handles it.”

Step 2: Call the demo number ON SPEAKER during the Zoom/phone call. Let the prospect listen in real-time.

Step 3: The AI answers instantly: “Thank you for calling [Demo HVAC Company], this is Sarah. I’m here to help. What seems to be the issue?”

Step 4: Role-play as the homeowner: “Yeah, my AC stopped working and it’s 95 degrees in here.”

Step 5: The AI handles it — asks for address, schedules appointment, sends confirmation text.

Step 6: Show the prospect the text message that arrived. Show the lead in the dashboard. “This is what your customer would experience. And this is what you’d see.”

The Killer Move

If you know the prospect’s business name, swap it into the demo agent 5 minutes before the call. When they hear “Thank you for calling [Their Actual Business Name]” — that’s the moment they go from skeptical to sold. Mike can do this swap in 30 seconds in the Vapi dashboard.

Recording Your Loom Demo (The #1 Sales Tool)

The Script (2 minutes)

0:00-0:15 — Hook

“Hey [Name], I noticed your business phone went to voicemail when I called — and that’s exactly the problem we solve. Let me show you what happens when you have our AI agent answering instead.”

0:15-1:15 — Live Call Demo

Where to Use This Loom

Cold email replies, LinkedIn DMs, website embed, Facebook group posts, follow-up after cold calls, and your Carrd/website hero video. One recording, used everywhere. Re-record every 3 months as your demo gets more polished.

Knowledge Check Module 3 Quiz

You built your demo agent. A prospect agrees to a live demo call. What's the single most important thing to do before the call?

Exactly. Calling their number gives you live proof of the problem: "I called your business at 6pm last night and got voicemail — here's the screenshot." Then your working demo shows the solution. Real evidence beats slides every time.
Slide decks and pricing sheets slow down the close. The power move is calling their actual number to document the problem (missed call, voicemail, long hold), then demoing your agent live. Show, don't tell.

Ask for referrals. "Do you know any other contractors who struggle with missed calls? I'd love to help them too. Happy to give you a $250 credit for any referral that signs up."

Write a LinkedIn case study post. "We helped [Client] capture [X] calls they would have missed in the first 2 weeks. That's an estimated $[Y] in jobs saved. Here's how..." (get client permission first).

Email Optimization Checklist

Reply rate below 2%? Test new subject lines (open rate is unreliable post-Apple-MPP — judge on replies). Best performers: question-based ("Still losing calls at [Company]?"), stat-based ("78% of callers hang up on voicemail"), personalized ("[First Name], quick question about [Company]")

Reply rate below 3%? Shorten the email body to 3-4 sentences max. Add a specific pain point. Include one clear CTA ("Worth 15 minutes this week?")

High unsubscribe/spam rate? Check warmup health in Smartlead. Lower daily send volume by 25%. Make sure unsubscribe link works.

Getting replies but no demos? Your reply template needs work. Respond within 30 minutes. Suggest 2 specific times instead of "when works for you?"

Ask: "How would you describe the AI to another contractor?" Use their exact words — authentic > polished

If You Have 0 Clients by End of Week 8

Don't panic. Check these in order: (1) Are your emails landing in inbox? Check Smartlead deliverability. (2) Are you sending enough volume? 50+ emails/day minimum. (3) Are you making phone calls? Email alone is slow — calls accelerate everything. (4) Is your offer clear? "I'll answer your phones 24/7 for $500/mo" is clearer than "AI-powered communication solutions." (5) Consider offering your first client a 50% discount or 30-day free trial to get proof. The first client is the hardest. After that, everything accelerates.

Hiring Your First Colombian VA

This is one of your biggest competitive advantages. Paola manages the VA in native Spanish — zero language barrier, zero cultural friction. Here’s how to do it right:

Where to Find Them

There Is Talent (pre-vetted, $8-12/hr) • SharkHelpers (bilingual, US timezone) • OnlineJobs.ph (Filipino VAs, $4-8/hr) • Upwork (broader pool, $5-15/hr) • Paola’s personal network in Colombia

What They Do (Start Small)

Lead list building from Google Maps/Apollo • Smartlead campaign management • Updating CRM/tracker • Scheduling follow-ups • Basic customer support replies • Social media content scheduling

Hiring Process

1. Post job description with clear tasks • 2. Screen 5-10 candidates with a 15-min video call • 3. Give top 2 a paid test task ($20-30) • 4. Hire the winner part-time (10-15 hrs/week) • 5. Start with a 2-week trial before committing • 6. Pay via Wise ($3 transfer fee) or PayPal

Cost Math

10 hrs/week × $10/hr = $400/mo. If they handle lead research that frees Paola for 10 more sales calls/week → 2-3 extra demos/month → 1 extra client ($1,000+/mo recurring). ROI: 2.5x in month one. Scale to 20 hrs/week ($800/mo) once you hit 12+ clients.

VA Job Post Template (Copy & Customize)

VIRTUAL ASSISTANT — AI Automation Agency (Part-Time, Remote) Company: Colibri Code LLC (US-based AI agency serving home service contractors) Role: Operations & Lead Research Assistant Hours: 10-15 hrs/week (flexible schedule, US business hours) Pay: $8-12/hr USD (paid weekly via Wise) Location: Remote (Colombia preferred, LatAm welcome) Language: Fluent English + Native Spanish required WHAT YOU'LL DO - Build targeted lead lists from Google Maps and Apollo.io (we'll train you — no prior experience needed) - Manage cold email campaigns in Smartlead (load leads, monitor replies, flag interested prospects) - Update our client tracker in Supabase/Google Sheets - Schedule follow-up tasks and calendar appointments - Reply to basic inbound emails using templates we provide - Create simple social media posts from templates - Research local contractors in target US cities WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Reliable, organized, detail-oriented - Comfortable learning new software tools quickly - Strong written English (you'll draft short emails) - Available during US Eastern hours (9am-1pm ET minimum) - Stable internet connection - Bonus: experience with CRM tools, cold email, or lead gen WHAT WE OFFER - Flexible schedule (work from anywhere) - Paid training (first week is training, still paid) - Clear SOPs for every task (no guessing) - Growth: start at 10 hrs, scale to 20+ as we grow - Long-term position (not a one-off project) - Supportive team (Paola manages in Spanish, zero friction) TO APPLY Send a short Loom video (2 min max) introducing yourself in English. Tell us: your name, where you're based, your relevant experience, and why you'd be a good fit. Email to: [EMAIL] Applications without a Loom video will not be reviewed.

Why the Loom requirement: It filters out 80% of low-effort applicants. Anyone who records a clear, confident 2-minute video in English is already proving they can communicate, follow instructions, and use basic tech tools. That’s your entire job description.

VA Interview Questions (15-Minute Screen)

“Walk me through your typical workday.” — You want someone who already works remotely and has structure. Red flag: “I’m flexible, whatever you need.” Green flag: “I work 8am–1pm, then again 3–5pm.”

“Tell me about a time you had to learn a new software tool quickly.” — They’ll be learning Smartlead, Apollo, Supabase. You need someone who isn’t intimidated by new tools.

“If I give you a task and the instructions are unclear, what do you do?” — Right answer: “I’d ask before guessing.” Wrong answer: “I’d figure it out myself.” You want communicators, not cowboys.

“What’s your internet speed?” — Have them run a speed test live on the call. Under 10 Mbps is a risk for video calls and tool access.

“What hours are you available in US Eastern time?” — You need at least 4 consecutive hours during US business hours. Colombia is ET or ET-1 depending on the season — perfect overlap.

Paid test task ($25): “Find 20 HVAC companies in Charlotte, NC from Google Maps. For each one, get: business name, phone number, Google rating, number of reviews, and whether they have a website. Put it in this Google Sheet. You have 48 hours.”

VA First-Week Training Checklist

Week 1 is 100% training, fully paid. Record Loom walkthroughs for each task so the VA can rewatch. This library also trains future VAs if this one leaves.

Day 1: Company overview (what you do, who your clients are, how the business works). Share the agency-plan overview section. Set up their email, Slack, and tool logins.

Day 2: Tool training: Google Maps prospecting. Walk them through finding contractors, extracting info, entering it into the lead tracker. Have them do 10 leads while you watch.

Day 3: Tool training: Apollo.io for email enrichment. Show them how to find emails, verify them, and export to Smartlead. Do 20 leads together.

Day 4: Tool training: Smartlead campaign management. Show them how to load leads, monitor replies, categorize responses (interested / not interested / out of office / wrong person).

Day 5: Solo practice day. Assign: “Build a list of 50 plumbing companies in Dallas, TX. Enrich emails in Apollo. Load into Smartlead staging.” Review their work at end of day. Give feedback.

Golden rule: Never give a VA access to client-facing tools (Vapi, Twilio, Stripe, client email) in the first month. Start with lead research only. Add responsibilities as trust builds. One mistake in a client’s Twilio account can cost you the relationship.

This VA is hire #1. For hires #2-5 — delivery tech, appointment setter, account manager — and the measurable trigger for each, see .

Knowledge Check Module 4 Quiz

Your first client has been live for 30 days. When you run the monthly review call, what's the most important metric to lead with?

Revenue protected is the only number that justifies their monthly payment. "Your agent caught 23 after-hours calls. At your average job of $2,800, that's $64,400 in potential revenue that would've gone to voicemail." That's what makes them say "worth every penny."
Call volume and voice quality are supporting details, not headlines. Lead with money: estimated revenue protected = missed calls caught × average job value. That's the number that makes them renew every single month.

Sales & Client Acquisition

Lead generation, cold email, pipeline management, scripts, and onboarding

3 hours Intermediate 12 Lessons
What You'll Learn
  • Build a multi-channel lead generation system
  • Set up cold email infrastructure that avoids spam
  • Run the Missed Call Audit to create urgency
  • Master the discovery call and demo script
  • Create proposals that close at 40%+ rate
  • Onboard new clients in under 48 hours
  • Qualify prospects with a structured discovery call framework
  • Run a content marketing engine that turns posts into pipeline
Growth Engine

Lead Generation Engine

You need a constant pipeline of prospects. Here's every channel, tool, and tactic for finding home service businesses that need you — ranked by cost and effectiveness.

Channel 1: Cold Email (Primary — Do This First)

How it works: Scrape contractor data → enrich with email → send personalized cold emails at scale → book demos from replies.

Tools:

  • • Apollo.io (free tier: 1,200 credits/mo) — Search "HVAC" + "Owner" + city. Export with verified emails.
  • • Outscraper ($0.002/result) — Scrape Google Maps for every plumber/HVAC in a city. Gets phone, website, reviews, address.
  • • Apify Google Maps Scraper (free tier: $5 credit/mo) — Alternative to Outscraper. More data per result.
  • • Clay.com ($149/mo when ready to scale) — Waterfall enrichment: finds emails by trying 5+ providers. 95%+ find rate.
  • • Smartlead.ai ($39/mo) — Sends emails from multiple inboxes, auto-warmup, tracks opens/replies.
  • • Instantly.ai ($97/mo alternative) — Higher sending limits. Consider upgrading from Smartlead at 5+ clients.

Volume targets:

  • • Week 3-4: 50 emails/day across 3 sending domains
  • • Month 2+: 150 emails/day across 5 sending domains
  • • Expected reply rate: 3-8% (book demo from ~30% of positive replies)
  • • Expected demos/month at 150/day: 8-15 demos → 3-5 closes

Channel 2: Cold Calling (Highest Conversion)

Why it works: Contractors are physical people. They respect someone who picks up the phone. A warm voice + "I just tried calling your business and got voicemail" is devastating.

Tools:

  • • Your Twilio number — Shows a US caller ID to the prospect
  • • OpenPhone ($15/mo) — Better UI for outbound calls, voicemail drops, call recording
  • • PhoneBurner ($149/mo, when scaling) — Power dialer. 60-80 calls/hour vs 15-20 manual.

Volume targets:

  • • 10-15 calls/day during your 3-5pm CET window (9-11am ET)
  • • Connect rate: ~30% (the rest are voicemails — leave one!)
  • • Demo booking rate from connects: 15-25%
  • • Expected demos/week from calls: 3-5

The "Live Test" power move: Call the prospect's business number first. If it goes to voicemail, you now have real proof. Call their cell: "Hey [Name], I just called [Company Name] and got voicemail. That's actually why I'm reaching out..."

Channel 3: LinkedIn Outreach

Best for: Larger contractors with 10+ employees, franchise owners, multi-location businesses.

Tools:

  • • LinkedIn Sales Navigator ($99/mo) — Advanced search: "Owner" + "HVAC" + specific metros
  • • Dripify ($59/mo) — Automated connection requests + follow-up sequences. Safe LinkedIn automation.
  • • Expandi ($99/mo alternative) — Cloud-based, mimics human behavior better. Lower ban risk.

Sequence: Connection request (personalized note) → Day 2: "Thanks for connecting" + value message → Day 5: Share relevant content → Day 8: Soft pitch with Loom demo link.

Volume: 25-30 connection requests/day. 15-25% accept rate. Message 5-8 new connections/day.

Channel 4: Google Maps Prospecting (Free)

How: Search "[trade] near [city]" on Google Maps. Open each listing. Look for:

  • • No website or crappy website (they need help)
  • • Few Google reviews (they need reputation management)
  • • Call the number — if voicemail, they're your perfect prospect
  • • Check their hours — if they close at 5pm but emergencies happen at 10pm, pitch 24/7 AI

Pro tip: Use Outscraper to bulk-export Google Maps results with phone numbers, review counts, and websites. Filter for businesses with <20 reviews and no website → these are your warmest leads. They're not tech-savvy enough to solve this themselves.

Channel 5: Facebook Groups (Free, High-Trust)

Target groups:

  • • "HVAC Technicians and Business Owners"
  • • "Plumbing Business Owners"
  • • "Contractor Marketing Tips"
  • • "Home Service Business Growth"
  • • City-specific: "[City] Small Business Owners"

Strategy: Don't pitch directly. Post value content: "We tracked 50 HVAC companies for a month — here's how many calls they missed after hours [infographic]." Let people come to you. Answer questions about AI and automation. DM anyone who engages.

Volume: Join 10-15 groups. Post 2-3x/week (rotate content). Comment on 5-10 posts/day. This builds pipeline for weeks 4+.

Channel 6: Referral Partners (Highest LTV)

Who refers contractors to you:

  • • Business coaches who serve contractors — They have 20-50 clients each. One intro = months of pipeline.
  • • Web designers who build contractor sites — They don't do AI/phone. You're a natural add-on.
  • • HVAC supply distributors — They know every HVAC company in town. Offer $250 per client signed.
  • • Trade association chapters — PHCC (plumbing), ACCA (HVAC). Offer to do a free webinar on "AI for contractors."
  • • Accountants/bookkeepers who serve contractors — They see the revenue leakage firsthand.
  • • Existing clients — $250 credit per referral that signs. Contractors know contractors.

Referral compensation: $250-$500 per closed deal, or 10-15% of the retainer for as long as the client stays, or reciprocal referrals. Whatever motivates the specific partner.

Channel 7: Paid Ads (Month 3+)

Don't start here. Only add paid after you have testimonials and a proven offer. Then:

  • • Google Ads: $15-30/day. Target: "HVAC answering service," "plumber virtual receptionist," "after hours phone service for contractors." Low competition. $5-15/click.
  • • Facebook/Meta Ads: $10-20/day. Target business owners in home services by interest + geo. Lead form ads → book demo directly.
  • • YouTube Ads: Run your Loom demo as a skippable ad targeting "HVAC marketing" and "contractor business growth" videos. $0.05-0.15/view.

Economics: If your average client value is $1,000/mo × 18 months average retention = $18,000 LTV, you can comfortably afford $500-$1,000 to acquire a client. At $15/click and 3% landing page conversion, CPA ≈ $500. Profitable.

Plain English: Paola's Sales Pipeline in Simple Terms

Think of lead generation like a funnel. Here's what Paola does each day:

Step 1 — Find people (30 min/day): Go on Apollo.io, search "HVAC owner in Houston." Export 20-30 names with emails. Add them to your Smartlead campaigns. This is the fuel that keeps the engine running.

Step 2 — Email them (automated): Smartlead sends your 3-email sequence automatically. You wrote the emails once. Now they go out every day to new people while you sleep.

Step 3 — Reply to interested ones (15 min/day): Check Smartlead each morning. When someone replies "I'm interested" or "Tell me more" — respond within 2 hours. Goal: book them for a 15-minute demo call.

Step 4 — Call cold prospects (3-5pm CET): Call 10-15 people from your list. These are HVAC/plumbing owners. Simple pitch: "I tried calling your business and got voicemail — that's costing you $50K+ a year. Want to see how we fix that?"

Step 5 — Run demo calls (with Mike): When someone's interested, you both jump on a 15-min video call. Mike shows the AI in action. Paola handles pricing and "let's get started."

The math: 150 emails/day × 5% reply rate = ~7-8 interested replies/week. + 50 calls/week × 30% connect × 20% interested = 3 interested/week. = ~10 hot leads/week → ~3-4 demos → 1-2 new clients/month. Rinse and repeat.

Client Acquisition Pipeline: Lead → Close

The Lead Gen section above fills the top of the funnel. This section covers what happens from the moment someone shows interest to the moment they hand you money. Every step, every script, every timeline.
