Stage 7.5: The Handoff Packet (the seam where client #1 breaks)

The pipeline used to jump straight from “signed” to “Mike builds, Paola manages” with nothing in between — which means every promise Mike made on the call lived only in Mike’s head. Paola then onboards a client whose expectations she cannot see. Mike fills this out before closing the laptop on signature day, pastes it into the client’s record, and messages Paola.

HANDOFF PACKET — [CLIENT NAME] — signed [DATE] WHAT I ACTUALLY SOLD Tier: [Founding / Starter / Bundle / Scale] Setup fee: $______ (paid in full? / 50-50?) Monthly: $______ starting [DATE] Minutes included: ______ overage $0.35/min — did I say this out loud? [Y/N] Anything I discounted or threw in: ______________________ Guarantee I promised, word for word: ____________________ THE PEOPLE Owner / decision maker: ______________ mobile: ______________ Second contact (office manager / dispatcher): ______________ Who internally is SKEPTICAL of this, and why: ______________ Language: [English / Spanish / both] → if Spanish, Paola leads the build review WHAT THEY ACTUALLY CARE ABOUT (their words, not mine) The pain they described: "_______________________________" The moment that sold them: "____________________________" What "working" looks like to them in 30 days: _____________ COMMITMENTS I MADE ON THE CALL Go-live date promised: ____________ (default: 48 hours) Anything custom I agreed to: ______________________________ Anything I explicitly said we would NOT do: _______________ OPERATIONAL FACTS FOR THE BUILD Trade / services: ______________________________ Service area (ZIPs): ______________________________ Hours + after-hours rule: _____________________________ What counts as an emergency: __________________________ Price ranges I may quote: _____________________________ Calendar / FSM they use: ______________________________ Current phone setup + who answers now: ________________ PAOLA'S FIRST THREE ACTIONS 1. Send welcome email + intake form (same day) 2. Book the kickoff call within 24 hours 3. Schedule the 10-call test BEFORE go-live — she holds the veto

The rule that makes this stick: the packet is done when Paola replies “got it.” Not when Mike sends it. If Mike closes a deal and goes to bed, Paola wakes up to a client who was promised something she can’t see — and the 48-hour clock is already running. Client #1 is the case study the entire Founding price exists to buy; the handoff has to work the very first time.

Stage 3: Booking the Demo (Paola)

When someone replies to your email or you connect on a cold call, the ONLY goal is to book a 15-minute demo. Don't sell on email. Don't explain pricing. Just book the call.

REPLY TEMPLATE — Booking the Demo "Hey [NAME], glad you're open to seeing it! The easiest thing is to hop on a quick 15-minute Zoom — I'll actually call your business number live so you can hear exactly how the AI handles a real customer call. No pitch deck, just a live demo. Here's my calendar — grab any slot that works for you: [CAL.COM LINK] Talk soon, Paola Colibri Code"

Key rules: Always send the Cal.com link (don't go back and forth on times). Respond within 2 hours of their reply. If they don't book within 48 hours, send one follow-up: "Hey [Name], just bumping this up — still happy to show you the demo. Here's the link again: [LINK]." After that, move them back to the email sequence.

Pricing Psychology: How to Present Your Prices

1. Anchor High, Then Show Your Price

“A receptionist costs $3,000/month. Ruby answering service is $449/month for just 100 minutes. We’re $1,000/month with 1,500 AI minutes included — roughly 600 calls — 24/7, with automation built in.” Always mention expensive alternatives BEFORE your price.

2. Frame as Daily Cost

“That’s about $33 a day — less than what you pay a helper for one hour. And it works 24/7.”

3. Use Their Numbers Against Them

“You’re losing $40K a year in missed calls. Our service is $12K a year. You’re 3x ahead even if we only catch half.”

4. Never Discount the Monthly — Discount the Setup

If they push back: “I can waive half the setup fee if you start this week.” Never reduce the monthly — protect recurring revenue.

5. Annual Discount (Lock Them In)

“$10,000/year instead of $12,000 — saves you $2,000. And I’ll waive the setup fee entirely.”

6. The Paid Pilot Close

For “I need to think about it”: “Let me set it up for a $250 pilot, credited to your setup fee. Run it 7 days. If you don’t see value, I shut it off and you decide at the end and the $250 comes off your setup either way.” Pilot conversion rate: 60-80%.

Discovery Questions Master List

Pick 3-5 based on the conversation. Goal: get them to tell YOU how much they’re losing.

Pain Discovery

“Walk me through what happens when a customer calls and you’re on a job.”

“How many calls would you guess go to voicemail in a typical week?”

“What’s your busiest time of day for incoming calls?”

“Do you get many calls after hours or on weekends?”

“Have you ever lost a job because you couldn’t answer the phone?”

“What happens with your Spanish-speaking callers?”

Value Qualification

“What’s your average job ticket?”

“How many trucks/techs do you have running?”

“Are you doing any marketing right now — Google Ads, mailers?”

“Have you looked into answering services before?”

“If you could wave a magic wand, what would your phone situation look like?”

“Who answers your phones right now?”

The Golden Question

“So if each of those missed calls is worth $[their average job], and you’re missing [X] per week… that’s roughly $[math] per month walking to your competitors. Does that number feel about right?” Let them sit with it. Then show the demo.

Stage 4: The Demo Call (Both — 15 Minutes)

This is where you close. Follow this structure exactly:

Minutes 0-2: Rapport + Pain Discovery (Paola leads)

"Thanks for jumping on, [Name]. Before I show you anything — tell me a little about your business. How many calls do you get per day? What happens when you're out on a job and can't answer?"

Let them talk. Listen for pain: missed calls, voicemail, losing jobs to competitors, overwhelmed receptionist. Write down specific numbers they mention — you'll use them later.

Minutes 2-3: Set Up the Live Test (Mike)

"I'm going to call a demo number right now so you can hear exactly what your customers would experience. This is a live AI agent set up for an HVAC company. Listen to how it handles the call."

Minutes 3-7: LIVE DEMO — Call the AI Agent (Mike)

Put your phone on speaker and call the demo number. Act as a customer: "Yeah, my AC stopped working and it's 95 degrees. Can someone come today?" Let the AI handle the full call — booking, confirmation, the works. This is the moment that sells. Let the product do the work.

While the call plays, share your screen showing the notification come in real-time: the lead captured in the dashboard, the SMS confirmation sent to the "customer," the owner notification. Visual proof.

Minutes 7-9: Connect to Their Pain (Paola)

"So [Name], you mentioned you miss about [X] calls a week. At an average job value of [amount they said], that's roughly $[math] a month walking out the door. This agent would catch every single one of those."

Minutes 9-11: Pricing + Offer (Mike — one quoter, always)

"Here's how it works. We set everything up for you — custom-scripted to your business, your services, your hours. It's $[setup fee] to build it and $[monthly] per month. Most of our clients see ROI in the first week just from calls they would've missed."

Present the Bundle as the default (Founding Client rate for clients 1-3). Only mention individual services if they push back on price. If they're a bilingual market, add: "And because you serve a lot of Spanish-speaking customers, we include bilingual support — the agent switches to Spanish automatically."

Minutes 11-13: Handle Objections + Close (Both)

See the FAQ & Objections section for every objection and exactly what to say. The most common:

  • • "Let me think about it" → Offer the 7-day paid pilot ($250, credited to setup) (see below)
  • • "That's too expensive" → Do the ROI math with their numbers
  • • "My customers won't like AI" → "Call the number yourself right now — did you notice it was AI?"

Minutes 13-15: Next Steps (Paola)

If YES: "Amazing! I'll send over the agreement today. Once signed, Mike will have your agent live within 48 hours. I'll send you a quick onboarding form to fill out — takes 5 minutes."

If MAYBE: "Totally fair. How about this — let me set up a $250 7-day paid pilot so you can see it in action with your real calls. Zero risk. If you love it, we'll make it permanent. If not, we turn it off and you decide at the end and the $250 comes off your setup either way."

If NO: "No worries at all. I'll follow up in a couple weeks — things change when peak season hits. In the meantime, here's a case study from a [similar trade] company that was in the same boat."

The 7-Day Paid Pilot ($250, credited to setup) — Your Secret Weapon

How it works mechanically:

  • • Mike builds their AI agent (same as a paid client — takes 2-3 hours)
  • • Set up call forwarding from their number to the AI (5-minute change on their phone)
  • • The AI answers their calls for 7 days. You monitor everything.
  • • Day 3: Send a text — "Your agent answered X calls so far. Here's a quick summary."
  • • Day 7: Send the full report — total calls answered, appointments booked, leads captured, estimated revenue saved
  • • Day 7 call: "Here are your results. Want to keep it running? Here's the agreement."

Your cost to run a paid pilot: ~$5-15 in Vapi/Twilio usage for the week. Your time: ~3 hours (build + monitoring). If they don't convert, you lost $15 and 3 hours. If they do, you gained a $1,000/mo client for the next 12+ months.

Conversion rate from pilot → retainer: 60-80% (they've already experienced it working — this isn't hypothetical anymore).

When to offer it: When someone says "let me think about it" or "I'm not sure." Never offer it upfront — always try to close at full price first. The trial is your fallback, not your opener.

The Follow-Up Machine: No-Shows, "Not Nows" & the 5-Hour Sales Week

Here's the uncomfortable math of your pipeline: roughly a third of booked demos will no-show, and 70-80% of the demos you DO give will end in "let me think about it" — not a no, just not a yes. Most agencies let both groups die in the CRM. That's where most of your future clients are hiding. This lesson is the system that keeps every lead alive with almost zero ongoing effort.

The mindset shift: a "not now" is an asset, not a rejection. That contractor's phone problem doesn't go away — it gets worse every season. Your job isn't to convince them today; it's to be the obvious call when the pain peaks. Sales studies consistently show most deals close after the 5th touch, and almost nobody makes it past touch 2.

Part 1: No-Show Recovery (Runs on Autopilot)

A no-show usually isn't disinterest — it's a contractor who got pulled onto a job site. Never shame, always make rebooking one tap. Build this once as an n8n workflow triggered by the Cal.com no-show flag:

WhenChannelGoal
5 min afterSMSAssume good faith, offer instant rebook link
Same day, ~4 hrs laterEmailRe-sell the value in 3 lines + rebook link
Next morningSMSThe "2-minute version" offer (video instead of meeting)
Day 4EmailGraceful close — moves them into the Not-Now Nurture below

Grab any 15-min slot that works and I'll show you the AI answering your phones live: [booking link] — [Your name] [SAME-DAY EMAIL] Subject: Missed you today — 15 min whenever works [Name], quick reset — no apology needed. In 15 minutes I'll show you: (1) me calling YOUR business line and what a customer hears right now, (2) my AI answering the exact same call and booking the job into a calendar. Rebook here: [booking link] If it's easier, reply with a day/time and I'll send the invite. [Your name] [NEXT-MORNING SMS] [Name] — if a meeting's tough this week, I recorded a 2-min video of the AI handling a real [trade] call instead: [Loom link]. Watch it whenever. If it clicks, my calendar's here: [booking link] [DAY-4 EMAIL] Subject: I'll leave you alone (mostly) [Name], I'll stop chasing — you're clearly busy, which is honestly the whole point of what I do. I'll check in once in a while with anything useful I find for [trade] companies in [city]. Meanwhile, one number worth knowing: across 70 million calls, only about half of home-services calls get answered by a person (Invoca, 2026) — and the ones that ring past 30 seconds do far better. Yours went to voicemail at [TIME]. When the phones get crazy this [season], I'm one text away. [Your name]

Part 2: The "Not Now" Nurture System

Every demo that doesn't close gets tagged with WHY, because the comeback message is different for each. Add a "Reason" field to your pipeline and use these four tags:

TagWhat they saidComeback triggerThe message that reopens it
PRICE"Too expensive right now"Their busy season starts (they have cash + pain)ROI math on THEIR ticket size, or the per-booking pricing option
TIMING"Call me after [event]"The exact date they said — put it in the calendar THAT DAY"You asked me to call you today" (massive credibility)
TRUST"Not sure AI can handle my customers"Every new case study / recording you produceA 60-sec call recording from a client in their trade
SILENTWent dark after demoQuarterly seasonal touchThe value-touch calendar below — never "just checking in"

The 12-touch value calendar. Every "not now" lead gets one useful message a month — never a pitch, always something a contractor would want anyway. Rotate these four formats (each month = one of them), and write all 12 in a single sitting each quarter with Claude:

📊 The Stat Drop

"Companies answering within 1 min win 4x more jobs — [source]. Curious where you land? Happy to run your number through my missed-call test again, free."

🏆 The Win Story

"An HVAC shop I work with booked 14 after-hours jobs last month — calls they used to lose to voicemail. Recording of one (30 sec): [link]"

🔧 The Free Tool

"Found a review-reply template pack that saves my clients an hour a week — here it is, no strings: [link]. (This is what being on my list gets you.)"

🌡️ The Seasonal Heads-Up

"Heat wave forecast next month = your phones triple. If you want the AI catching overflow before then, setup takes a week. Worth a 15-min call?"

Write 12 monthly nurture messages (one per month, starting [MONTH]) for [TRADE] business owners in [CITY/REGION] who saw my AI receptionist demo but didn't buy. Rotate these formats: stat drop, client win story, free tool/template, seasonal heads-up tied to the [TRADE] calendar (summer AC surge, fall furnace checks, winter pipe bursts, spring maintenance). Rules: 60-90 words each, SMS-friendly, zero pressure, no "just checking in," every message must be useful even if they never buy, end at most 4 of the 12 with a soft CTA. My proof points: [PASTE 2-3 CLIENT RESULTS]. Voice: plainspoken, contractor-to-contractor, no marketing fluff.

Automate the plumbing, keep the sends personal. n8n workflow: on the 1st of the month, pull every lead tagged NURTURE from your CRM, match to this month's message, and queue drafts for you to skim and send (personal SMS/email beats blast tools here — you have dozens of leads, not thousands). TIMING-tagged leads skip the queue: their callback date is a calendar event with an alarm. Total cost: ~$0. Total time: 30 min/month.

Part 3: The 5-Hour Sales Week

When delivery gets busy, sales is the first thing that slips — and a slipped pipeline shows up as a revenue hole 6 weeks later. This is the minimum effective dose. If you only protect five hours a week for getting customers, spend them exactly here:

BlockTimeDo exactly thisWeekly quota
1. Feed the machine60 minApprove VA's new prospect list, load into Smartlead, keep sequences full50+ new prospects

Cold Email Infrastructure Blueprint

Cold email still works in 2026 but inbox placement is harder than ever. Google and Microsoft are ruthless about filtering. If you skip the infrastructure, your emails go straight to spam. Follow this exactly.

The Domain Setup (Do This Week 1)

Rule #1: NEVER send cold email from your main domain (colibricode.com). If it gets flagged, your entire business email is burned.

Buy 3-5 secondary domains from Namecheap (~$10-12 each). They should look legitimate and related to your agency:

  • • colibricodeai.com / colibricodeagency.com / getcolibricode.com
  • • Or use variations: trycolibri.com / colibriautomation.com
  • • Avoid weird TLDs (.xyz, .io for cold email). Stick with .com

For each domain, set up:

  • • Google Workspace ($6/user/mo) — Create paola@ and mike@ on each domain
  • • SPF record — v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all
  • • DKIM — Generated in Google Workspace admin
  • • DMARC — v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com
  • • Custom tracking domain in Smartlead (so click tracking doesn't flag you)

Total cost: 5 domains = ~$55/year + 10 Google Workspace accounts = $60/mo. This is your most important investment.

The Warmup Timeline (Don't Rush This)

DayWhat to DoSending Limit
Day 1Create accounts, connect to Smartlead warmup0 cold emails (warmup only)
Days 2-14Smartlead sends/receives warmup emails automatically. Send a few personal emails from each account to build history.0 cold emails (warmup only)
Day 14Start slow: 5 cold emails per inbox per day5/inbox = 50 total (10 inboxes)
Day 21Increase to 10/inbox/day if deliverability is good (>95% inbox rate)10/inbox = 100/day
Day 28+Scale to 15-20/inbox/day max. Never exceed 20.15-20/inbox = 150-200/day

Common Mistake That Kills Deliverability

If you send 50+ emails from a single inbox, or blast 500 emails on day one, your domain gets blacklisted immediately. There is NO recovery. You'd need to buy new domains and start over. Patience here = everything.

Finding Contractor Emails (The Data Pipeline)

Step 1: Scrape Google Maps — Use Outscraper or Apify to pull every HVAC/plumber/electrician in your target city. You get: business name, phone, website, address, Google rating, review count.

Step 2: Find owner emails — Upload the list to Apollo.io (free tier: 1,200 credits/mo). Apollo matches businesses to owner/decision-maker emails. Expect ~40-60% match rate.

Step 3: Fill gaps with enrichment — For businesses Apollo misses, use:

  • • Hunter.io (free tier: 25 searches/mo) — Find emails from the business website
  • • Snov.io ($39/mo if needed) — Email finder + verifier
  • • Manual check: Visit the business website. 30% of contractor sites have the owner's email on the Contact page.

Step 4: Verify everything — Run all emails through a verifier (NeverBounce, $0.003/email or Smartlead's built-in). Never send to unverified emails — bounces destroy your sender reputation.

Target: 200-500 verified contractor emails per city. Focus on businesses with 10-100 Google reviews (big enough to have call volume, small enough to not have enterprise solutions).

Loom Video Prospecting (20% Reply Rate)

How to use personalized Loom videos for cold outreach

The Missed Call Audit: Your Secret Weapon

This single tactic has the highest conversion rate of any prospecting method. It's free, takes 10 minutes per prospect, and makes you look like a genius. Here's exactly how to do it.

The Method (Step by Step)

1
Pick a contractor from your prospect list. Ideally one who you've already sent a cold email to (or plan to). Someone with 20-100 Google reviews — established but not huge.
2
Call their business number during business hours (Mon-Fri, 10am-2pm their timezone). Use your personal phone. Note what happens: Does it ring? How many times? Does someone answer? Voicemail? IVR menu?
3
Call again after hours (6pm+ their timezone, or Sunday). Same thing — note what happens. This is where most contractors fail completely.
4
Check their Google reviews for complaints about responsiveness. Search reviews for: "couldn't reach," "never called back," "left a message," "went to voicemail," "no answer." Screenshot these.
5
Record a 2-minute Loom video showing: (1) You calling their number live and it going to voicemail, (2) The Google reviews mentioning responsiveness, (3) A 30-second demo of YOUR AI agent answering a similar call perfectly. End with: "I built this for [THEIR TRADE]. Want to see it working for [THEIR COMPANY NAME]?"
6
Send the Loom link via email, text, or both. Subject line: "I just called [COMPANY NAME] — here's what happened."

Why This Works So Well

It's not theoretical. You're not saying "you might miss calls." You're showing them VIDEO PROOF that they missed YOUR call. It's undeniable.

It creates urgency. When they see their own Google reviews complaining about responsiveness, they realize customers ARE leaving. Right now.

The demo sells itself. The contrast between "voicemail... voicemail... voicemail..." and then a smooth AI agent answering instantly is visceral. It's the before/after that closes deals.

Expected response rate: 25-40% (vs 3-8% for cold email alone). This is the single highest-converting prospecting tactic in the AI agency space.

2026 stats to put in the video and the follow-up

The reason this lands isn’t the tech — it’s the math. Use only sourced numbers (see the Command Center): only 52% of home-services calls are answered by a person, rising to 73% when the phone rings past 30 seconds (Invoca, 2026, 70M calls); 46% of answered home-services phone leads convert (Invoca, 2026); only 17% of HVAC pros respond to a lead within the hour (Jobber, 2026). Then do the arithmetic with their ticket size, not an internet average. And the kicker for outbound: cold AI-written email is dead (73% delete it on sight), but a recording of their own line going to voicemail is undeniable, personal proof — the highest-converting opener that exists for this niche. Lead with the leak, never with the features.

Scale it: let your AI place the after-hours call

Instead of dialing every prospect by hand, point a Vapi outbound agent at your prospect list to place a single after-hours “test” call to each published number, and log which ones went to voicemail/no-answer in Supabase. You wake up to a ranked list of the hottest prospects (the ones who clearly miss calls) plus the recording you’ll reference in your opener: “I called your line at 7:14pm last night and got voicemail — here’s what your AI front desk would have said instead.” Keep it to a brief, polite single call (no repeat dialing) to stay on the right side of the consent rules.

The Loom Video Script

LOOM VIDEO SCRIPT (2 minutes) [Screen recording — show your phone dialing their number] "Hey [FIRST NAME], this is [YOUR NAME] from Colibri Code. I actually just called [COMPANY NAME] — watch what happens... [Let it ring, show it going to voicemail] That's what your customers experience when you're busy on a job. And look — I found these in your Google reviews: [Show screenshots of reviews mentioning responsiveness] [Customer A]: 'Called twice, no answer. Went with someone else.' [Customer B]: 'Left a message. Nobody called back.' Now watch what happens when the same call hits an AI agent I built for [THEIR TRADE]: [Call your demo number — show AI answering instantly, booking an appointment] That just answered in under one second, got the customer's info, and booked the appointment. Your customer gets a confirmation text. You get a notification with all the details. If you want to see this working for [COMPANY NAME] specifically, I can set up a live demo in 15 minutes. Here's my calendar: [CAL.COM LINK] Have a great day."

Scaling the Audit: 5 Per Week Is the Floor, 5 Per Day Is the Ceiling

The Daily Prospecting Routine (Paola + Mike)

Spend 1 hour per day on audit outreach. The workflow:

  • • Paola (30 min): Pick 5 prospects from the list. Call each business number. Note results. Check Google reviews for complaints. Prepare the data.
  • • Mike (30 min): Record 5 Loom videos (gets faster with practice — 3-4 min each after a few). Paola sends them out with a personalized note.
  • • Weekly output: 25 personalized audit videos. At 30% response rate = 7-8 conversations. At 30% demo booking = 2-3 demos. At 30% close = 1 new client per week.

Inbound Lead Machine

The Content Marketing Engine: Turn Posts Into Pipeline

Cold calls and cold email get you started. Content gets you found. A simple, repeatable posting system across LinkedIn, Facebook Groups, TikTok/Reels, and optionally a Substack newsletter turns you from "who are you?" to "I've been following you — let's talk." The best part: AI does 80% of the work. You supply 20 minutes of thinking and Claude generates a week of content.

When to Start This

Not Day 1 — the phone is your Day 1 channel. Start the content engine in Week 3-4 once you have a working demo and ideally one client result. Content without proof is just noise; content with proof is a magnet.

The Weekly Content System (90 Minutes Total)

Every Monday morning, one person runs this system. By Monday afternoon, the whole week's content is scheduled. Here's the repeatable process:

Step 1 — Capture one insight (5 min): What happened this week? A client result, a call recording highlight, a stat you found, a mistake you made, a question a prospect asked. Write one sentence. That's your "seed."

Step 2 — Generate the content batch (15 min): Feed the seed to Claude using the prompt below. It generates: 2 LinkedIn posts, 3 short-form video scripts (TikTok/Reels), 2 Facebook Group comments, and 1 newsletter paragraph. Review and tweak — don't publish AI output raw.

Step 3 — Record 2-3 short videos (20 min): Talking head, phone in hand, show the AI agent in action. Under 60 seconds each. Film vertically. No editing needed — raw and authentic outperforms polished in this niche. One take, post it.

Step 4 — Schedule everything (10 min): Use Buffer (free for 3 channels) or just the native schedulers. LinkedIn: Tue + Thu. TikTok/Reels: Mon + Wed + Fri. Facebook Groups: engage when relevant, don't force a schedule.

Step 5 — Engage for 5 min/day: Reply to every comment. DM anyone who engages twice. "Thanks for the comment — do you deal with missed calls at your shop?" turns a like into a conversation. This is where content actually converts.

The AI Content Generator Prompt

WEEKLY CONTENT BATCH — PROMPT I run an AI automation agency that sells AI phone agents to home service businesses (HVAC, plumbing, electrical). My agency is called [NAME]. This week's content seed: "[PASTE YOUR ONE-SENTENCE INSIGHT — e.g., 'Client's AI agent booked 6 after-hours appointments this week that would have been missed calls']" Generate a content batch: 1. TWO LINKEDIN POSTS (each 100-150 words) - Post A: Tell the story behind the insight. Open with a hook line. End with a soft CTA ("DM me if you want to see how this works"). - Post B: Turn it into a contrarian take or data point. Open with a surprising stat or question. 2. THREE SHORT-FORM VIDEO SCRIPTS (TikTok/Instagram Reels) - Each under 45 seconds when read at normal pace - Hook in the first line (pattern interrupt) - Show don't tell: "Watch what happens when I call this HVAC company at 9pm..." - End with CTA: "Link in bio" or "Comment DEMO" 3. TWO FACEBOOK GROUP COMMENTS (for contractor groups) - Not pitches — value-first responses to common complaints like "I keep missing calls" or "Angi leads never answer" - End with an offer to share more info, not a link 4. ONE NEWSLETTER PARAGRAPH (for Substack/email list) - 3-4 sentences. The insight + the takeaway + link to book a demo Match my tone: direct, no-BS, conversational. I talk to blue-collar business owners, not marketers. No jargon.

The 7 Content Pillars (Rotate Weekly)

Never wonder "what should I post?" again. Every piece of content fits one of these seven angles. Rotate through them and you never repeat yourself:

PillarExample HookFormat
The Live Test"I called 20 HVAC companies in Houston at 6pm. 17 went to voicemail. Here's what that costs them..."Video (call on speaker) or LinkedIn post with data

The Repurposing Machine (One Idea = 7 Pieces)

You never need 7 ideas per week. You need one good idea and a system to repurpose it:

1. Seed idea (e.g., "client's AI caught 11 after-hours calls this week")

2. LinkedIn post (the story version, 150 words)

3. TikTok/Reel #1 ("watch what happens when I call this HVAC company at 10pm")

4. TikTok/Reel #2 (the data angle: "only about half of home-services calls reach a person — the rest go to a competitor who picks up. Reel on missed calls")

5. Facebook Group comment (wait for someone to complain about missed calls, reply with the insight)

6. Newsletter paragraph (weekly roundup: "This week's win...")

7. Cold email P.S. line ("P.S. We just helped a [city] HVAC company catch 11 after-hours calls in one week")

The AI Content Generator prompt above does steps 2-6 automatically. You add step 7 to your Smartlead sequences manually.

Short-Form Video: The 3 Formats That Work

Format 1: The Live Call Demo (highest conversion)

Record yourself calling your AI agent on speakerphone. Show the phone screen. Let viewers hear the AI answer, ask questions, and book an appointment. End: "This runs 24/7 for $500/month. Link in bio."

Format 2: The Missed Call Exposé

"I called 10 [plumbing] companies in [city] at 5:30pm. 7 went to voicemail. If you're one of them..." Show the call log on screen. This is Missed Call Audit content that doubles as marketing.

Format 3: The Before/After

Split screen: left side "Before: missed call, voicemail, dead lead." Right side: "After: AI answers, books appointment, sends confirmation text." Works as a Reel or a LinkedIn carousel.

The Content Compound Effect

Content doesn't replace outbound — it multiplies it. When a cold prospect gets your email, they Google you. If they find LinkedIn posts with real results, TikToks of the AI in action, and a newsletter with client testimonials, you've already built trust before the demo. The agencies charging $1,500/mo+ for AI voice agents are the ones that look credible online. 90 minutes a week for 3 months builds that credibility permanently.

Client Onboarding SOP (Step-by-Step)

When a client signs, follow this exact process. Target: client fully live in 48-72 hours. The faster they go live, the faster they see ROI, the less likely they churn.

Send Stripe invoice for setup fee (50% upfront, 50% on go-live — or 100% upfront for bundle discount)

Send welcome email with what to expect + timeline (use template from Scripts section)

Add client to your Supabase tracker: name, plan, start date, phone number, key contacts

Send this form as a Google Form, Tally, or plain email. You cannot build the agent without this info. Don’t schedule the build until you have it back.

If the client doesn’t return it within 48 hours, Paola follows up by text: “Hey [NAME], just need that intake form back so we can start your build! Anything I can help with?”

Hours 1-4: Discovery & Setup (Mike)

Discovery call (15 min): What services do you offer? What's your service area? Business hours? How do you want appointments booked? What info do you need from callers? Emergency protocol?

Get assets: Business name, address, logo, service menu, pricing (if they share it), scheduling preferences

Buy Twilio phone number in their area code ($1/mo). Configure call forwarding as backup.

Build the AI agent script in Vapi customized to their business. Use your template as the base — swap business name, services, hours, booking flow.

Connect to n8n: Call received → log to Supabase → send SMS confirmation to caller → notify client via SMS/email → create calendar event

Set up call forwarding or number porting (see Phone Setup section)

Hours 4-8: Testing & Polish (Both)

Internal test calls (5-10): Paola calls as different customer types — emergency, price shopper, appointment booker, Spanish speaker (if bilingual plan). Mike monitors.

Verify: caller info captured correctly? SMS sent? Notification to client works? Appointment booked?

Fix any edge cases: "What if they ask for a quote?" "What if they're an existing customer?" "What about after-hours emergencies?"

Record 2-3 sample calls to share with the client

Set up monitoring alerts: if agent doesn't answer within 3 rings → alert to Mike

Hours 8-24: Client Approval & Go-Live

Client demo call (15 min): "Here's your agent. Call this number and try it yourself." Let them call in and experience it as a customer would.

Walk them through the notification they'll receive when a call comes in

Show them the dashboard/report they'll get monthly

Get verbal approval: "Are you happy with how it sounds? Ready to go live?"

Flip the switch: Activate call forwarding from their existing number → your AI number. Or if porting, submit the port request.

Send "You're Live!" email with: the number, what to expect, how to reach you for questions

Days 2-7: Monitoring & Optimization

Monitor every call for the first 72 hours. Listen to recordings. Fix anything that sounds wrong.

Day 3: Quick check-in text to client: "How's the agent doing? Any calls you want us to adjust?"

Day 7: First mini-report: "Your agent answered X calls this week. Y appointments booked. Z leads captured."

Adjust scripts based on actual call patterns (most agents need 2-3 tweaks in week 1)

Day 30: First Monthly Review

Send full monthly report (automated via n8n): total calls, appointments booked, leads captured, estimated revenue saved

Schedule 15-min check-in call: "How's it going? Anything we should adjust?"

Ask for a Google review (they're happy, this is the moment)

Ask for referrals: "Know any other contractors who miss calls?"

Pitch add-ons if appropriate: bilingual, reputation management, follow-up sequences

Time Investment Per Client

First client: 6-8 hours total (you're learning). Clients 2-5: 4-5 hours (template exists). Clients 6+: 2-3 hours (everything is templated, you just swap details). Monthly maintenance: 1-2 hours/client (mostly automated reports + quarterly check-ins).

Plain English: Who Does What During Onboarding

Paola's onboarding tasks (no tech skills needed):

  • • Send the contract and invoice via PandaDoc/Stripe (click a button, fill in client name and amount)
  • • Send the welcome email (copy template, swap client name)
  • • Run the 15-min discovery call: ask what services they offer, their hours, their service area
  • • Make 5-10 test calls to the AI agent pretending to be different customers
  • • Run the client demo call: walk them through what their customers will experience
  • • Send the "You're Live!" email and schedule the Day 30 check-in

Mike's onboarding tasks (technical):

  • • Buy the Twilio phone number and set up forwarding
  • • Build the AI agent script in Vapi (copy template, swap business details)
  • • Connect the n8n workflows (copy template, change phone number + client info)
  • • Fix any issues found during Paola's test calls
  • • Set up monitoring alerts

Total time: Paola ~2 hours, Mike ~3 hours. You can onboard a client in a single afternoon if you work together during the 3-5pm CET window.

The Offer & Objection System (Frameworks, Not Just Scripts)

Scripts tell you what to say when the conversation goes as planned. Frameworks tell you what to do when it doesn't — which is most of the time. These five are the ones elite sales programs actually teach. Learn them once and every script in this course becomes something you can improvise from instead of read from.

1. The Value Equation: Why They Say Yes

Alex Hormozi's framing, and still the dominant offer scaffold: Value = (Dream Outcome × Perceived Likelihood of Achievement) ÷ (Time Delay × Effort & Sacrifice). Dream Outcome is set by the market — every competitor promises the same thing, and all you can do is say it in their words. Your three real levers are Perceived Likelihood (proof), Time Delay, and Effort & Sacrifice. Competitors compete on the promise; you win on the other three.

LeverWhat the contractor is thinkingHow you move it
Dream Outcome“I want to stop losing jobs to the guy who picks up.”Say it in their words, not yours. Never “AI-powered omnichannel.”
Perceived Likelihood“Sounds good, but will it work for MY shop?”Recording of a same-trade call + a conditional guarantee + a named local reference. This is where you win or lose.
Time Delay“How long until this actually does something?”Live in 48 hours. Book a first-win call within 2 days. Speed is your biggest edge over enterprise vendors with 6-week onboardings.
Effort & Sacrifice“I don't have time to learn another system.”“You forward your phone. That's your entire job.” Done-for-you is the product. Every extra step you remove raises the price you can charge.

The one-sentence test. Before any call, finish this out loud: “You stop losing $____ a month in missed calls, you're live in 48 hours, and all you do is forward your phone.” If you can't fill the blank with a number from their business, you're not ready to pitch — go run the audit first.

2. The Guarantee Matrix: Pick the Right Risk Reversal

“Money-back guarantee” is the weakest thing you can offer, because it's what everyone says. Hormozi's taxonomy names four distinct types, and the right one depends on how much proof you have:

Unconditional

“30 days, full refund, no questions.” Strongest converter, highest abuse risk. Functions as a free trial.

Use when: you're new and need the first 3 clients badly. Cap it at your setup fee, not the whole engagement.

Conditional YOUR DEFAULT

“If the AI doesn't book you at least [N] jobs in 30 days, the next month is free — provided your phone is forwarded and you answer transfers during business hours.”

Why it wins twice: the conditions ARE the onboarding checklist. It converts skeptics and forces the client behaviour that makes the service work.

Anti-Guarantee

“All sales final — because I'm turning down anyone who isn't serious about answering their phone.”

Use when: you have a waitlist and want to filter tire-kickers. Powerful, but only credible with proof behind it.

Implied Performance

“Lower base + $25 per booked job — if it doesn't book, I don't get paid.”

Use when: the client is price-anxious and you control the calendar integration so booking is provable.

Never guarantee revenue, only activity you control. Guarantee booked appointments, never “$X in new business” — you don't control their pricing, their techs, or whether they show up. And write the conditions into the contract in plain English; a guarantee argued over email costs more than the refund.

3. The Missed-Revenue Worksheet (run this live, on every call)

The single highest-converting five minutes in the whole sale. Do the arithmetic with them, on their numbers, writing as you go. A number they helped calculate is a number they believe.

THE FIVE QUESTIONS (ask in this order, write the answers down) 1. "Roughly how many calls come in a week?" → A = ______ 2. "Honestly, what portion get missed — after hours, on a job, lunch, second calls while you're talking?" → B = ______% (If they say "we get them all," ask permission to test it live. You will win.) 3. "When you DO reach someone, how often does it become a job?" → C = ______% (Home-services average is ~46% — Invoca, 2026 — but use THEIR number.) 4. "What's your average ticket on a job like that?" → D = $______ 5. "So let's just multiply it out..." A × 4.3 weeks × (B÷100) × (C÷100) × D = $__________ per month AT RISK WORKED EXAMPLE: 40 calls/wk × 4.3 = 172 calls/mo. 30% missed = 52 missed calls. × 46% close rate = 24 lost jobs. × $450 average ticket = $10,700/mo at risk. 6. Now HALVE it out loud, before they do: "Even if we only recover half of that, it's $5,350 a month against my $1,000. Some of those callers leave a voicemail or call back — I'm not counting on catching every one." Discounting your own number is the single most credibility-building move available on a sales call. THEN, AND ONLY THEN: "My service is $[price]. The gap between those two numbers is the entire conversation. Do you want me to close it, or do you want to keep testing whether it closes itself?" RULES: - Never inflate. If the honest number is small, say so: "That's $1,800/month — worth fixing, but let's start you on the Starter tier, not the bundle." Under-selling on the first call is how you get a client for five years. - Screenshot the math and paste it into the follow-up email the same day.

Get their real data if you can. Ask them to pull the last 30 days from their phone system, CallRail, or FSM while you're on the call. Real call logs beat estimates — and the moment you're looking at their data together, you've stopped being a vendor and started being their consultant.

4. SPICED: The Discovery Spine

Use one discovery framework everywhere so both of you run the same call. SPICED (Winning by Design) is the cleanest spine for short SMB calls, and its fourth letter is the one most agencies skip — and the one that actually determines whether the deal closes this month or “after the season.”

LetterAsk this
S — Situation“Who answers the phone right now — you, an office manager, an answering service? What happens after 5pm and on Sundays?”
P — Pain“When was the last time you found out about a job you lost because nobody picked up? Tell me what happened.”
I — ImpactThe worksheet above. Quantify it in their dollars, out loud, together.
C — Critical Event“What's coming that makes this urgent?” For trades it's always seasonal: first heat wave, first freeze, storm season, a tech quitting, the office manager going on leave. No critical event = no deal this month. Find it or create one: “July is your peak — do you want this running before it hits, or after?”
D — Decision“If this makes sense, is it just you deciding, or does anyone else weigh in? What would need to be true to start Monday?”

Full question bank in the Discovery Framework lesson — map each existing question to its SPICED letter and you'll spot which letter you habitually skip. It's almost always Critical Event.

5. LAER: The Objection Sequence

Carew International’s LAER sequence — and the fix for the most common beginner mistake: answering an objection the second you hear it. Slow down by one step and your close rate climbs.

L — Listen

Let them finish completely. Then wait two more seconds. The real objection usually arrives in the second sentence, not the first.

A — Acknowledge

Label it, don't argue with it (Chris Voss's tactical empathy): “It sounds like you've been burned by an answering service before.” Then stop talking.

E — Explore

“When you say it's too expensive — too expensive versus what?” Nine times in ten, “price” is really risk, timing, or a bad past experience.

R — Respond

Only now. Answer the real objection you uncovered in Explore — which is usually not the one they opened with.

The stall-breaker (Sandler negative reverse + alternative choice) — for “let me think about it”:

“That's completely fair. Can I ask — is it that this isn't a priority right now, or that you're not convinced it'll work for a shop like yours? Because if it's the second one, that's on me and I can fix it in five minutes. If it's the first, I'll get out of your hair.”

Two moves in one: first you head toward no (the negative reverse) to take the pressure off, then you offer two exits — one of which blames you, not them. Giving someone permission to say no is what makes them tell the truth. Then handle the real objection with LAER.

Word-for-word answers to the eight objections you'll actually hear are in the Objection Killers cheat sheet. Use LAER to decide when to deploy them — never at the first sentence.

Practice drill (do this before your first real demo): paste this into Claude — “Act as a skeptical 55-year-old HVAC owner with 4 trucks who's been pitched by three AI companies this month and thinks it'll sound robotic to his customers. I'm selling an AI receptionist. Push back hard, interrupt me, and don't be won over easily. Start the call.” Run it ten times. It costs pennies and it's the cheapest reps you will ever get.

Discovery Call Framework: Qualify, Diagnose, Close

A structured 17-minute call that qualifies the prospect, diagnoses their pain, and closes the trial. Follow this framework every time — consistency beats improvisation.

Pre-Call Preparation Checklist

Do these 5 minutes before every discovery call. Walking in prepared earns instant credibility.

Call their business number first. Does it go to voicemail? How many rings? What does the voicemail say? Screenshot the result — you will use this on the call.

Check their Google reviews. How many? What’s the rating? Any complaints about “couldn’t reach anyone” or “nobody called back”? Screenshot these.

Look at their Google Business Profile. Are their hours listed? Do they have a website? What services do they advertise?

Check their website (if any). Do they have a contact form? Live chat? Or just a phone number? Note how they currently capture leads.

Prepare your demo number. Make sure your demo agent is live and working. Test-call it once before the meeting.

The 5-Phase Call Structure (17 Minutes)

Phase 1: Rapport & Intro (2 min)

Thank them for their time. Briefly explain what you do in one sentence. Set the agenda: “I’d love to ask a few questions about your business, then show you something cool, and we’ll see if it makes sense. Sound good?”

Key: Be warm, be human, don’t pitch yet. Contractors respect people who get to the point without being pushy.

Phase 2: Problem Diagnosis (8 min)

This is where you earn the right to sell. Ask these questions and listen. Take notes. Their answers become your pitch.

“How many calls does your business get per day, roughly?”

“How many of those go to voicemail or get missed?”

“What happens with after-hours calls right now?”

“What’s your average job value?”

“Have you lost a job recently because of a missed call?”

“Do you have a receptionist or office manager answering phones?”

“What happens on weekends — do calls go anywhere?”

“If a customer calls and nobody answers, what do they do?”

Pro tip: When they say “yeah we miss a lot of calls,” ask “how many per week, would you guess?” Get a number. You need their numbers for Phase 3.

Phase 3: Value Presentation (3 min)

Mirror their own numbers back to them. This is not a generic pitch — it’s their specific situation.

Example: “So you said you miss about 5 calls a week, and your average job is $3,000. That’s potentially $15,000 a week walking to your competitors. Even if only 20% of those would have booked, that’s $3,000/week or $12,000/month in lost revenue. Our service costs $1,000/month. The math kind of speaks for itself.”

Key: Use THEIR numbers, not yours. Let the ROI math do the selling.

Phase 4: Live Demo (2 min)

“Let me show you what this actually sounds like. I’m going to call our demo number right now — pretend you’re a homeowner with a broken AC.”

Call the demo number on speaker. Let the AI handle it. This is always the “wow” moment. Don’t talk over it — let them hear it work.

After the call: “Imagine that answering every call to your business, 24/7, and texting you the details instantly.”

Phase 5: Trial Close (2 min)

“Based on what you’re telling me, this could save you $[AMOUNT] a month in missed jobs. Want us to set this up for you this week?”

If yes: “Great, I’ll send you a short intake form today and we’ll have your agent live in 48 hours.” → Send the proposal template within 1 hour.

If not sure: “Totally fair. How about a free 1-week trial? We set it up, you see the results, and decide after that. No commitment.”

If no: “No problem at all. Mind if I follow up in a month? Things might change during busy season.”

Red Flags: When to Walk Away

Not every prospect is a good fit. Walking away from bad clients saves you months of headaches. Watch for these:

Budget under $300/mo: They can’t afford the service and will churn fast. Politely redirect to a DIY solution.

Wants to “think about it” for more than 2 weeks: They’re not in pain. Follow up once, then move on.

Wants you to guarantee a specific number of calls: You can’t control how many people call their business. You guarantee every call gets answered.

Wants custom development for free: “Can you also build us a website and CRM?” Scope creep kills profitability. Offer it as a paid add-on.

Abusive or disrespectful: Trust your gut. If they’re rude on the sales call, they’ll be worse as a client.

Qualification Criteria (BANT)

Score every prospect against these four criteria. If they hit 3 of 4, they’re a strong lead. Less than 2 — deprioritize.

B — Budget

$500+/month budget. They understand this is a business expense, not a gadget purchase.

A — Authority

Owner or decision-maker on the call. Not an office manager who “needs to check with the boss.”

N — Need

Actually missing calls — verified by your audit or their own admission. If they have a full-time receptionist and never miss calls, they don’t need you (yet).

T — Timeline

Ready to start within 30 days. If they say “maybe next quarter,” put them in a nurture sequence and move on.

Discovery Questions (Copy-Paste List)

DISCOVERY CALL QUESTIONS — Ask in order 1. Tell me about your business — how long have you been operating? 2. How many calls does your business get per day, roughly? 3. How many of those go to voicemail or get missed? 4. What happens with after-hours calls right now? 5. Do you have someone answering phones, or is it just you? 6. What's your average job value? 7. Have you lost a job recently because of a missed call? 8. What happens on weekends — do calls go anywhere? 9. If a customer calls and nobody answers, what do they usually do? 10. How do you currently follow up with leads who call in? 11. Do you get many calls in Spanish? (if relevant to area) 12. Have you tried any answering services or AI tools before? 13. What would it be worth to you to never miss another call? 14. If we could set this up for you this week, would you want to try it?

Word-for-Word Demo Call Script

DISCOVERY CALL — DEMO TRANSITION SCRIPT [After diagnosis questions] "Based on what you're telling me, it sounds like you're missing about [X] calls a week. At $[AVG JOB] per job, that could be $[WEEKLY LOSS] a week in lost revenue. Let me show you exactly what we do about that. I'm going to call our demo line right now — it's set up for an HVAC company similar to yours. Pretend you're a homeowner whose AC just broke. [Dial demo number on speaker] [Let AI handle the call — don't interrupt] [After call ends] That's what your customers would hear instead of voicemail. Every call gets answered in under a second, the caller's info gets texted to you immediately, and if they want an appointment, it books automatically. The setup takes us about 48 hours. We customize everything — your business name, your services, your hours, your service area. And it's month-to-month, so if you don't love it after 30 days, you cancel with no obligation. Want us to set this up for you this week?"

After Every Discovery Call

Log the call in your CRM immediately: prospect name, phone, BANT score (1-4), key pain points mentioned, next step (proposal sent / trial starting / follow-up date / not a fit). This takes 2 minutes and prevents leads from falling through the cracks.

Technology Delivery: Exactly What Gets Built

For each service tier, here's precisely what you deploy, what the client sees, and what runs in the background.

The AI Phone Agent (Core Product)

What the Client Sees:

A phone number in their area code that answers every call 24/7

SMS notifications for every new lead within 30 seconds of the call

A weekly/monthly email report with call stats and recordings

A link to listen to any call recording on demand

What You Build (Behind the Scenes):

Vapi AI Agent: Custom system prompt with business info, service menu, scheduling rules, FAQ answers, escalation triggers. Voice: "Rachel" or "Josh" (ElevenLabs via Vapi). Latency: <800ms first response.

Twilio Number: Local area code, call forwarding configured, SMS enabled, A2P 10DLC registered.

n8n Workflow — Call Handler: Vapi webhook → parse call data → save to Supabase → send SMS to client → send SMS confirmation to caller → create Google Calendar event (if appointment booked) → log everything.

n8n Workflow — Escalation: If caller says "emergency" or "urgent" → immediately call/text the client's personal phone. If no answer in 60 seconds → try backup number.

n8n Workflow — Reporting: Weekly cron → query Supabase for call stats → generate summary → email to client. Monthly: detailed PDF with charts.

Monitoring: n8n health-check every 5 minutes. If Vapi doesn't respond → alert Mike → auto-activate fallback (forward to client's phone).

Lead Follow-Up Automation

What the Client Sees:

Every missed lead gets automatic follow-up texts/emails within minutes

Appointment reminders sent automatically (reduces no-shows by 40-60%)

Post-job review requests sent automatically

What You Build:

n8n Workflow — Missed Lead Sequence: If call ends without appointment → wait 5 min → SMS: "Hi [name], thanks for calling [Business]. We'd love to help — want to book a time?" → wait 24hr → Email follow-up → wait 48hr → Final SMS.

n8n Workflow — Appointment Reminder: 24hr before → SMS reminder. 2hr before → final reminder. If they reply "cancel" → notify client + offer reschedule.

n8n Workflow — Review Request: After job completion (client marks done in a simple Google Form or text trigger) → wait 2hr → SMS: "How was [Business]? If you had a great experience, we'd love a review: [Google review link]"

n8n Workflow — Database Reactivation: Monthly: query leads who called 30+ days ago but never booked → SMS: "Hi [name], we noticed you reached out last month. Still need help with [service]? We have availability this week."

The Margin Math

Technical Implementation: Database & Workflows

Copy-paste SQL schema, automated report template, and a plain-English walkthrough of how the whole system connects.

Supabase Database Schema (Copy-Paste SQL)

Run this SQL in your Supabase SQL Editor on Day 2. This creates every table you need for the first 20 clients.

-- ===== AGENCY CRM SCHEMA ===== -- Run this in Supabase SQL Editor (supabase.com → your project → SQL Editor) -- Your clients (the businesses you serve) CREATE TABLE clients ( id UUID DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY, business_name TEXT NOT NULL, owner_name TEXT NOT NULL, owner_email TEXT, owner_phone TEXT NOT NULL, address TEXT, city TEXT, state TEXT, trade TEXT DEFAULT 'HVAC', -- HVAC, Plumbing, Electrical, Roofing plan TEXT DEFAULT 'bundle', -- starter, bundle, premium monthly_rate INTEGER DEFAULT 1000, setup_fee INTEGER DEFAULT 2500, twilio_number TEXT, vapi_agent_id TEXT, status TEXT DEFAULT 'onboarding', -- onboarding, active, paused, churned go_live_date DATE, notes TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() ); -- Calls handled by AI agents CREATE TABLE calls ( id UUID DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY, client_id UUID REFERENCES clients(id), caller_name TEXT, caller_phone TEXT, caller_address TEXT, service_needed TEXT, urgency TEXT DEFAULT 'normal', -- normal, urgent, emergency call_duration_seconds INTEGER, outcome TEXT, -- appointment_booked, message_taken, transferred, escalated appointment_date TIMESTAMPTZ, recording_url TEXT, vapi_call_id TEXT, language TEXT DEFAULT 'en', -- en, es created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() ); -- Leads captured (may or may not become appointments) CREATE TABLE leads ( id UUID DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY, client_id UUID REFERENCES clients(id), call_id UUID REFERENCES calls(id), name TEXT NOT NULL, phone TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, service_requested TEXT, status TEXT DEFAULT 'new', -- new, contacted, booked, completed, lost follow_up_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0, next_follow_up TIMESTAMPTZ, notes TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() ); -- YOUR agency prospects (people you're selling to) CREATE TABLE prospects ( id UUID DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY, business_name TEXT NOT NULL, owner_name TEXT, email TEXT, phone TEXT, trade TEXT, city TEXT, state TEXT, source TEXT, -- cold_email, cold_call, linkedin, referral, inbound stage TEXT DEFAULT 'cold', -- cold, engaged, demo_booked, demo_done, proposal, closed, lost lead_score INTEGER DEFAULT 0, notes TEXT, assigned_to TEXT DEFAULT 'paola', -- mike or paola last_contact TIMESTAMPTZ, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() ); -- Monthly metrics per client (for reporting) CREATE TABLE monthly_reports ( id UUID DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY, client_id UUID REFERENCES clients(id), month DATE NOT NULL, -- first of the month total_calls INTEGER DEFAULT 0, appointments_booked INTEGER DEFAULT 0, leads_captured INTEGER DEFAULT 0, avg_call_duration INTEGER DEFAULT 0, estimated_revenue_saved DECIMAL(10,2) DEFAULT 0, sent_at TIMESTAMPTZ, opened BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE ); -- Enable Row Level Security ALTER TABLE clients ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ALTER TABLE calls ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ALTER TABLE leads ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ALTER TABLE prospects ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ALTER TABLE monthly_reports ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; -- Create indexes for common queries CREATE INDEX idx_calls_client ON calls(client_id, created_at DESC); CREATE INDEX idx_leads_client ON leads(client_id, status); CREATE INDEX idx_prospects_stage ON prospects(stage, assigned_to); CREATE INDEX idx_reports_client ON monthly_reports(client_id, month DESC);

After Running the SQL

Go to Supabase → Settings → API to get your project URL and anon key. You’ll need these in n8n to connect your workflows. The free tier gives you 500MB storage and 50,000 rows — enough for 20+ clients running for months.

Client Monthly Report Template

This is what your automated n8n report email looks like. Build this as an HTML email template. The data comes from your Supabase queries.

Subject: [BUSINESS NAME] AI Agent Report — [MONTH YEAR] Hi [OWNER NAME], Here's your monthly AI agent performance report: 📞 CALL SUMMARY Total calls handled: [NUMBER] Appointments booked: [NUMBER] Messages taken: [NUMBER] Emergency escalations: [NUMBER] Average call duration: [X] min [Y] sec Busiest day: [DAY] ([NUMBER] calls) Busiest hour: [TIME] — [TIME] 💰 ESTIMATED VALUE Calls that would have gone to voicemail: [NUMBER] Estimated revenue captured: $[AMOUNT] (Based on [X]% booking rate × $[AVG JOB] avg job value) 📊 TRENDS vs. last month: [+/-X%] calls, [+/-X%] bookings Top service requested: [SERVICE] Spanish-language calls: [NUMBER] ([X]%) ⭐ REVIEW REQUESTS SENT: [NUMBER] New Google reviews received: [NUMBER] Current rating: [X.X] ★ ([TOTAL] reviews) 🔧 OPTIMIZATIONS MADE THIS MONTH - [Adjustment 1] - [Adjustment 2] Questions? Reply to this email or text me at [YOUR NUMBER]. [YOUR NAME] [YOUR AGENCY]

Automate This With n8n

Create a workflow: Cron trigger (1st of each month, 9am ET) → Supabase query (aggregate last month’s data per client) → HTML template node (fill in the data) → Resend email node (send to client). Total build time: ~2 hours. After that, it runs forever with zero effort.

Plain English: How a Client's Call Actually Flows

Here's what happens when someone calls your client's business, start to finish:

1. Phone rings → The client's phone forwards to your Twilio number (because they're on a job and can't answer).

2. AI picks up → Vapi answers in under 1 second. Sounds like a real receptionist: "Hi, thanks for calling [Business]. How can I help you today?"

3. Conversation happens → The caller says "My AC broke" and the AI asks smart questions: what's the issue, your address, when works for a technician. The Claude/OpenAI brain behind Vapi understands the caller and responds naturally.

4. Appointment booked → The AI checks available times and books the caller into the next open slot.

5. Instant notifications → n8n fires automatically: saves the caller's info to Supabase, texts the caller a confirmation ("Your appointment is confirmed for Tuesday at 2pm"), and texts/emails the business owner ("New appointment booked: John Smith, broken AC, Tuesday 2pm").

6. Nobody did anything manually. The entire flow — answer, converse, book, confirm, notify — happened in 2-3 minutes with zero human involvement. That's what you're selling.

What Mike tells prospects: "Imagine a really smart receptionist who never takes a break, answers in 1 second, always captures the right info, and sends you a text the moment a new job is booked. That's what we set up for you."

The Paste-Ready Build Kit

Everything above explains how the pieces fit. This lesson is the pieces themselves — the exact JSON that turns a chatbot that talks about appointments into an agent that actually books them. Copy these three artifacts in order and a real phone number books a real slot on a real calendar.

The difference between a demo and a product is function calling. Without tools, your agent can only promise “someone will call you back” — which is exactly the voicemail experience the client is paying you to eliminate. The book_appointment schema below is the single most important 30 lines in this entire course.

"type": "string", "description": "One sentence in the caller's own words" }, "slot_start": { "type": "string", "description": "ISO 8601 datetime returned by check_availability" }, "is_existing_customer": { "type": "boolean" } }, "required": ["customer_name", "phone", "address", "service_type", "slot_start"] } }, "server": { "url": "https://n8n.yourdomain.com/webhook/book-appointment" } }, { "type": "transferCall", "destinations": [ { "type": "number", "number": "{{OWNER_MOBILE_E164}}", "message": "This sounds urgent — let me get you to someone right now, please hold." } ] } ] }, "voice": { "provider": "cartesia", "voiceId": "{{CARTESIA_VOICE_ID}}", "model": "sonic-3.5" }, "transcriber": { "provider": "deepgram", "model": "flux-general-multi" }, "analysisPlan": { "summaryPlan": { "messages": [ { "role": "system", "content": "Summarize in 2 sentences: what the caller wanted and what was agreed." }, { "role": "user", "content": "Transcript:\n\n{{transcript}}" } ] }, "structuredDataPlan": { "schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "outcome": { "type": "string", "enum": ["booked", "message_taken", "transferred", "price_shopper", "wrong_number", "spam"] }, "service_type": { "type": "string" }, "urgency": { "type": "string", "enum": ["emergency", "same_week", "flexible"] }, "estimated_job_value": { "type": "number" } } } } }, "server": { "url": "https://n8n.yourdomain.com/webhook/vapi-events", "timeoutSeconds": 20 }, "serverMessages": ["end-of-call-report", "status-update", "tool-calls"], "artifactPlan": { "recordingEnabled": true }, "endCallPhrases": ["goodbye", "have a good one", "bye now"] }

Why these specific settings: temperature 0.4 keeps the agent from improvising prices. maxDurationSeconds 420 caps a runaway call at about $0.55 of spend. structuredDataSchema is what fills your client dashboard and monthly report automatically — without it you're reading transcripts by hand at 20 clients. And the firstMessage contains both required disclosures (AI identity + recording) in one natural sentence, which is your entire compliance posture in most states.

Artifact 2: The Webhook Contract

This is what trips up every first build: Vapi calls your n8n webhook and waits for a specific response shape. Return anything else and the agent goes silent mid-call. Your n8n “Respond to Webhook” node must return exactly this:

// What Vapi SENDS to your webhook on a tool call: { "message": { "type": "tool-calls", "toolCallList": [ { "id": "call_abc123", "name": "book_appointment", "arguments": { "customer_name": "Jane Doe", "phone": "+19195551234" } } ], "call": { "id": "...", "customer": { "number": "+1919..." } } } } // What your n8n workflow MUST return (Respond to Webhook node, JSON): { "results": [ { "toolCallId": "call_abc123", "result": "Booked for Tuesday July 21 between 9 and 11 AM. Confirmation text sent." } ] } // RULES THAT SAVE YOU HOURS: // 1. toolCallId must be echoed back EXACTLY or Vapi ignores the response. // 2. "result" is a STRING the AI reads aloud — write it like a human sentence, // not JSON. The caller hears this. // 3. Respond in under 3 seconds. Longer and the caller hears dead air. // Put slow work (CRM sync, emails) AFTER the respond node, not before. // 4. On failure, still return a result string: // "I couldn't confirm that slot — let me take a message instead." // Never return an error object; the agent will freeze. // 5. toolCallList entries are FLAT. Read message.toolCallList[0].name and // message.toolCallList[0].arguments.customer_name — there is no .function // wrapper. Getting this wrong is the #1 reason a first build silently fails.

Lock the webhook down before it goes live. A public n8n webhook that books appointments is a public API for anyone who finds the URL. Vapi removed the inline server.secret field, so create a Custom Credential instead: Dashboard → Settings → Integrations → Server Configuration → Add Custom Credential → Bearer Token, header name x-vapi-secret, Bearer prefix OFF, then paste a long random token. Attach it to the assistant, and make your first n8n node reject any request whose x-vapi-secret header doesn’t match. One token per client, stored in that client’s credential record.

Artifact 3: The 10-Call Pre-Flight Test

Never hand a client a number you haven’t attacked. Run all ten from your own phone and write the result next to each. Any fail = fix before go-live, no exceptions.

1. Happy path: “My AC stopped working” → books a real slot, you receive the confirmation SMS

2. Emergency: “I smell gas” → says call 911 first, then transfers immediately

3. Price shopper: “How much for a new furnace?” → gives the range, does NOT invent a quote

4. Out of area: ZIP 90 minutes away → politely declines, takes a message

5. Existing customer: “I need to reschedule Thursday” → handles or transfers cleanly

6. Spanish speaker: switches language and still books

7. Interruption: talk over the agent mid-sentence → it stops and listens

8. Noise: call from a car with windows down / jobsite noise → still transcribes

9. Angry caller: “Third time I’ve called!” → de-escalates, escalates to human

10. Silence: say nothing for 20 seconds → ends gracefully, no infinite loop

Keep the recordings. Save every pre-flight call to a folder named after the client. Test #1 becomes the demo clip you send the next prospect in that trade, and the full set is your proof if a client ever says “it never worked properly.” Re-run all ten after any prompt change — a one-word edit can break booking in a way you won’t notice for a week.

Phone Setup & SMS Compliance

The #1 question clients ask: "What happens to my phone number?" Here are the three options, when to use each, and the SMS compliance you must handle.

Option A: Call Forwarding (Recommended to Start)

How it works: Client keeps their existing number. They set up conditional call forwarding (on no-answer, busy, or all calls) to your Twilio AI number.

Pros: Zero risk for client. Done in 5 minutes. They keep their number. Easy to revert.

Cons: Slight delay (1-2 extra rings before forwarding). Some carriers charge for forwarding.

Setup steps:

  1. Buy a Twilio number in client's area code
  2. Configure Vapi to use that Twilio number as its inbound line
  3. Client activates forwarding: iPhone: Settings → Phone → Call Forwarding. Android: Phone app → Settings → Call Forwarding. Or dial *72 + [your Twilio number] on a landline.
  4. Test with a call — should ring to AI after client doesn't answer

Best for: Every new client. Start here. Switch to porting only if they want to fully hand over call management.

Option B: Full Number Porting

How it works: Client's existing business number is ported to Twilio. All calls go directly to your AI agent. You control everything.

Pros: No forwarding delay. Full control. Cleaner setup. Better call quality.

Cons: Takes 1-3 weeks to port. Client must authorize. If they leave you, they need to port back.

When to use: Month 2+ clients who are committed. Enterprise plans. Clients who want you managing everything.

Setup: Submit LOA (Letter of Authorization) through Twilio. Provide: business name, authorized contact, account number with current carrier, PIN if applicable.

Option C: New Number (Simplest)

How it works: You give the client a new number that's answered by AI. They advertise it as their "24/7 service line" alongside their existing number.

Pros: Instant setup. No risk. Client can test without changing anything.

Cons: Doesn't capture calls to their existing number. Requires them to promote a new number.

Best for: Free trials, demo phase, or as an "after-hours line" alongside their main number.

A2P 10DLC SMS Compliance (Mandatory)

If you send SMS to clients' customers (confirmations, follow-ups, review requests), you must register for A2P 10DLC. Without it, carriers will block your messages.

What it is: "Application-to-Person 10-Digit Long Code" — the US carrier registration system for business SMS.

What you register:

  • • Brand: Register Colibri Code LLC ($4 one-time for sole proprietor, $4-48 for standard)
  • • Campaign: Register each use case — e.g., "Appointment confirmations for home service clients" ($15/campaign)

Timeline: 2-4 weeks for approval. Start this on Day 1 — don't wait until you have a client.

Per-client: You can use one campaign for multiple clients if they're the same use case. Or register the client's own brand if they prefer.

Without registration: Messages get filtered/blocked. Deliverability drops to 20-40%. Fines possible.

Action: Register your Twilio brand + campaign in Week 1. It takes time to approve and you can't send SMS without it. Do NOT skip this.

Plain English: Phone Setup Explained

Call forwarding = the client keeps their phone number. They just set their phone to forward missed calls to your AI number. Like saying "if I don't answer, send the call here." Takes 5 minutes to set up. This is what you do for every new client.

Number porting = moving the client's actual phone number to Twilio so you control it directly. The calls go straight to AI — no forwarding delay. But it takes 1-3 weeks and the client has to sign paperwork. Only do this for committed long-term clients.

A2P 10DLC = the government and phone carriers require businesses to register before sending text messages. Without registration, your texts get blocked. It's like getting a license plate for your SMS. Register Colibri Code LLC once, and you can send texts for all clients.

What Paola needs to know: When you're onboarding a client, just tell them: "We'll set up a new number in your area code. You forward your missed calls to it — takes 5 minutes on your phone. Nothing else changes for you."

Twilio ConversationRelay — The Future of Voice AI on Twilio

Twilio announced three new Conversation products at SIGNAL 2026, now GA. These are Twilio-native alternatives to using Vapi as a middleware layer. You don’t need them yet, but understand what they are so you can evaluate them as your agency scales.

Conversation Orchestrator

Routes calls between AI agents and human agents in real time. Think of it as a traffic controller: AI handles routine calls, and the orchestrator seamlessly transfers to a human when the AI hits its limits — with full context carried over. Useful when your clients want “AI first, human backup” without callers noticing the handoff.

Conversation Memory

Persistent context across calls. If a customer called last Tuesday about a leaking faucet, the AI remembers that on the next call — no need to repeat themselves. Stores structured data (name, address, service history) and unstructured notes. Today you build this yourself with Supabase lookups in n8n; Conversation Memory does it natively inside Twilio.

Conversation Intelligence

Real-time call analytics: sentiment detection, keyword spotting, escalation triggers. If a caller says “I want to cancel” or sounds frustrated, Intelligence flags it and can auto-trigger a transfer or alert. Replaces manual call review and lets you build smarter reports for clients.

When to evaluate: If you outgrow Vapi’s telephony (10+ concurrent calls, need HIPAA compliance, or want to cut out the middleware layer), ConversationRelay + these products let you build Vapi-equivalent functionality directly on Twilio. The tradeoff: more engineering work, but lower per-minute costs at scale and full data sovereignty. Revisit at the 15-client mark.

A2P 10DLC Registration (CRITICAL for SMS)

Do NOT Skip This

If you send business SMS through Twilio without A2P 10DLC registration, your messages WILL be filtered/blocked by carriers. US carriers now require all business texting to be registered. Unregistered messages get near-0% delivery. This is the #1 technical mistake new agencies make.

Step-by-Step Registration (Do This in Week 1)

Step 1: Register your Brand — Twilio Console → Messaging → Trust Hub → A2P Brand Registration. Enter: Colibri Code LLC, your EIN (or SSN if no EIN), business address, website. Cost: one-time ~$4-4.50 fee (standard brand vetting runs ~$41.50 if required).

Step 2: Create a Campaign — Trust Hub → A2P Campaigns. Use case: “Mixed” or “Customer Care.” Describe: “Appointment confirmations, call follow-ups, and service notifications on behalf of home service businesses.”

Step 3: Link your Twilio numbers — Associate each phone number with the campaign. One campaign can cover all client numbers.

Step 4: Wait for approval — Takes 1-5 business days. You’ll get a “trust score” determining throughput. Small businesses typically get 15 msg/sec. Plenty.

Step 5: For each new client number — Add it to your existing campaign (2 minutes). No need to re-register.

NEW (effective June 30, 2026): Privacy Policy + Terms URLs are now mandatory

Every A2P campaign registration now requires two new fields: a public PrivacyPolicyUrl and a TermsAndConditionsUrl. Submissions without them get a hard 400 error — registration simply fails. The privacy policy must be a live HTTPS page that states SMS opt-in data isn’t shared/sold, names the messaging program, and specifies message frequency (T-Mobile rejects pages that don’t). Build one reusable compliant privacy + terms page now (host it on your agency site) and point every client campaign at it — or host a per-client page if they prefer their own brand. Existing campaigns keep running, but any edit triggers the new validator.

Carrier fee note (2026): T-Mobile added a ~$0.0025/message pass-through fee on Jan 19, 2026. At your volumes it’s trivial (~$1-2/client/mo), but build it into your minute/SMS cost model. Virginia SB 1339 also requires honoring SMS opt-outs for 10 years — keep STOP suppression permanent, never reuse a number across brands (that’s an “evasion” violation, up to $1,000/incident on T-Mobile).

SMS Compliance Checklist (Per Client)

Callers receive SMS only AFTER they’ve called in (implied consent for transactional messages)

Every first SMS includes business name and opt-out: “Reply STOP to unsubscribe”

Honor STOP replies immediately (Twilio handles this if you enable Advanced Opt-Out)

Only send transactional SMS (confirmations, follow-ups) — not marketing without explicit consent

Keep consent log (Supabase calls table = your proof the caller initiated contact)

The 2026 Pricing Playbook: How the Best Agencies Structure the Deal

Flat retainers still work, but in 2026 the agencies winning the skeptical contractors (and only ~50% of contractors trust AI per ServiceTitan’s 2026 survey) use three upgrades to the basic model. Each one either closes a hesitant buyer or expands revenue without a price-increase conversation.

1. Hybrid: Base Retainer + Per-Booking Bonus

Pure pay-per-booking is a trap — one runaway month of call volume wipes your margin. The 2026 standard is a hybrid: keep your retainer as the floor, then layer a small per-outcome fee on top.

Structure: “$1,000/mo includes the first 20 booked jobs, then $25 per booked appointment after that.”

Pricing rule: price each outcome at 2.5–3.5× your blended cost per booking so it survives your worst (90th-percentile) cost month.

Why it wins: aligns your pay with their revenue (kills the trust objection), and captures upside in HVAC summer / plumbing winter exactly when contractors are happiest to pay.

Guardrails (don’t skip): define “booked” precisely (calendar event created + caller confirmed, not just a transferred call), add a monthly spend cap, and give the client a live dashboard so billing is never an honor-system fight.

2. Tiered Minute Bundles + Overage (Expanding Recurring Revenue)

Turn a flat retainer into an account that grows on its own. Include a minute allowance, charge for overage, and offer seasonal tiers so clients self-upgrade instead of you renegotiating.

Example: “$1,200/mo includes 1,500 AI minutes; overage at $0.35/min; minutes roll over one month.” Your real all-in cost is ~$0.10–$0.13/min, so you hold 85–90% margin on the base and still profit on overage.

Seasonal tiers: Standard / Peak-Season / Multi-Location — a contractor heading into summer upgrades themselves.

The 2026 lesson: uncapped usage quietly destroys margins and causes bill-shock churn. Capped/guardrailed plans + a transparency dashboard are what sustain 70%+ margins. Always show the usage dashboard — bill-shock is the #1 cause of churn in usage models this year.

3. The 30-Day Booked-Jobs Guarantee (Risk Reversal)

The single fastest way to crack the contractor trust gap: “If your AI doesn’t book at least [X] jobs in the first 30 days, that month is free.” You already know your conversion math, so the risk to you is tiny — but to a skeptical contractor it removes the entire reason to say no. As one 2026 operator put it: “if you aren’t offering a guarantee, someone else will.”

The Moat: Integrate Into Their Field-Service Calendar

“Answering the phone” is now commoditized at $49/mo by a dozen apps. What contractors will pay $1,000+ for is booking the job directly into the software they already run — ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro, or Jobber. Make FSM-calendar integration the headline capability in every proposal: “Your AI doesn’t just take a message — it books the appointment straight into ServiceTitan, with the customer, address, and job type already filled in.” That integration is the line between you and the $49 tier, and it’s what makes you genuinely hard to rip out. (Connect via the platform’s API through n8n, or via MCP where available.)
