The Four Numbers That Decide Everything

Margin tables tell you the business is profitable. These four tell you whether it's fundable by its own cash flow — which is the only question that matters when you're two people with no investor. Calculate them today, then recalculate on the first of every month.

NumberHow to calculate itYour targetWhat it means when it's wrong
CAC
cost to acquire		All sales & marketing spend in a month ÷ clients signed that month. Loaded CAC adds your own hours at $50/hr — do this one too, it's the honest version.Hard CAC <$400
Loaded CAC <$1,200		If loaded CAC exceeds one year of gross profit, you're buying clients you can't afford. Fix the close rate before spending more.
LTV
lifetime value		Monthly gross profit × average months retained. At $1,000 ARPU, ~88% gross margin and 18 months: $880 × 18 = $15,840. Add the setup fee.LTV:CAC above 5:1 while small; never below 3:1Below 3:1 means growth destroys cash. Almost always a churn problem, not a pricing problem.
Payback
months to recover CAC		Loaded CAC ÷ monthly gross profit. With a setup fee collected up front, payback is often immediate — that's the whole reason this business is self-funding.Under 3 months
(ideally month 0)		Over 6 months and you must slow down hiring — every new client makes cash worse before better.
Break-even
clients to cover overhead		Fixed monthly overhead ÷ gross profit per client. At ~$400/mo overhead and $880 gross profit: 1 client covers the business.Known to the exact numberIf you can't state it from memory, you don't know when you can quit other work. Write it on the Command Center.

Why this business is unusually forgiving: the setup fee makes payback near-instant, and fixed overhead is so low that one client covers it. That combination means you can fund growth from client #1 without debt or investors — but it only holds if you keep charging setup fees. The moment you start waiving them to close deals, payback stretches, cash gets tight, and you start taking bad clients out of desperation. Discount the setup fee if you must; never delete it.

Client Retention & Churn Prevention

Acquiring a client costs 5-10x more than keeping one. Your #1 job after closing is making them never want to leave. Here's how.

The Sticky Stack (What Makes Them Stay)

1. Show ROI Every Month (Automated)

Your n8n workflow sends a monthly report: "Your AI agent answered 47 calls, booked 12 appointments, and captured 8 new leads. Estimated revenue saved: $36,000." When they see real numbers, cancellation becomes unthinkable.

2. Quick Response to Issues

Promise and deliver <2 hour response to any concern during US business hours. Most agencies take days. Your monitoring catches issues before clients even notice. This alone justifies the retainer.

3. Quarterly Optimization Calls

Every 90 days: "Let's review your agent's performance and update anything." Add new FAQ answers, adjust for seasonal changes (AC in summer, heating in winter), update appointment availability. This makes them feel actively managed.

4. Free Upgrades & New Features

"We just added a Spanish language option to all our agents — yours is updated for free." "We now send appointment reminders via SMS — activated on your account." Ship improvements proactively. Clients feel they're getting more value over time.

5. Make Switching Painful (In a Good Way)

The longer they're with you, the more data you hold: call recordings, lead history, appointment patterns, customer lists. If they leave, they lose all of that. This is natural lock-in, not a trick — it's genuine value accumulated over time.

Churn Warning Signs (Monitor These)

Target Metrics

Industry average churn for agencies: 5-10%/month. Your target: <3%/month (1 lost client per 33 per month). At 20 clients, that's losing roughly 1 client every ~2 months. If you close 2-3 new clients/month, you grow net 1-2 clients/month even with churn.

One more reason to obsess over this: retention isn't just MRR defense. If you ever sell the agency, each point of monthly churn you cut is worth roughly 15-25% more valuation — churn history is the first thing a buyer checks. See .

The First 30 Days: Lock In Every New Client (+ Save & Win-Back Scripts)

Churn isn't decided in month 6 — it's decided in the first 30 days. A client who sees a booked job in week one and hears from you five times in month one basically never leaves. A client who signs, goes live, and then hears silence until the invoice? They're already writing the cancellation email. This is the exact touchpoint calendar, with every message pre-written.

The metric that predicts retention: time-to-first-win. Target: the client sees their first AI-booked job within 48 hours of go-live, and hears about it from YOU before they notice it themselves. If 48 hours pass with no booking, manufacture the win — have a friend call the line and book a test appointment on speakerphone with the owner listening. They need to FEEL it work, fast.

The Save Call: Verbatim Script for "I Want to Cancel"

The concepts are in the retention lesson above; this is the word-for-word flow. Rules: get them on the PHONE (never negotiate a save over email), pull their numbers up before you dial, and never open with a discount — price is the last lever, not the first.

STEP 1 — OPEN (calm, zero defensiveness): "Thanks for telling me straight. Before we do anything, help me understand — what's driving it? I'd rather fix the real problem than talk you into anything." [Then SILENCE. Let them talk. Take notes. Don't interrupt.] STEP 2 — MIRROR IT BACK: "So if I'm hearing right: [their reason, in their words]. Did I get that right? Anything else?" [A second "anything else?" usually surfaces the REAL reason.] STEP 3 — MATCH THE FIX TO THE REASON: • "Not seeing results" → "Fair. Can I walk you through last month's log right now? [X] calls, [Z] booked — job #[example] alone was worth $[amount]. Which of these would've reached you on voicemail?" (Most saves happen right here — they genuinely don't know.) • "AI made mistakes" → "Show me the call — I'll pull the recording while we talk. If it misfired, that's a prompt fix and I'll ship it today, plus I'll credit that week. One bad call means tuning, the same way you'd tune a new tech." • "Money's tight / slow season" → "Then let's not cancel — let's PAUSE. I keep your number, your setup, everything frozen for up to 2 months at $0. Restarting later means a new setup fee and losing your tuned agent; pausing costs nothing." • "Too expensive" → "What if the plan matched output instead? [Per-booking option: lower base + $25/booked job.] Slow month, you pay less. Busy month, it's printing money for you anyway." STEP 4 — IF THEY STILL WANT OUT: "Understood — I'll make it easy, exactly like the contract says: 30 days, full data export, forwarding released. Two things first: [exit survey — 3 questions], and the door stays open. Your setup stays archived 90 days, so coming back is a switch-flip, not a rebuild." [A graceful exit is a marketing asset. Contractors talk to contractors.]

The save ladder, in order: Fix → Pause → Restructure → Graceful exit. A discount without a fix just delays the same cancellation 60 days at lower margin. And track every save reason in a spreadsheet — three saves with the same root cause means a delivery problem, not a client problem.

Win-Back: Churned Clients Are Your Warmest Pipeline

They already know you, trust you enough to have paid you, and their missed-call problem came BACK the day your agent went offline. Two emails, sent automatically (n8n task created at offboarding):

[DAY 30 AFTER CANCELLATION] Subject: How's the phone situation? [Name], no pitch — genuinely curious how the first month back has gone. Is [whoever took over / voicemail] keeping up with the calls? If anything's slipping through, your whole setup is still archived: your number, your tuned agent, your calendar hookup. Flipping it back on takes me about an hour, no setup fee for returning clients. Either way, hope business is booming. [Your name] [DAY 90 AFTER CANCELLATION — seasonal timing beats calendar timing: send before THEIR busy season if that's sooner] Subject: Before [season] hits [Name], [season] is about to do what it does to your phones. Since you left, the agent got better: [1-2 real improvements — "faster responses, books directly into Jobber now"]. Returning clients skip the setup fee, and I'll guarantee it: [N] booked jobs in 30 days or that month's free. Want me to switch it back on before the rush? [Your name]

Expect 10-20% of churned clients to come back within a year if you send these two emails and archive setups for easy resurrection — the highest-ROI "acquisition" channel you have, because CAC is one email and delivery is a restore, not a build. This is also why the graceful exit in the save script matters: nobody returns to an agency that got bitter on the way out.

Upsell Math

With 18 add-ons available, a typical client adopts 3-5 over their first year. If your average client adds $900/mo in expansions, average revenue per client jumps from $1,000 → $1,900. At 15 clients: $28,500/mo instead of $15,000. That extra $13,500/mo costs you under $600/mo to deliver. See the Master Profit Matrix below for exact numbers on every item.

Selling Sequence (Don't Pitch Everything at Once)

Month 1: Just deliver the core AI phone agent flawlessly. Month 2 (after they see results): Lead with Quote Follow-Up (I) — easiest "yes" because it recovers money they're actively losing. Month 3: Layer in Review Automation (C) + Satisfaction Surveys (O) — low cost, high perceived value. Month 4+: Bilingual (D), Maintenance Plans (J), Warranty Reminders (Q). Once trust is high: Google Ads (K), Blog/SEO (P), and Hiring Screener (L) — bigger commitments, stickier relationships. Each add-on makes the client harder to lose.

Churn Recovery: When a Client Wants to Cancel

Don’t panic. Most cancellation requests are negotiable. Here’s your save playbook:

Step 1: Ask Why (Within 2 Hours)

Call them immediately. “I got your message. Before we do anything, I want to understand what happened. What changed?” Listen. Don’t defend. Write down their exact words.

Step 2: Diagnose the Real Issue

“Too expensive” → Show ROI numbers. “You’re paying $700 and capturing $3,200 in additional jobs.” If needed, offer a temporary discount. “Not seeing results” → Pull their data. Often they ARE getting results but don’t realize it. Show them. “Going another direction” → Ask what direction. Match or beat it if you can. “Business is slow” → Offer to pause (not cancel) for 1 month. They keep their number and setup.

Step 3: Make a Save Offer

Options in order of preference: (1) Fix the issue + add a free feature for 30 days. (2) Reduce to a lower tier for 2 months. (3) Pause for 1 month at $0 (keeps them in your system). (4) If they still leave, be gracious. Ask for a referral. “I totally understand. If you know anyone who could use this, I’d really appreciate the introduction.”

White-Label & Partner Program (Month 6+)

Once your delivery is dialed in and you have capacity, other agencies and consultants can sell your service under their brand. You build and manage the tech; they own the client relationship. This is how you scale to 50+ clients without 50x the sales effort. The full economics of white-label as an income stream — including GHL SaaS Mode and wrapper platforms — are in .

Model A: Referral Partner

They send you leads, you close and deliver. They get a recurring commission.

Their role: Introduce you to contractors in their network.

Your role: Handle the entire sales call, build, and delivery.

Commission: 10–15% of monthly retainer, paid as long as the client stays. On a $1,000/mo client, they earn $100–$150/mo passively.

Best for: Marketing agencies, business coaches, trade association leaders, commercial real estate agents who know contractors.

Model B: White-Label Reseller

They sell AI phone agents under their brand. You build and manage everything behind the scenes.

Their role: Sell, bill the client, own the relationship.

Your role: Build, deploy, monitor, optimize, report. Invisible to the end client.

Pricing: Charge them wholesale ($400–$700/mo per client — start at the low end, raise as your delivery track record grows). They mark up to $800–$1,500 and keep the difference.

Best for: Digital marketing agencies, GHL agencies who want to add voice AI, IT MSPs serving SMBs.

White-Label Operational Requirements

Separate Twilio sub-accounts per reseller so their clients’ numbers and billing are isolated.

Branded monthly reports — swap your logo for theirs in the n8n report template. Takes 5 minutes per partner to set up.

SLA agreement: Commit to 99.5% uptime, 4-hour response on issues, 48-hour onboarding for new clients. Put it in writing.

Minimum commitment: Require 3+ clients within 90 days. One-off resellers aren’t worth the onboarding overhead.

Communication channel: Dedicated Slack channel per reseller partner. They tag you when they close a deal; you handle build and go-live.

When to Start This

Don’t white-label until you have 8+ direct clients and your delivery is under 4 hours per onboarding. White-label clients have someone else’s brand on the line — quality problems get amplified because the reseller loses trust in you. Nail direct delivery first, then scale through partners.

Vertical Money-Makers (Validated Mid-2026)

Four newer plays with real 2026 traction. Each is a service wrapper around a proven tool — you sell setup + operation, the tool does the heavy lifting:

🏠 Roofing Insurance-Supplement Ops

Storm-restoration roofers leave thousands per claim on the table in missed line items. AI supplement tools (RoofGenius, RAFTER) scan carrier estimates and draft code-backed supplements — RoofGenius claims ~$4,800 average recovery per claim. You operate the tool per-claim for a rev-share (10-20% of recovered amount) or flat $150-300/claim. Roofing-only, but the per-claim dollars are the biggest in this catalog.

📸 Instant-Quote Widgets

Photo-to-quote and address-to-estimate tools are now $30-40/mo (QuoteIQ, BuildFolio; Roofr for roofs). Embed an instant-estimate widget on the client's site and wire it into your speed-to-lead flow — the homeowner gets a ballpark in seconds, your AI calls them before they finish comparison shopping. Sell as +$100-150/mo bundled with the website chat add-on.

🎙️ Sales Ride-Along Coaching (Service Wrapper)

AI ride-along coaching (Rilla hit $70M ARR; Siro integrates with ServiceTitan) records in-home sales visits and lifts close rates 14-18% — but at ~$4K+/user/yr it's out of reach for small shops. Your play: record visits with consent, run transcripts through Claude against a coaching rubric, deliver a weekly 1-page coaching report. $300-500/mo for shops with 2-5 salespeople. Consent + all-party-consent states checklist applies (Legal section).

💳 Financing Wiring

Financed jobs run ~4.5x larger. Wisetack (up to $25K, native in every major FSM) and Hearth (up to $250K) are mature — your job is wiring "as low as $X/mo" into every quote follow-up message and having the AI mention financing on qualifying calls. Small direct fee ($100/mo or free as a retention sweetener), big effect on the client's average ticket — which powers your per-booking bonus and their loyalty.

Bonus Revenue Stream

Speed-to-Lead AI: Call Every Internet Lead in 60 Seconds

Your phone agent catches inbound calls. But contractors also pay $30–$300 per lead on Angi, Thumbtack, HomeAdvisor, and Google Local Services Ads — and then lose those leads by calling back hours later. Speed-to-Lead flips your existing stack from defense to offense: the moment a lead form hits the contractor’s inbox, your AI calls that lead within 60 seconds, qualifies them, and books the appointment. Same tools you already run, brand-new revenue line.

Why This Sells Itself

17%
Of HVAC pros respond to a lead within the hour — the slowest of any trade (Jobber Home Service Economic Report, 2026). Speed is the gap you sell.
78%
Of customers buy from the company that responds first — not the cheapest or the best-reviewed
$50–$300
What the contractor already paid for each lead that goes cold in their inbox while they’re on a roof

The Pitch Math (Use Their Numbers)

“You buy 40 Thumbtack leads a month at $75 each — that’s $3,000. You told me you reach maybe half of them, because you call back at the end of the day. The half you don’t reach is $1,500/month in dead spend. Our AI calls every lead in under a minute, even at 9pm. If it converts just 5 extra leads a month at your $2,500 average job, that’s $12,500 in new revenue. The service is $500/month.”

How It Works (Your Existing Stack, New Trigger)

Step 1 — Capture the lead: New leads from Angi/Thumbtack/LSA/website forms arrive by email. Set up a dedicated forwarding address (leads@client-domain) or use the platform’s webhook if available. n8n watches the inbox via IMAP trigger.

Step 2 — Parse it: n8n passes the email body to Claude (Haiku is plenty): extract name, phone, service requested, zip code, urgency. Output JSON.

Step 3 — Call within 60 seconds: n8n triggers an outbound Vapi call to the lead: “Hi, this is the assistant for [Business Name] — you just requested a quote for [service]. I can get you on the schedule right now. Is this a good time?”

Step 4 — Qualify & book: The agent confirms the job details, address, and timing, then books directly into the client’s calendar — same booking flow as your inbound agent.

Step 5 — SMS fallback: No answer? Immediately text: “Hi [Name], it’s [Business] about your [service] request — want us to call back, or pick a time here: [link]”. Retry the call at 30 min and 3 hours.

Step 6 — Report it: Log every lead, call attempt, connection, and booking to Supabase. Add a “Speed-to-Lead” block to the monthly report: leads received, % contacted in under 2 minutes, appointments booked.

Build time: If a client already runs your phone agent, this is 3–4 hours of n8n work — the Vapi agent, booking flow, and Supabase logging already exist. You’re adding one trigger and one outbound call node.

SPEED-TO-LEAD UPSELL — SCRIPT [During the monthly review, after showing results] "One more thing I wanted to flag. Do you buy leads from Angi, Thumbtack, or Google — or get quote requests through your website? [They almost always say yes.] How fast does someone call those leads back? [Typical answer: 'end of the day' or 'when I get a chance.'] So here's the thing — the data on this is brutal. 78% of customers go with whoever responds FIRST. If you're calling back at 6pm, that lead already booked with someone else at 9:15am — and you still paid for it. We can connect your AI agent to those lead sources. The second a lead comes in, the AI calls them — under 60 seconds, any hour. It qualifies them and books them straight into your calendar, exactly like it does for your inbound calls now. For your volume, it's $[X]/month on top of your current plan. If it saves even two leads a month, it's paid for itself five times over. Want me to set it up this week?"

Watch-Outs Before You Sell It

TCPA consent: A lead who submits a quote request has given implied consent to be contacted about that request — that’s your safe zone. Call about their request only; don’t add them to marketing campaigns without separate consent.

Platform rules: Thumbtack and Angi occasionally change how leads are delivered (some hide phone numbers until the pro responds in-app). Verify the client’s lead format during onboarding — ask them to forward you 3 real lead emails before you quote the build.

Identify the AI honestly: The agent should say it’s the business’s assistant calling about their request. Honest framing converts fine — deception gets complaints.

Speed is the product: Monitor the trigger-to-call latency in n8n weekly. If “60 seconds” quietly becomes 10 minutes because an IMAP poll slowed down, you’re not delivering the thing they’re paying for.

Quiet hours: Don’t auto-call leads between 9pm and 8am local time — send the SMS immediately and queue the call for morning. Configure per client.

Why This Is Your Best Bonus Revenue Stream

It reuses 100% of your existing stack, takes half a day to deploy, attacks money the client is already visibly wasting (they can see the unanswered leads in their Thumbtack inbox), and it makes your core service stickier — a client using you for inbound calls AND internet leads has twice the switching cost. Pitch it to every client at the Day 60 review.

2026 Upgrade: RCS Branded Messaging (Early-Mover Window)

Plain SMS is becoming the flip phone of business texting. RCS — now GA on Twilio (~$0.008/msg, auto-fallback to SMS) and mainstream since Apple joined — lets your speed-to-lead and missed-call texts arrive as verified branded messages: company name and logo instead of a random 10-digit number, plus tappable "Book Now" buttons, photo cards, and read receipts. For a homeowner deciding which of three contractors to trust, a verified-sender message with a booking button beats a bare-text stranger every time. Upsell it to every SMS client at +$50-100/mo ("verified branded texting"), or bake it into the Scale tier as a differentiator. Setup is a one-time Twilio RCS sender registration per client — do it once, charge forever. Most local agencies haven't touched this yet; move now.

Fast-Cash Offer

Database Reactivation: The Easiest Yes in the Industry

Every contractor has a graveyard: hundreds of past customers and dead leads sitting in a spreadsheet, a CRM, or a shoebox of invoices. Database Reactivation (DBR) wakes them up — AI texts or calls the list with a timely, relevant offer and books the responses straight into the calendar. It's the single best front-door offer in this business because you can sell it with zero risk to the owner: "You pay per booked job. If we book nothing, you pay nothing." Elsewhere in this playbook DBR appears as a $250-500 add-on campaign for existing clients; this lesson is about using it to win brand-new clients fast.

Why It Closes When Nothing Else Does

$0

5-15%

The Math That Sells It (and Pays You)

A 600-contact list at an 8% response with half of those booking = ~24 booked appointments. At $75/booking you make $1,800 on one campaign for roughly 3 hours of work. Now the contractor's side, honestly — in two stages: those 24 bookings are mostly tune-ups at ~$99-149, so stage one is ~$2,400-3,500 of direct revenue. Stage two is where the real money is: industry-typical conversion from tune-up to a repair or replacement runs roughly 20-30%, so ~5-7 of those visits become jobs averaging $1,200-1,800 — another $7,000-12,000. Total realistic return: ~$10,000-15,000 from a dead list. Never pitch 24 × full ticket (~$43K) — a contractor knows a tune-up isn't a system replacement, and inflating it costs you the deal the moment they do the math themselves. Your hard cost: ~$10-25 of SMS and AI usage. Then you say: "That was your old list. Imagine what the AI does with every new call" — and the $497/mo receptionist conversation starts itself.

How to Run a Campaign (3 Hours of Work)

Step 1 — Get the list: Ask for any export: CRM, QuickBooks invoices, even a phone-contacts dump. Minimum viable: name + mobile number. 300+ contacts makes the math work.

Step 2 — Verify consent: Have the client confirm in writing (email is fine) that these are their past customers/leads with an existing business relationship. No purchased lists, ever — see the compliance box below.

Step 3 — Clean it: Dedupe, drop landlines (use a free line-type lookup or Twilio Lookup API), drop anyone serviced in the last 60 days. Load into Supabase.

Step 4 — Pick the hook: Tie it to the season from the Seasonal Calendar: spring AC tune-up, fall furnace check, water-heater flush. Specific beats generic, an offer with a deadline beats both.

Step 5 — Send in waves: n8n sends 50-100 SMS per day (not the whole list at once — the client's calendar can drown). Message: "Hi [Name], it's [Business] — we serviced your AC in 2024. We're doing $89 pre-summer tune-ups this month for past customers. Want a spot? Reply YES and we'll text you times. Reply STOP to opt out."

Step 6 — AI handles replies: YES replies get times and a booking link (or your voice agent calls them back within 5 minutes — that's the premium version). Claude classifies ambiguous replies; STOP is honored instantly and logged.

Step 7 — Report with receipts: Send the owner a daily one-liner during the campaign ("Day 2: 31 replies, 9 booked") and a final tally with the invoice. The daily texts ARE the upsell.

The Pitch (Cold Call or DM, Word for Word)

DATABASE REACTIVATION — COLD PITCH "Quick question — how many past customers do you have in your system? Rough number. A few hundred? Here's why I ask. We run what's called a reactivation campaign: our AI texts your past customers with a seasonal offer — like a pre-summer tune-up — answers their questions, and books them straight into your calendar. For a list your size that's usually 15 to 25 booked jobs in a week or two. And here's the part that makes this easy: you don't pay anything upfront. We charge $75 per appointment that actually books. Nothing books, you pay nothing. The list is just sitting there either way. All I need is a customer export — even a QuickBooks list works — and we're live in 48 hours. Want me to send over the one-page agreement?"

Compliance Box (Read Before Your First Campaign)

Existing business relationship only: Texts go to the client's own past customers and leads. Purchased or scraped lists are a TCPA lawsuit with your name on it. Get the client's written confirmation of the relationship.

Identify the business in every message and include opt-out language ("Reply STOP to opt out") in the first text. Honor STOP instantly and keep the suppression list forever in Supabase.

AI voice calls = robocall rules: The FCC has ruled AI-generated voices count as "artificial voices" under the TCPA. Outbound AI calls need prior express consent — which is why the SMS-first version is the default and AI calls are reserved for people who reply YES.

A2P 10DLC must be approved before you send a single campaign text — unregistered traffic gets filtered and can get the number blocked. This is why you register on Day 1 of the sprint.

Quiet hours: Send between 10am and 8pm in the recipient's local time zone.

Where DBR Fits in Your Funnel

DBR is the wedge, not the business. Margins per hour are great but it's campaign work, not recurring revenue. The play: close the $0-risk pilot → deliver 15-25 bookings → convert the relationship into the $497/mo receptionist (“the AI that just filled your calendar can answer every call you're missing”) → keep DBR as a quarterly $297-497 add-on synced to the seasonal calendar. One good DBR campaign produces a case study, a testimonial, and a flagship client.

Agentic AI: The Premium Tier That Changes Everything

Your core AI phone agent is reactive — it answers when the phone rings. Agentic AI is proactive and autonomous — it reasons, plans multi-step actions, uses tools, and executes tasks without human involvement. This is the difference between a receptionist and an operations manager. It’s your biggest competitive moat and your highest-margin upsell.

Reactive vs. Agentic: What’s the Difference?

Reactive AI (Your Core Product)Agentic AI (Premium Tier)
TriggerPhone rings → AI answersAI decides when and how to act on its own
Decision-makingFollows a script with branching logicReasons about context, weighs options, chooses the best action
ToolsCaptures info, books an appointmentChecks calendars, queries databases, sends emails, updates CRMs, triggers workflows, calls APIs
MemorySingle conversation contextRemembers past interactions, learns patterns, builds customer profiles over time
Multi-stepOne task (answer call → log it)Chains 5-10 actions: check availability → match to right tech → consider drive time → book → confirm → prep dispatch notes
Example“I booked you for Tuesday at 2pm”“Based on the issue, I assigned your most experienced HVAC tech who’s already in that neighborhood tomorrow. He’ll arrive between 10-12. I also noticed this customer’s AC unit is 12 years old — I flagged a replacement consultation.”

1. Smart Dispatch Agent

$500-800/mo

Instead of just booking appointments, this agent thinks like a dispatcher. It matches incoming jobs to the right technician based on skills, location, availability, and priority — then coordinates everything automatically.

What it does:

• Checks all technician calendars + locations

• Considers: tech specialization, drive time, customer priority, job urgency

• Auto-assigns to the optimal tech

• Sends dispatch details to tech (address, issue, customer history)

• Notifies customer with tech name, ETA, and photo

• Handles rescheduling if tech runs late (auto-notifies next customers in queue)

How you build it:

• Tools: Google Calendar API (check availability), Google Maps API (drive time), Supabase (tech profiles + skills), Twilio (notify tech + customer)

• Orchestration: n8n workflow triggered by new appointment in Supabase

• Build time: 8-12 hours first client, 2-3 hours after template exists

• Your cost: ~$15-30/mo (API calls + Maps API)

Sell it as: “Your own AI dispatch coordinator. It knows where every tech is, what they’re good at, and assigns jobs to minimize drive time and maximize your daily job count. Most companies see 15-25% more jobs completed per day.”

3. Intelligent Quote Follow-Up Agent

$300-500/mo

Contractors send quotes and then forget to follow up. This agent tracks every outstanding quote and nurtures until the customer decides — adjusting its approach based on the customer’s behavior.

4. AI Reputation Management Agent

Goes far beyond “send a review request after the job.” This agent monitors all review platforms, responds intelligently, routes negative feedback before it goes public, and strategically requests reviews from the happiest customers.

5. Maintenance Plan Sales Agent

HVAC and plumbing companies make their most predictable revenue from annual maintenance plans ($150-$400/year per household). This agent proactively sells plans to the client’s existing customer base and handles renewals.

6. Customer Intelligence & Upsell Agent

This agent builds and analyzes customer profiles to identify upsell opportunities and predict needs before the customer asks. It’s the difference between a business that waits for calls and one that proactively generates revenue.

How to Build Agentic Workflows (Technical)

The core pattern for every agentic AI service is the same. Once you build one, the others are variations on the same architecture.

The Agent Loop Pattern

Trigger → Gather Context → LLM Decides Action → Execute Action → Observe Result → LLM Decides Next Action → Loop Until Done

Implementation in your stack:

• n8n “AI Agent” node: Built-in support for the agent loop pattern. Give Claude tools (Supabase query, Twilio send, Calendar check, etc.) and a goal. It reasons about which tool to use and when.

• Claude tool use (function calling): Define your tools as JSON schemas. Claude receives the context, decides which tool(s) to call, you execute them, feed results back, Claude decides next step. This is the core of agentic behavior.

• Supabase for memory: Store conversation history, customer profiles, and action logs. The agent reads history before deciding. This gives it long-term memory across interactions.

• n8n cron for proactive triggers: Not all agents are triggered by a call. The Maintenance Plan agent runs daily at 9am, checks which customers need outreach, and acts. The Quote Follow-Up agent runs every 2 hours and checks for stale quotes.

When to Introduce Agentic Services

Month 1-3

Don’t offer agentic services yet. Focus on the core AI phone agent. Get 3-5 clients, deliver great results, build case studies. The basic product is compelling enough.

Month 4-6

Build your first agentic agent for an existing client. Pick the Quote Follow-Up agent — it’s the simplest and most obvious ROI. Offer it free for 30 days to your best client. When it recovers $5K+ in stale quotes, you have your case study.

Month 6+

Launch the Agentic Pro tier for new clients. Lead with: “Most AI agencies just answer your phone. We run your entire front office.” Existing clients get offered the upgrade at a discount. New clients see it as the premium option on your pricing page.

Month 9+

Launch Enterprise for larger contractors. 10+ truck companies, multi-location businesses, franchise operators. These companies pay $3,500-5,000/mo without blinking because it replaces an office manager and a dispatcher. This is where the real money is.

Why This Is Your Moat

Anyone can set up a Vapi phone agent — YouTube tutorials make it a weekend project. But building truly agentic systems that reason, use tools, maintain memory, and orchestrate multi-step workflows? That requires real engineering skill. The moment you offer agentic AI, you’re not competing with “AI answering services” anymore — you’re competing with hiring a full-time operations manager. And you’re 80% cheaper. That’s a moat that widens over time as you build more agent types and accumulate customer data.

Google's AI Now Calls Contractors: Sell "Agent-Readiness" (Summer 2026)

This is the most time-sensitive opportunity in the entire playbook. At I/O in May 2026, Google announced agentic booking for home repair, rolling out across the US through summer 2026: when a homeowner asks Google to "find someone to fix my AC today," Google's AI searches local businesses, compares reviews and availability, and places a phone call to the contractor on the customer's behalf. If the line rings out, goes to voicemail, or nobody can state services, pricing, and availability quickly — Google's agent simply calls the next contractor on the list. The business owner never even knows the lead existed.

Read that again from your client's perspective: the missed-call problem you've been selling against just got an upgrade. It's no longer a homeowner leaving a voicemail and maybe calling back — it's a machine that instantly, silently routes the job to a competitor. Every contractor in your pipeline is about to become dramatically easier to close, because "an AI answers your phone 24/7" is now the literal entry requirement for Google's referral flow.

The Agent-Readiness Package (New Sellable, $500-1,000 Setup + Baked Into Retainer)

Position it as a certification-style upgrade: "when Google's AI calls, your business passes the test." Five deliverables, all built on assets you already have:

1. Answer instantly, every time. Your existing AI receptionist already does this — it's now the ticket to play. Tune the system prompt to handle machine callers gracefully: answer direct questions about services, service area, pricing ranges, and next available slots in the first exchange, no hold music, no "let me transfer you."

2. Speak "agent" fluently. Add a knowledge-base block with crisp, factual answers: services offered (list), service area (zips/cities), price ranges per job type, license/insurance status, emergency availability. AI callers reward direct answers and abandon vague ones.

3. Real-time booking. Connect the calendar (Cal.com or their FSM) so availability quoted on the call is real. An agent that gets "we can be there tomorrow between 9 and 11" books; one that hears "someone will call you back" moves on.

4. Structured Google Business Profile. Complete services with prices, hours, booking URL, attributes, fresh photos, active Q&A. Since Google merged LSA reviews into GBP (2025) and unified badges into the Google Verified checkmark, GBP is now the single reputation source Google's agent reads — which also supercharges your existing review-management service.

5. Prove it monthly. Add a "machine-caller test" to your QA pack: a scripted rapid-fire test call (services? area? price? tomorrow?) recorded and included in the monthly report as their Agent-Readiness check.

The pitch (works on prospects AND existing clients):

"Google started rolling out something this summer that changes your phone forever: when someone asks Google for an AC repair, Google's own AI calls contractors and books whoever answers with real availability. Voicemail means invisible — the job goes to the next name on the list, and you never know. I set businesses up to pass that test: instant answer, instant quote ranges, real calendar booking. Want me to run Google's test-call script against your line right now and show you what their AI hears?"

Why this window matters: the rollout is happening NOW (summer 2026), most contractors have no idea, and most competing agencies haven't built a package around it yet. Six months from now "AI answers your Google calls" will be table stakes — today it's a differentiator that makes your core product feel inevitable rather than optional. Lead every piece of outreach with it this quarter. One caution: describe the mechanics accurately and cite Google's announcement — don't invent statistics about how fast the agent hangs up; the honest version is scary enough.

Your Differentiators (In Order of Impact)

2. Bilingual (English + Spanish): 90% of AI agencies are English-only. You serve the fastest-growing segment of the trades market. A bilingual AI receptionist has zero direct competitors at your price point.

3. Done-for-you: You don't give them a login and say "good luck." You build it, test it, deploy it, monitor it, and fix it. They sign up and forget about it — except when they see the monthly report showing how much money you saved them.

Competitor Deep Dive: What They Actually Deliver

Know your competitors cold. Prospects will Google before they call you. Here’s what they’ll find, what each competitor actually delivers, and where they fall short. Use this intel on every sales call.

Smith.ai

$240–$900/mo

What they sell: Virtual receptionists (humans) + AI-assisted answering. Per-call pricing ($6–$12/call). Also offer outbound calls, lead qualification, appointment booking.

Their strengths: Established brand (10+ years), real humans available as backup, integrations with 30+ CRMs, free spam blocking.

Their weaknesses: Expensive at volume (30 calls/day = $5,400/mo). Humans are inconsistent across shifts. No niche specialization — same receptionist handles law firms, HVAC, and dentists. No bilingual at the lower tiers. Setup fees of $0 but high per-call pricing makes it unpredictable for contractors with variable volume.

Your edge: Fixed monthly pricing (predictable for contractors). Your AI is custom-trained for their specific trade. 24/7 with zero quality variance. At 30 calls/day, you’re 5x cheaper.

Ruby Receptionists

$235–$1,640/mo

What they sell: US-based virtual receptionists. Minute-based plans (50–500 min/mo). Live chat add-on. No AI — all human.

Their strengths: Excellent human call quality, strong brand, good mobile app for real-time notifications.

Their weaknesses: Not 24/7 on cheaper plans (Mon–Fri 5am–9pm PT). Overage charges ($2.20/min) destroy budgets on busy months. Receptionists take messages but don’t book appointments into the contractor’s calendar. No Spanish option. No AI — pure labor cost, doesn’t scale.

Your edge: True 24/7 including weekends and holidays. Appointments booked automatically. No overage charges. Bilingual standard.

Dialzara / Generic AI Voice Startups

$29–$199/mo

What they sell: Self-service AI phone agents. Contractor signs up, configures via a dashboard, plugs in their phone number. Some offer templates for different industries.

Their strengths: Low price, fast signup, some have decent templates.

Their weaknesses: DIY setup — contractors are non-technical and won’t do it. Generic prompts that don’t understand trade-specific language. No ongoing optimization (nobody’s listening to calls and fixing scripts). No integration with booking, SMS follow-up, or CRM. Support is a help desk ticket, not a partner who knows your business.

Your edge: Done-for-you. Custom-built. Ongoing optimization based on real call data. Full pipeline integration (answer → qualify → book → follow up → report). You’re an outsourced operations partner, not a tool login.

GoHighLevel Agencies (White-Label AI)

$297–$497/mo

What they sell: Full CRM + website + AI chat + missed-call text-back. White-labeled under a brand name. Some include AI phone agents via GHL’s Conversation AI.

Their strengths: All-in-one platform. Client gets a login with their branding. Built-in reputation management, email marketing, pipeline tracking. Huge ecosystem of agencies reselling the same platform.

Their weaknesses: Voice AI quality is mediocre (GHL’s native AI is behind Vapi). Clients get overwhelmed by the CRM dashboard they never asked for. Over-promise on features, under-deliver on execution. Most GHL agencies are one-person shops who set-and-forget — no optimization, no reporting, no call review. High monthly cost for features the contractor doesn’t use.

Your edge: Your voice agent quality is superior (Vapi + ElevenLabs vs. GHL native). You’re focused on the one thing that matters most: answering the phone. You don’t overwhelm them with a CRM they won’t use. You actively manage and optimize. And you’re typically cheaper for the core service.

Traditional Answering Services (AnswerConnect, MAP, etc.)

$300–$1,500/mo

What they sell: Human operators in a call center answer calls using a script. Take messages, sometimes do basic dispatching.

Their strengths: Humans handle complex calls well. Established industry with proven track record. Some contractors have used them for years and trust the model.

Their weaknesses: $1–$3 per minute adds up fast. Quality varies by shift and operator. Hold times during peak hours. No booking, no follow-up, no SMS, no data — just a message slip. They’re a cost center, not a revenue tool.

Your edge: Zero hold time. Instant booking. SMS follow-up. Monthly reports with revenue-impact data. And 50–70% cheaper at the same call volume. You turn the phone from a cost center into a revenue engine.

How to Use This on Sales Calls

Never trash-talk competitors — it makes you look desperate. Instead, ask: “What have you tried before?” or “Have you looked at any other solutions?” Then calmly address their specific option using the weaknesses above. The strongest move is the live demo: “Let me show you what ours sounds like, and you can decide for yourself.”

AI Agent Script Library

These are the Vapi system prompts you'll customize per client. Start with the HVAC template and adapt for other trades — 80% stays the same.

HVAC AI Agent — System Prompt Template

You are a friendly, professional AI receptionist for [BUSINESS NAME], an HVAC company in [CITY, STATE]. Your job is to answer calls, help customers, and book appointments. BUSINESS INFO: - Company: [BUSINESS NAME] - Services: AC repair, AC installation, heating repair, furnace installation, duct cleaning, maintenance/tune-ups - Service area: [CITY] and surrounding areas within [X] miles - Business hours: Monday-Friday [HOURS], Saturday [HOURS] - Emergency service: Available 24/7 for no heat/no cool emergencies YOUR BEHAVIOR: - You are an AI assistant and you never hide it. Your opening line is: "Thanks for calling [COMPANY], this is [AGENT NAME], an AI assistant. This call is recorded. How can I help?" If anyone asks whether you are a real person, answer plainly and immediately: "I'm an AI assistant" — never deflect. - Be warm, friendly, and conversational — you're a helpful receptionist, not a robot - Keep responses concise (1-2 sentences). Don't ramble. - If you don't know something specific (like exact pricing), say "I'd be happy to have our team get back to you with specific pricing for your situation" - Always capture: caller's name, phone number, address, and what they need help with - For emergencies (no heat, no AC, gas smell, water leak): immediately say "I understand this is urgent. Let me get a technician scheduled for you as soon as possible." APPOINTMENT BOOKING: - Available time slots: [DEFINE SLOTS] - Offer the next available slot first, then alternatives - After booking: confirm date, time, address, and phone number - Say: "You'll receive a text confirmation shortly with all the details." PRICING GUIDANCE (approximate, for reference only): - Service call/diagnostic: $89-$129 - AC tune-up: $79-$149 - Don't quote prices for repairs — say "pricing depends on what our technician finds, but I can get you scheduled for a diagnostic" ESCALATION: - If caller is upset or demands a manager: "I completely understand your frustration. Let me get our team lead to call you back within [TIMEFRAME]. What's the best number to reach you?" - If caller asks something you can't answer: "That's a great question. Let me have our team get back to you today with that information." - If caller mentions: gas leak, carbon monoxide, electrical sparking → "For your safety, if you're in immediate danger, please call 911 first. Otherwise, I'll get an emergency technician dispatched to you right away." END OF CALL: - Always end with: "Is there anything else I can help you with today?" - Confirm next steps: "Great, you're all set for [DAY] at [TIME]. You'll get a text confirmation. Have a great day!"

Plumbing AI Agent — Key Differences

PLUMBING-SPECIFIC ADDITIONS: SERVICES: Drain cleaning, water heater repair/installation, pipe repair, leak detection, sewer line, fixture installation, bathroom remodels, garbage disposal EMERGENCY TRIGGERS (escalate immediately): - Burst pipe / flooding - Sewer backup - No hot water (in winter) - Gas smell near water heater - Water damage actively happening PRICING GUIDANCE: - Service call: $79-$149 - Drain cleaning: $150-$350 - Water heater install: "Depends on the type and size — our tech will provide options on-site" - Don't quote for: pipe repair, sewer line, remodels (too variable) SEASONAL PROMPTS (add in winter): - "With cold weather coming, we're also offering pipe winterization services if you'd like to add that to your visit."

Mi nombre es [AI NAME]. ¿En qué puedo ayudarle hoy?" SPANISH BOOKING CONFIRMATION: "Perfecto, tiene una cita para el [DÍA] a las [HORA]. Recibirá un mensaje de texto con los detalles. ¿Hay algo más en lo que pueda ayudarle?" SPANISH EMERGENCY: "Entiendo que esto es urgente. Permítame programar un técnico lo antes posible. ¿Me puede confirmar su dirección?"

Electrical Contractor AI Agent — Key Differences

ELECTRICAL-SPECIFIC: SERVICES: Panel upgrades, outlet installation, lighting, ceiling fans, EV charger installation, generator installation, rewiring, troubleshooting, inspection EMERGENCY TRIGGERS: - Sparking outlet / burning smell - Power outage (partial — full outage = call utility first) - Exposed wiring - Water near electrical SAFETY SCRIPT: "If you're seeing sparks or smelling burning, please turn off the breaker for that area if you can safely reach it, and stay clear. I'll get an electrician to you as quickly as possible." UPSELL PROMPT (after booking standard service): "Just so you know, we're also seeing a lot of customers adding EV charger installations and panel upgrades. If that's something you've been thinking about, our tech can provide a quote while they're there."

Emergency Escalation Playbook

When a real emergency call hits your AI agent — gas leak, flooding, no heat in winter, sparking wires — the agent must handle it differently than a normal appointment request. Get this wrong once and you lose the client (and potentially face liability). Configure this during onboarding and test it before go-live.

Emergency Detection: What the AI Listens For

Add these trigger phrases to the agent’s system prompt. When the AI detects an emergency, it switches to the emergency script below instead of the normal booking flow.

HVAC Triggers

“gas leak” · “smell gas” · “no heat” (winter) · “no AC” (summer, 95°+) · “carbon monoxide” · “furnace won’t turn on” · “flooding from AC unit”

Plumbing Triggers

“burst pipe” · “flooding” · “water everywhere” · “sewer backup” · “no water” · “water heater leaking” · “toilet overflowing and won’t stop”

Electrical Triggers

“sparks” · “burning smell” · “exposed wires” · “outlet smoking” · “power out” (partial) · “water near electrical”

General Triggers

“emergency” · “urgent” · “right now” · “dangerous” · “someone could get hurt” · “kids in the house” (with any hazard)

EMERGENCY ESCALATION — SYSTEM PROMPT ADDITION (Add this block to every client's agent prompt) ## EMERGENCY HANDLING If the caller describes any of the following situations, switch to emergency mode immediately: - Gas leak / smell of gas - Active flooding or burst pipe - Electrical sparks, burning smell, or exposed wires - No heat with outside temperature below 40°F - No AC with outside temperature above 95°F - Carbon monoxide alarm sounding - Sewer backup into living space EMERGENCY SCRIPT: "I understand this is urgent and I want to make sure you're safe. [If gas leak or CO alarm]: First, please get everyone out of the house and call 911 from outside. Do not use light switches. [If electrical sparks/fire]: If you can safely reach your breaker box, turn off the breaker for that area. If you see smoke, get everyone out and call 911. [If flooding]: If safe, turn off your main water shut-off valve. It's usually near your water meter or where the main line enters. I'm going to get [BUSINESS NAME] on the line right now. Please stay on the phone." AFTER SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS: 1. Attempt warm transfer to client's emergency number: [NUMBER] 2. If no answer after 4 rings, try backup number: [BACKUP] 3. If no answer on backup, tell the caller: "I wasn't able to reach [OWNER NAME] directly, but I've sent them an urgent text and email with your information. They typically respond to emergencies within [X] minutes. Can I confirm your callback number?" 4. Send URGENT SMS to client: "🚨 EMERGENCY: [Caller Name] at [Address] — [Issue]. Call them ASAP: [Phone]" 5. Send URGENT email with same info 6. Log the call as priority:emergency in Supabase

n8n Emergency Workflow

Trigger: Vapi webhook with call_type: "emergency" (set via tool call in the agent prompt).

Step 1: Send high-priority SMS to client’s cell via Twilio (use priority queue: contentRetention=discard, validityPeriod=300).

Step 2: Send email to client with subject “URGENT: Emergency call from [Caller Name]”.

Step 3: Log to Supabase calls table with priority='emergency' and status='awaiting_response'.

Step 4: Set a 15-minute delay node, then check if client responded (Supabase status update). If not, send a follow-up SMS: “Reminder: emergency call 15 min ago. [Caller Name]: [Issue]. Call them: [Phone].”

Setup During Onboarding (Critical)

Collect the emergency number from the intake form. Confirm: “Is this the cell phone that’s always on you, even at 2am?”

Collect a backup number (partner, office manager, on-call tech). The AI tries both before giving up.

Test the warm transfer before go-live. Call the demo agent, say “I smell gas,” and verify it correctly attempts the transfer to the client’s cell.

Test the fallback path — let the emergency number ring to voicemail. Verify the urgent SMS and email arrive within 10 seconds.

Set expectations with the client: “Your agent handles emergencies by trying to reach you immediately. If you don’t answer, it takes the caller’s info and sends you an urgent text. You should respond within 15 minutes.”

Liability Note

Your contract’s limitation of liability clause covers this, but always tell callers to call 911 first for life-threatening situations. The AI should never tell someone to wait for the contractor if there’s a fire, gas leak, or CO alarm. Safety instructions first, then business routing.

Rule of Thumb

Don't switch tools unless something is broken or you've outgrown it. Every migration costs time. Stick with the "Primary" column until you have a specific reason to change. The most expensive tool is the one you spend a week migrating to.

Knowledge Check Module 6: Technical Architecture

A client's AI agent needs to: answer calls, check the calendar for open slots, book an appointment, and send a confirmation text. What's the correct data flow?

Exactly! Twilio handles telephony, Vapi manages the AI conversation, n8n orchestrates the workflow via webhooks, Supabase stores the data, Cal.com handles scheduling, and Twilio sends the confirmation SMS.
The correct flow uses your full stack: Twilio (phone) → Vapi (AI conversation) → n8n (workflow automation) → Supabase + Cal.com (data + scheduling) → Twilio SMS (confirmation).

The 2026 Shift: Speech-to-Text Now Detects When the Caller Stops Talking

The most underrated upgrade of 2026 isn't a prettier voice — it's end-of-turn detection moving into the STT model itself. Old pipelines needed a separate VAD (voice-activity detector) to guess when the caller finished a sentence; that guesswork is what causes the bot to interrupt people or leave awkward pauses. New STT models do it natively, shaving 200-600ms off every response. That's the difference between "feels like a robot" and "felt like a person" in a demo.

STT ProviderCostWhy it matters
Deepgram Flux$0.0065/min (EN), $0.0078/min (multilingual)First conversational STT with built-in end-of-turn detection (median EOT <300ms, no external VAD). Available in Vapi. Removes a whole component and saves real latency at trivial cost.
Cartesia Ink-2usage-basedNew streaming STT with built-in turn detection + noise-robust transcription (great for noisy job-site callers). Pairs with Sonic for a single-vendor STT+TTS stack — fewer moving parts.
ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtimeusage-basedSub-150ms, 90+ languages, ~2.3% word error rate. Strong accuracy+latency combo if you want ElevenLabs end-to-end.

Two newer architectures to know (don't default to them yet)

Speech-to-speech (OpenAI Realtime, in Vapi since May 7). One model does STT + reasoning + TTS in a single pass — lower latency, more natural turn-taking. But ~$0.30/min all-in (vs. your ~$0.10-0.13 Cartesia+Haiku pipeline), and in Vapi it doesn't support knowledge bases or custom voice cloning (voices limited to Cedar/Marin). For a branded contractor receptionist that must quote service areas and pricing, that's a dealbreaker today. Treat it as a premium tier to test, not the default. July 6 update: OpenAI shipped gpt-realtime-2.1 (p95 latency cut ~25%, better interruption/noise handling, configurable reasoning — use "low" for voice) and gpt-realtime-2.1-mini at roughly 1/3 the audio price (~$10/$20 per M audio tokens) — the mini finally makes speech-to-speech worth benchmarking against your pipeline on cost, not just feel.

Gemini 3.1 Flash Live (audio-to-audio, ~960ms TTFT). Google's speech-to-speech option, also in Vapi. Cheaper than Realtime-2 but slower first-token than a tuned Cartesia path. Worth a benchmark, not a switch.

Cost Lever: Cache Your System Prompt and Cut LLM Cost ~90%

Your receptionist's system prompt is large (identity, hours, service area, pricing rules, transfer logic) and identical on every call. Anthropic prompt caching reads a cached prefix at ~0.1× the normal input price (≈90% off) after the first call. This is free money you're probably leaving on the table.

How: Put the stable system prompt + business knowledge before the cache_control breakpoint, and the live call transcript after it. Every turn after the first reads the cached prefix at 1/10th the cost.

Batch the offline work: overnight call-transcript summaries, lead scoring, and CRM enrichment don't need to be real-time. Run them through the Batch API at 50% off (Haiku 4.5 batch = $0.50/$2.50). Stack caching + batch and offline jobs cost almost nothing.

Keep the live call path on Haiku 4.5 (or test GPT-5.4 Nano) — never batch the real-time conversation, only the after-the-fact analysis.

Vapi Simulations: Test Your Agent Before It Talks to Real Customers

Vapi launched Simulations in 2026 — AI-powered test calls that stress-test your agent before it goes live. This is the single biggest QA upgrade for agencies: instead of manually calling your agent 20 times, you define scenarios and the system runs them automatically. Use it:

Before every go-live: Vapi Dashboard → your agent → Simulations tab. Create 5-8 scenarios that cover your client's reality:

• Standard booking request during business hours

• After-hours emergency ("my pipe burst")

• Spanish-language caller

• Angry/confused caller who interrupts

• Caller asking about pricing the agent shouldn't quote

• Caller asking to speak to a human

After every script change: Re-run your simulation suite. Catches regressions you'd miss manually.

Pair with QA Monitoring: Vapi's new monitoring dashboard flags live calls with low scores, long pauses, or hang-ups. Set up alerts → n8n webhook → Slack/email notification. Review flagged calls weekly.

Sell this as a feature: "Before we go live, we run your agent through 8 different test scenarios — angry callers, emergencies, Spanish speakers, weird questions. We don't ship until it passes every one." Clients love hearing this; it builds trust that you're not just flipping a switch.

Backup, Security & Access Management

Your clients trust you with their business communications. One leaked API key or lost workflow can cost you a client and your reputation. Lock everything down from Day 1.

API Key Management

Use a password manager: Store every API key, password, and credential in Bitwarden (free) or 1Password. Never in plain text, never in a Google Doc, never in a Slack message.

Never put keys in n8n node names or workflow comments. Anyone with access to your n8n instance can see these. Use n8n’s built-in credential store instead.

Use n8n credentials properly: Go to Settings → Credentials → Create New. Store Supabase, Twilio, Vapi, and email API keys here. Reference them in nodes — don’t paste keys directly into HTTP request nodes.

Separate keys per service where possible. Don’t reuse the same API key across different integrations. If one is compromised, only that integration is affected.

2FA Checklist

Enable two-factor authentication on every account. No exceptions. Use an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy), not SMS.

Vapi — Settings → Security → 2FA

Twilio — Console → Account → Security → 2FA

Supabase — Account Settings → Security

Stripe — Settings → Team → Two-step authentication

Email (Google Workspace) — Account → Security → 2-Step Verification

GitHub (if using for code) — Settings → Security

Hetzner — Account → Security → Two-factor authentication

Domain registrar (Namecheap, Cloudflare, etc.)

Backup Procedures

n8n workflows (weekly): Settings → Export All Workflows. Save the JSON file to Google Drive or a password-protected folder. Do this every Sunday night. One lost workflow = hours of rebuilding.

Supabase (auto on paid, manual on free): Paid plans have daily auto-backups with point-in-time recovery. On the free tier: monthly, go to SQL Editor and run pg_dump or use the Supabase CLI to export your data. Save the SQL file.

Vapi agent configs: Document each agent’s system prompt, voice settings, and tool configurations in a shared Google Doc. If Vapi ever resets or you need to rebuild, you have the blueprint.

Client data: Export Supabase client table as CSV quarterly. Store in a folder: /backups/[YEAR-MONTH]/clients.csv

Automation idea: Build an n8n workflow that auto-exports your Supabase data on the 1st of each month and emails you the CSV. Takes 30 minutes to build, saves you from ever forgetting.

Access Control

Never share master credentials. If Paola needs Twilio access, create a sub-user with limited permissions. Same for n8n — create a separate user account.

Create sub-accounts where possible: Twilio supports sub-accounts per client. Supabase lets you create separate projects. This keeps client data isolated.

Rotate API keys quarterly. Set a calendar reminder for every 3 months. Generate new keys, update your credential store and all workflows, then revoke the old keys.

If an API Key Is Compromised

Act immediately. Don’t wait — every minute a compromised key is live is a risk.

Step 1: Revoke the compromised key immediately in the provider’s dashboard.

Step 2: Generate a new key from the same provider.

Step 3: Update every n8n workflow and credential that used the old key.

Step 4: Audit recent API calls in the provider’s logs. Look for unusual activity — calls you didn’t make, data exports, new resources created.

Step 5: If client data was potentially exposed, notify affected clients within 24 hours. Transparency builds trust even in bad situations.

Real-World Supply-Chain Lesson: The Vapi Incident (June 3, 2026)

On June 3, 2026, a malicious supply-chain worm compromised Vapi's GitHub repos and npm packages (including @vapi-ai/server-sdk, 408K+ monthly downloads). Malicious code was pushed using an unexpired access token. Vapi rolled it back within hours and confirmed no customer data was leaked — but the lesson is real:

Pin your dependency versions. Don't auto-update npm/pip packages in production. Lock to known-good versions and update intentionally.

Monitor vendor status pages. Bookmark status.vapi.ai, status.twilio.com, and status.supabase.com. Check them first when something breaks — before blaming your own code.

Your stack portability is your insurance. If you own the phone number (Twilio), the prompts (your repo), the data (Supabase), and the workflows (n8n), you can swap any one vendor in 1-2 days. If you're locked into a single platform, you're one incident from a fire drill.

VPS Security Basics

Your Hetzner VPS runs n8n and potentially other services. Lock it down.

SSH key only: Disable password authentication. Use SSH key pairs. Add your key during Hetzner server creation, then edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config and set PasswordAuthentication no.

Firewall: Allow only ports 80 (HTTP), 443 (HTTPS), and your SSH port. Block everything else. Use ufw on Ubuntu:

sudo ufw default deny incoming sudo ufw default allow outgoing sudo ufw allow 22/tcp # SSH sudo ufw allow 80/tcp # HTTP sudo ufw allow 443/tcp # HTTPS sudo ufw enable

Automatic security updates: Enable unattended upgrades so critical patches install automatically:

sudo apt install unattended-upgrades sudo dpkg-reconfigure -plow unattended-upgrades

Keep Docker updated: Run sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade monthly. Check for n8n Docker image updates: docker pull n8nio/n8n:latest then restart the container.

Technical Troubleshooting Guide

When something breaks (and it will), don’t panic. Find the symptom below, follow the fix steps, and you’ll be back online in minutes.

1. AI agent sounds robotic or has long pauses

Check Vapi latency settings: Dashboard → Agent → Advanced → ensure “Response Delay” is under 800ms.

Try a different TTS voice: Some ElevenLabs voices have more natural cadence. Test “Rachel,” “Josh,” or “Bella.”

Verify LLM selection: Use Haiku 4.5 for speed-critical responses, Sonnet 4.6 for quality-critical conversations. Opus/Fable are overkill and add latency. Also try GPT-5.4 Nano ($0.20/$1.25) — the new budget pick, competitive on speed.

Check VPS CPU usage: SSH in and run htop. If CPU is pegged at 100%, your VPS is too small or something else is consuming resources.

2. n8n workflow isn’t triggering

Check webhook URL: Is the URL in Vapi/Twilio pointing to your current n8n instance? Copy it from the webhook node in n8n and compare.

Verify n8n is running: SSH in and run docker ps. If n8n container isn’t listed, restart it with docker-compose up -d.

Check workflow is Active: In n8n, the toggle in the top-right must be ON (green). Inactive workflows ignore all triggers.

Review execution log: n8n → Executions (left sidebar). Look for red (failed) executions. Click to see the error message and which node failed.

Check if n8n is publicly reachable: Try opening your n8n webhook URL in a browser. If you get a timeout, your VPS firewall or DNS might be misconfigured.

3. SMS confirmations not sending

Verify Twilio credentials in n8n: Settings → Credentials → Twilio. Test the connection. Re-enter Account SID and Auth Token if needed.

Check A2P 10DLC registration status: Twilio Console → Messaging → Trust Hub. If your campaign is “Pending” or “Rejected,” SMS will be blocked.

Confirm Twilio account balance: If your Twilio balance hits $0, all messaging stops. Set up auto-recharge in Billing.

Check phone number capability: Twilio Console → Phone Numbers → click the number → verify it’s SMS-enabled (not all numbers are).

4. Supabase connection errors

Check API key hasn’t expired: Supabase → Settings → API. Copy the anon key and update it in n8n credentials if needed.

Verify RLS policies: If you enabled Row Level Security but didn’t create policies, all queries will return empty results. Check Tables → Policies.

Check free tier limits: Free tier gives you 500MB storage and limited connections. If you’re near the limit, consider upgrading ($25/mo) or cleaning old data.

Test connection independently: In n8n, create a simple workflow with a Supabase node that reads one row. If this works, the issue is in your specific workflow logic.

5. Call recordings not saving

Verify Vapi recording settings: Agent → Advanced Settings → ensure “Record Calls” is enabled.

Check webhook payload: In n8n, look at the incoming webhook data. Is recording_url present? If not, the call may have been too short or recording failed.

Verify Supabase column exists: Check that your calls table has a recording_url column of type TEXT. If it’s missing, add it via SQL Editor.

Check timing: Vapi recordings take 30-60 seconds after the call ends to process. Your webhook might fire before the recording URL is available. Add a “Wait” node (60s) before saving.

6. Agent answers but doesn’t book appointments

Check Cal.com integration: Verify the Cal.com API key in your n8n workflow is valid. Test by manually creating a booking via the API.

Verify calendar has available slots: Log into Cal.com → Availability. If all slots are blocked, the agent can’t book anything.

Test the booking webhook independently: Trigger the booking node in n8n manually with test data. Check if the error is in the Cal.com node or upstream.

Check the agent prompt: Make sure the system prompt tells the AI to collect the right data (name, phone, address, preferred time) before attempting to book.

7. Client says calls are going to voicemail instead of AI

Verify call forwarding: Call the client’s business number yourself. Does it ring and then forward, or go straight to voicemail? If voicemail, forwarding isn’t set up correctly.

Test the Twilio number directly: Call the Twilio number (not the client’s number). If the AI answers, the issue is forwarding, not your setup.

Check Twilio call logs: Console → Monitor → Logs → Calls. Are incoming calls showing up? If not, the forwarding isn’t reaching Twilio.

Common fix: Have the client re-activate forwarding. On iPhone: Settings → Phone → Call Forwarding → toggle off, then on, re-enter Twilio number. On landline: dial *73 to cancel, then *72 + Twilio number to re-set.

Quick Diagnostic Commands

SSH into your VPS and run these to diagnose common issues.

# Check if n8n is running docker ps # View n8n logs (last 50 lines) docker logs n8n --tail 50 # View n8n logs in real-time (Ctrl+C to exit) docker logs n8n -f # Restart n8n docker-compose down && docker-compose up -d # Check disk space df -h # Check memory usage free -h # Check CPU usage htop # Check if ports are open sudo ss -tlnp | grep -E '80|443|5678' # Test if n8n webhook is reachable from outside curl -I https://your-n8n-domain.com/webhook-test/test

Monitoring Setup

UptimeRobot (free tier): Create an account at uptimerobot.com. Add a monitor for your n8n URL (HTTP check, 5-minute interval). Set up email + SMS alerts. Free tier gives you 50 monitors — more than enough.

n8n health-check workflow: Create a workflow with a Cron trigger (every 5 min) that pings your Vapi agent, checks Supabase connectivity, and verifies Twilio is responding. If any check fails, send yourself an SMS alert via Twilio.

Twilio error alerts: Console → Monitor → Alerts → set up email notifications for failed calls or error codes.

Supabase dashboard: Check the built-in metrics (API requests, database size, connection count) weekly to catch issues before they become problems.

The 5-Minute Fix Rule

90% of issues are solved by: (1) checking if the service is running, (2) checking credentials, (3) restarting the container. If you can’t fix it in 5 minutes, check the provider’s status page — it might be their outage, not yours. Vapi, Twilio, and Supabase all have status pages.

Legal Essentials & Contract Template

Keep it simple. A 2-page agreement protects both sides. Here are the key terms every client contract must include.

Must-Have Contract Clauses

Scope of work: Exactly what you deliver (AI phone agent, X number of minutes, SMS follow-ups, monthly report). What's NOT included (website, SEO, marketing — unless sold separately).

Pricing & payment: Setup fee amount, monthly retainer, payment due date (1st of month), accepted methods (Stripe), late payment terms (5-day grace, then service paused).

Term: Month-to-month. 30-day written notice to cancel. No long-term lock-in (reduces sales friction).

Ownership: You own the technology, workflows, and system prompts. Client owns their call recordings and customer data. Upon cancellation, you provide them an export of their data within 30 days.

Limitation of liability: Your liability is capped at the last 3 months of fees paid. You're not responsible for lost business, missed emergency calls (they have backup forwarding), or third-party outages (Twilio, Vapi).

Indemnification: Client is responsible for the accuracy of their business info, pricing, and service claims that you program into the AI.

Confidentiality: Both parties keep each other's business information confidential.

Right to use as reference: Client grants you permission to use their business name, results, and testimonials in marketing (with approval).

Tools for Contracts

PandaDoc (free for e-signatures) — create template, send, get signed. Tracks when they view/sign.

HelloSign / Dropbox Sign — alternative. 3 free documents/month.

Google Docs + DocuSign — draft in Docs, send for signature via DocuSign.

Data Handling & Privacy

Call recordings: You must inform callers they're being recorded. Add to the AI greeting: "This call may be recorded for quality purposes." This is legally required in most US states.

Customer data: Store securely (Supabase with Row Level Security). Don't share one client's data with another. Basic hygiene, but put it in writing.

TCPA compliance for SMS: You must have consent to text someone. Inbound callers give implied consent by calling. For outbound campaigns (reactivation), client must confirm they have prior business relationship.

GDPR: Doesn't apply to your US clients' US customers. But as a Germany-based business, be aware of it for your own data practices and European prospects (if you expand later).

2026 Compliance Updates (Action Required)

The one rule that covers 80% of your risk: have every agent say it's an AI at the start of the call, in both languages, on every call. That single line satisfies Utah's safe harbor, California's AB 2905 expectation, and the emerging national baseline. Then add a recorded-call notice. Everything below is detail on top of those two habits.

Utah AI Policy Act (amended, in force; extended to July 2027): A business using generative AI to talk to consumers must disclose it's AI when asked — but there's a safe harbor: if your agent clearly states it's not human at the outset and throughout, you're exempt from enforcement. Penalty up to $2,500/violation. Do this in every state — it's the cheapest, highest-leverage compliance step you have.

California AB 2905 (in force since Jan 1, 2025): Any prerecorded/autodialed call using an AI-generated voice must disclose — before the AI voice is used — that an artificial voice follows, plus the nature of the call and contact info. This hits ordinary AI-voice outbound calling (distinct from SB 243). For any outbound AI-voice campaign into California, lead with that disclosure.

California SB 243 (effective Jan 1, 2026) — know the scope: This law targets companion / social chatbots (AI built for ongoing emotional relationships), not a transactional receptionist/scheduler. Your AI receptionist almost certainly falls outside it — don't over-scope. The receptionist-relevant California rule is AB 2905 above. (Same for WA HB 2225, OR SB 1546, TN SB 1580, NY's chatbot law — all companion-bot laws.)

Colorado AI Act — date corrected: Originally slated for 2026, it was delayed to Jan 1, 2027 (SB 189, signed May 14, 2026) and enforcement was paused by a federal court in April 2026 (xAI suit + DOJ intervention). Don't build compliance work against a 2026 date. Monitor it — status is fluid.

Call-recording consent (11 all-party states: CA, DE, FL, IL, MD, MA, MT, NV, NH, PA, WA): AI transcription doesn't change this — the law targets the act of recording. Play an audible "this call is recorded" notice at the start of every recorded call. One 2026 settlement ran $4.2M for ~5,000 calls recorded without consent.

Illinois BIPA — voiceprint risk: Voiceprints are protected biometric data; statutory damages $1,000–$5,000 per person, per instance. Don't generate or store voice embeddings/voiceprints unless you have explicit written consent and a retention/deletion policy. Standard transcription is fine; voice "fingerprinting" is the trap.

FCC consent revocation rule (effective Apr 2025): Consumers can revoke consent with any reasonable phrase ("stop," "cancel," "don't call me"). Must honor within 10 days. Your n8n STOP-handler should catch variants, not just the literal word "STOP." Use Claude to classify opt-out intent on every inbound reply.

Review requests: never gate, never incentivize. Two rules that protect your clients from Google penalties and FTC exposure — and that you must build into every review workflow you sell: (1) No gating. Do not survey first and send the review link only to happy customers. Google's policies prohibit soliciting reviews selectively, and the FTC's 2024 rule on consumer reviews (with penalties per violation) treats suppressing negative reviews as deceptive. Ask everyone, the same way. (2) No incentives for reviews. Never offer a discount, gift card, entry to a draw, or free service in exchange for a review — that's a direct Google policy violation and an FTC problem, and it can get a contractor's entire review history wiped. Referral rewards to your own clients for introducing new business are fine and legal — that's a referral fee, not a paid review. If a client asks you to build "5-star filtering," decline and explain why: getting their profile penalized would cost them more than every review it gained.

FCC AI-robocall rule still pending: The proposed rule to require AI-call disclosure + affirmative consent is still an NPRM (not final as of mid-July 2026; trackers expect a final rule Q4 2026/Q1 2027). The operative federal rule remains the Feb 2024 ruling that AI voices are "artificial" under the TCPA. Keep documented prior express written consent for any AI-voice outbound marketing, and confirm your telephony vendor is RMD-listed + STIR/SHAKEN compliant (get it in writing) — the FCC's July 22 meeting votes on tightening RMD vetting, so upstream-carrier hygiene matters more, not less.

July 2026 state-law watch list: Colorado signed a Chatbot Safety Act (HB 26-1263, July 1) — consumer-facing conversational AI must disclose it's AI, effective Jan 1, 2027, up to $20K/violation; your existing AI self-ID line already satisfies the core duty. Pennsylvania passed SB 992 (awaiting the governor's signature): telemarketing rules extend to texts and ringless voicemail, calls limited to 9am-7pm with no Sundays, and uniform opt-out keywords (STOP/QUIT/END/REVOKE/OPT OUT/CANCEL/UNSUBSCRIBE) — if you serve PA clients, tighten calling windows and make sure your n8n STOP-handler catches all six words. Tennessee (SB 1580, effective July 1): AI must never imply it's a licensed professional — fine for receptionists, just don't let prompts claim credentials. California's SB 942 AI-transparency duties start Aug 2, 2026 but target large AI developers, not agencies. Net: your one rule — AI self-ID + recorded-call notice — still covers the overwhelming majority of this.

SMS/10DLC 2026 changes: T-Mobile added a per-message pass-through fee (~$0.0025/msg) on Jan 19, 2026 — budget it or pass it through. Virginia SB 1339 (in force 2026) requires honoring SMS opt-outs for 10 years — keep a permanent suppression list, never reuse it. Carriers now hard-block unregistered traffic (T-Mobile penalties up to $10,000/violation).

Federal preemption backdrop: The June 2, 2026 EO, a DOJ AI Litigation Task Force, and the "Great American AI Act" draft (June 4, 2026) are all trying to preempt state AI laws — but none has passed. State laws remain enforceable now (except where courts paused them, like Colorado). Don't strip compliance based on EO talk; executive orders don't preempt state law without Congress.

This is a fast-moving area and not legal advice — confirm specifics with counsel before relying on any single rule. The two habits in the blue box are safe in every state regardless of how the litigation shakes out.
