Pro Tip: Keep It Simple

Contractors hate long contracts. 2 pages max. Use plain English, not legal jargon. Send via PandaDoc or HelloSign — they sign on their phone in 30 seconds. If a prospect asks for changes, that’s actually a good sign — they’re serious about signing.

Statement of Work (SOW) Template

The Services Agreement above is your master contract — you sign it once per client. The SOW is the one-page attachment that spells out exactly what you’re building for this engagement. Attach it to the agreement so there’s zero ambiguity about deliverables, timeline, and what counts as “done.” This is your single best defense against scope creep.

STATEMENT OF WORK — [Client Business Name] Attached to and governed by the Services Agreement dated [Date] Provider: Colibri Code LLC | SOW #: [001] | Date: [Date] 1. PROJECT SUMMARY Deploy a 24/7 AI phone answering agent for [Client Business Name], a [trade] company serving [City/Region]. Goal: answer 100% of inbound calls, capture lead details, and book appointments. 2. DELIVERABLES [x] AI voice agent configured with client's business info, hours, services, and pricing [x] Dedicated phone number + call forwarding setup [x] SMS confirmation + missed-call text-back automation [x] Appointment booking integration ([Cal.com / client calendar]) [x] Call logging dashboard (Supabase) with recordings [x] Automated monthly performance report [x] 1 round of script revisions after go-live 3. NOT INCLUDED (available as paid add-ons) - Website, SEO, or paid ad management - CRM build-out beyond call logging - Outbound calling / cold-call campaigns - Custom integrations not listed above 4. TIMELINE Day 0: Signed SOW + intake form completed by client Day 1-2: Agent build + number provisioning Day 3: Internal testing + client test call Day 4: Go-live Day 7: Week-1 review call Acceptance: Deliverables deemed accepted if no written issues are reported within 5 business days of go-live. 5. CLIENT INPUTS REQUIRED (to start) - Business hours, service area, pricing/quote ranges - List of services offered + common FAQs - Where to route emergency / urgent calls - Calendar access or booking preferences 6. FEES FOR THIS SOW Setup fee: $[X] (one-time) | Monthly: $[X]/mo Add-ons selected: [none / list] 7. CHANGE REQUESTS Work outside this SOW is quoted separately and added via a written change order before work begins. Approved by: ____________________ Date: __________ [Client Name] Approved by: ____________________ Date: __________ Colibri Code LLC

Satisfaction Guarantee & Refund Policy

A clear guarantee removes the #1 objection (“what if it doesn’t work?”) and closes more deals than any discount. Because you’re month-to-month with a low setup fee, the risk to you is tiny — but the trust it buys is huge. Pick the policy that fits your risk tolerance and state it the same way every time.

Recommended: 14-Day “It Works” Guarantee

“If your agent isn’t answering calls and capturing leads within 14 days of go-live, we’ll refund your setup fee in full — no questions asked.” You keep the first month’s retainer (work was performed); you refund only the one-time setup fee. Low risk, high trust.

Aggressive: 30-Day Money-Back

“Try it for 30 days. If you’re not happy for any reason, cancel and we’ll refund your first month + setup fee.” Closes the most deals but exposes you to ~$1,000+ per refund. Use only once your delivery is dialed in and churn is low.

Policy Rules (Put These in Writing)

Guarantee covers performance, not buyer’s remorse on results you can’t control. You guarantee the agent answers and captures leads — not how many people call their business.

Setup fee refundable, monthly retainer is not (after the period passes). Work performed in a paid month isn’t refunded once that month is delivered.

One guarantee window per client. The window resets only if they cancel and re-sign 6+ months later.

Refunds processed within 7 business days via the original Stripe payment. Document the reason every time — refunds are your most honest churn data.

Data export still provided. Even on a refund, give the client their call recordings and lead data. It costs you nothing and protects your reputation.

SATISFACTION GUARANTEE (add to proposal + contract) We're so confident your AI agent will pay for itself that we back it with a simple promise: If your agent isn't live and answering calls within 14 days of your completed intake, we'll refund your setup fee in full. There's no long-term contract. You're month-to-month and can cancel anytime with 30 days' notice. We earn your business every single month.

Sales Tip: Say It Out Loud

Read the guarantee aloud on the discovery call right before the trial close. It reframes the decision from “should I risk $1,000?” to “what do I have to lose?” Pair it with the month-to-month term and most objections evaporate.

Insurance Checklist

General Liability (GL): ~$50-60/mo through Next Insurance or Hiscox. Covers basic business liability. Get this before your first client.

Errors & Omissions (E&O): ~$40-50/mo. Covers claims of negligence (e.g., AI mishandles a call). Worth having once you pass 3+ clients.

Cyber Liability: Consider at 10+ clients. Covers data breaches and cybersecurity incidents. ~$30-50/mo.

When to get insurance: GL before first client (non-negotiable). E&O by month 3. Cyber liability by month 6+. Total: ~$100-150/mo — already included in the P&L projections.

Case Study Factory: Build Social Proof Fast

After 30 days with your first client, you have enough data for a case study. Case studies are your single best sales asset — more powerful than any pitch deck.

The Template (Fill This for Every Client)

Title formula: "How [BUSINESS] Captured [X] More Calls in 30 Days (and Booked $[Y] in New Jobs)"

The Problem (2-3 sentences): "[Business Owner] runs a [X]-person [trade] company in [City]. During peak season, they were missing 30-40% of incoming calls because the team was out on jobs. Every missed call meant a $[job value] job going to a competitor."

The Solution (2-3 sentences): "We deployed a 24/7 AI phone agent that answers every call in under 1 second, captures the caller's information, and books appointments directly. [Business Owner] didn't have to change their phone number or learn any new software."

The Results (bullet points with numbers):

  • • Calls answered: [X] per month (previously missing [Y]%)
  • • Appointments booked automatically: [X] per month
  • • Estimated additional revenue captured: $[X]/month
  • • ROI: [X]x their monthly investment

The Quote: "I was skeptical about AI answering my phone, but honestly? It sounds better than my last receptionist. And it never calls in sick." — [Name], Owner of [Business]

Creating Video Case Studies (Higher Impact)

Written case studies work. Video case studies crush. Here’s how to create both without bothering your client too much:

Option A: Loom Screen Recording (Easiest)

Record yourself showing the client’s before/after data. Show the Supabase dashboard with real call numbers. Narrate the story. No client involvement needed. Takes 5 minutes. This is your default.

Option B: Client Video Testimonial (Best)

Ask the client for a 2-minute Zoom call. Record it (with permission). Ask 3 questions: “What was the problem before?” “What changed?” “Would you recommend this?” Edit to 60-90 seconds. Use on website and LinkedIn. Most contractors will say yes — they’re proud of their business.

Option C: Before/After Call Recording (Most Convincing)

With permission, play a real AI call recording in your demo. Nothing sells better than hearing the AI actually handle a real plumbing emergency call at 11pm on a Saturday. “Listen to this — this call came in at 11:15pm last Tuesday. The AI booked a $4,200 job.”

Seasonal Marketing Calendar: When to Sell What

Home service businesses are extremely seasonal. Time your outreach and upsells to their busiest periods for maximum conversion. A contractor panicking about missed calls in July is 10x easier to close than one in November.

The Golden Rule

Start your outreach 4-6 weeks BEFORE peak season. An HVAC company will buy in April for the May-August rush. They won't buy in January because they're not thinking about AC yet. Time it right and your close rate doubles.

First-90-Days Client Health Scorecard

The timeline above is what you do. This scorecard is how you know a client is healthy — or quietly about to churn. Score each client at Day 30, 60, and 90. A dropping score is your early-warning system: act before they cancel, not after.

Health Signal2 pts (Green)1 pt (Yellow)0 pts (Red)
Call volume answeredSteady or risingFlat / lowNear zero
Appointments bookedBooking regularlyOccasionalNone in 30 days
Client responsivenessReplies same daySlow repliesGhosting you
Payment statusOn timeLate onceLate 2+ / failed
Sentiment on callsEnthusiasticNeutralComplaints
Logged in / engagedChecks reportsRarelyNever opens

9–12: Healthy

Ask for a testimonial and a referral. This is your expansion and case-study client.

5–8: At Risk

Book a value call this week. Show them their saved-revenue number. Fix the weakest signal.

0–4: Churn Imminent

Call the owner directly today. Run the save-attempt playbook before they cancel.

How to Run It

Score every client at Day 30, 60, and 90, then monthly after that. Takes 2 minutes per client.

Track scores in a simple sheet (or a Supabase client_health column). Watch the trend — a drop from 11 to 7 matters more than the absolute number.

Any single red signal triggers a touch, even if the total is green. A late payment or a complaint never waits for the next scheduled call.

Review the board every Friday in your weekly ritual. Two minutes of prevention beats a month of lost MRR.

The Silent Churn Trap

Most clients don’t cancel because they’re angry — they cancel because they forgot why they’re paying you. A client at score 6 who’s never complained is more dangerous than one who calls to vent. The scorecard catches the quiet ones.

The Referral Program

Structure: $250 credit on their next invoice for every referral that becomes a paying client. No limit.

When to ask: Only after Month 2 (they need to be happy first). Ask during the monthly report call when the numbers look good.

How to ask: "You know how we caught [X] calls for you last month? I'd love to do the same for other contractors. Do you know anyone who's still losing calls to voicemail? I'll knock $250 off your next month for any intro."

Expected results: Happy clients refer 1-2 people per quarter. At 10 clients, that's 3-5 warm referrals per quarter — the easiest closes you'll ever make.

The Monthly Client Report (Automated)

Build this as an n8n workflow that runs on the 1st of every month. Send via email and text.

MONTHLY REPORT TEMPLATE Subject: [COMPANY NAME] — AI Agent Performance: [MONTH] Hey [FIRST NAME], Here's how your AI agent performed in [MONTH]: CALLS & LEADS Calls answered: [X] After-hours calls: [Y] (these would've been voicemails) Appointments booked: [Z] Leads captured: [W] ESTIMATED IMPACT Revenue protected: $[AMOUNT] (based on [Z] appointments x your avg job value) Missed calls saved: [Y] calls that went to AI instead of voicemail TOP INSIGHT [One specific finding — e.g., "43% of your calls come between 5-8pm when your office is closed. Your AI agent is capturing all of them."] Want to discuss your results or explore additional features? Reply to this email or call me anytime. — Paola, Colibri Code

Monthly Review Call Script (Day 30 / 60 / 90)

This is the call that keeps clients. Reports prove value; the call proves you care. Paola leads; Mike listens in on Day 30 in case there are technical questions. Keep it to 15 minutes.

MONTHLY REVIEW CALL — SCRIPT [Before the call: pull their report numbers. Know them cold.] OPENING (1 min) "Hey [NAME], thanks for hopping on. I just want to walk you through last month's numbers and see how everything's going on your end. Should take about 15 minutes." RESULTS WALK-THROUGH (5 min) "So here's what your agent did in [MONTH]: - Answered [X] total calls - [Y] of those were after hours — calls that would've gone to voicemail before - Booked [Z] appointments automatically - Captured [W] new leads Based on your average job value of $[AVG], that's roughly $[REVENUE] in revenue your agent helped protect." [Pause. Let them react. They usually say "wow" here.] FEEDBACK CHECK (3 min) "Have you noticed anything that didn't sound right, or any calls where the agent could've done better?" [If they have feedback — write it down, promise to fix it this week. If not: "That's great to hear."] "Are your customers saying anything about it? Any feedback from your team?" HEALTH CHECK (2 min) "Just a couple quick things: - Is the notification system working well for you? Getting texts/emails promptly? - Any services you've added or seasonal changes coming up that we should update the agent for?" [Update the agent if needed after the call.] EXPANSION (2 min — Day 60+ only, skip on Day 30) "One thing I noticed in your data: [SPECIFIC OBSERVATION]. [Pick ONE that matches their situation:] - "You're getting a lot of after-hours calls. Have you thought about adding text follow-ups for those callers?" - "I see about [X]% of your calls are in Spanish. We can add a bilingual agent for those — same price." - "You've got [X] past customers in the database. Want us to run a reactivation campaign before [SEASON]?" No pressure at all — just something to think about." CLOSE (2 min) "Anything else on your mind? ... Great. I'll send you the full report by email today. We'll check in again next month. Oh, and one more thing — if you know any other [TRADE] owners who are still losing calls to voicemail, I'd love an intro. We'll knock $250 off your next invoice for anyone who signs up. Thanks [NAME], talk soon!"

Timing tip: Schedule review calls on Tuesdays or Wednesdays, 9–11am in the client’s timezone. Mondays are hectic, Fridays people check out. Send a calendar invite with a 15-min block the week before so they don’t forget.

Client Offboarding: When a Client Leaves

Not every client stays forever. A professional exit protects your reputation and often leads to referrals or re-sign-ups later. Today’s cancellation is tomorrow’s referral source.

30-Day Offboarding Checklist

Day 1: Acknowledge the cancellation graciously. Call them (don’t text). “We understand, and we appreciate you being a client.”

Day 1-3: Schedule a brief exit call to understand why they’re leaving. This is for learning, not saving.

Day 3-5: Remove call forwarding from their phone system back to their original setup.

Day 5: Deactivate their Vapi agent (don’t delete yet — keep for 30 days in case they come back).

Day 5: Release their Twilio number, or port it to them if they request.

Day 7: Export their call data from Supabase as CSV and send to them.

Day 7: Send final invoice for any outstanding balance via Stripe.

Day 10: Deactivate their n8n workflows (don’t delete — you may reuse the templates).

Day 30: Send goodbye email leaving the door open.

Day 90: Delete their customer data from Supabase per your contract’s data retention policy.

Goodbye Email Template

Subject: Thanks for working with us, [FIRST NAME] Hi [FIRST NAME], I wanted to personally thank you for being a Colibri Code client. We've enjoyed working with [BUSINESS NAME] and wish you all the best. A few things for your records: - Your call data export is attached (CSV) - Your Twilio number [NUMBER] has been released / ported back to you - All your data will be securely deleted from our systems in 90 days If you ever need AI phone support again — whether it's next month or next year — we'd love to have you back. No hard feelings, no awkward re-onboarding. Just reach out. In the meantime, if you know any other [TRADE] companies struggling with missed calls, we'd really appreciate an introduction. Happy to offer them a free trial. Wishing you a great rest of the year, [YOUR NAME] Colibri Code

Exit Survey (3 Quick Questions)

Ask these on the exit call. Track the answers — patterns reveal what to fix.

1. “What was the main reason you decided to cancel?” (cost, quality, no longer needed, switching providers, business change)

2. “Was there anything we could have done differently?”

3. “Would you recommend us to another contractor? If so, can I ask who?”

The Save Attempt (Before Offboarding Starts)

Before you accept the cancellation, offer one save play: a free month, a lower tier, or a pause. If they decline, accept gracefully. Never beg or guilt-trip — contractors talk to each other, and your reputation matters more than one month’s revenue.

Knowledge Check Module 7 Quiz

A client's health scorecard drops from 10 to 6 over two months. They haven't complained. What should you do?

Exactly. Most churn is silent — clients don't cancel because they're angry, they cancel because they forgot why they're paying. A score drop from 10 to 6 means something changed. Call now, diagnose the issue, and fix it before they cancel.
Waiting lets the problem compound, and unsolicited discounts signal weakness. The right move is a proactive call: "Hey, I noticed [specific signal]. What's going on?" Catching a drop early saves the client. Waiting until they cancel is too late.

Once you're past the setup phase (Month 2+), these recurring actions keep the machine running. Pin this somewhere visible.

The Non-Negotiable

The 3-5pm CET sales window is sacred. Protect it. No tech work, no admin, no meetings that aren’t with prospects or clients. This 2-hour block is where revenue happens. Everything else supports it.

Monthly Rituals

1st of month: Send automated monthly reports to all clients (n8n workflow pulls from Supabase, formats, emails)

1st of month: Review P&L — revenue, costs, profit, per-person split. Update your financial tracker.

5th of month: Follow up on any unpaid invoices. Stripe handles most of this automatically.

10th of month: Review each client’s call data. Any agent scripts need updating? Any new FAQ patterns?

15th of month: Quarterly tax estimate payment (Apr/Jun/Sep/Jan). Set calendar reminders.

Last week: Plan next month’s outreach campaigns. New cities? New sub-niches? New email angles?

Communication Tools

How you stay in sync as a team and communicate with clients:

Between Mike & Paola: WhatsApp or Slack. Quick async updates. Daily 10-min standup at 8am CET — “what I’m working on, what I need from you, any blockers.”

With clients: Email for formal communication. Text/SMS for urgent issues. Monthly report email on the 1st. Quarterly video call for retention.

Project tracking: A simple Google Sheet or Notion board. Columns: Client Name, Status, MRR, Add-ons, Next Action, Last Contact Date. Don’t overthink this — a spreadsheet works until 15+ clients.

Task management: Todoist (free) or a shared Google Keep list. Each Monday morning, both write down top 3 priorities for the week.

Mindset: What to Expect

The Hard Parts (Be Ready)

• Week 1-2: Setup feels overwhelming. So many accounts and tools. This is normal.

• Week 3-4: Cold outreach feels uncomfortable. Rejection hurts. Every successful agency went through this.

• Month 2: Imposter syndrome hits. “Who am I to sell this?” You’re someone solving a $45K problem.

• Client #1: Something will break. A call will go weird. Fix it fast and they’ll respect you more.

• Month 3-4: Growth feels slow. Compound growth kicks in around month 4-5.

The Wins to Look Forward To

• First demo call where the prospect says “wow” when they hear the AI

• First Stripe notification: “You received $2,500”

• First client saying “my guys love it — they don’t have to answer the phone anymore”

• Month where recurring revenue exceeds your tool costs by 10x

• First referral from a happy client (you didn’t even have to sell)

• The day you realize this is a real business, not a side project

When Things Go Wrong (And They Will)

Here’s exactly what to do for the 5 most common emergencies. Save this section — you’ll need it.

AI agent says something wrong to a caller

Immediate: Listen to the recording. Identify the exact prompt issue.

Fix: Update the Vapi system prompt to handle that scenario. Test 5 times.

Communicate: Text the client: “We caught an issue on a call and already fixed it. Here’s what happened and what we changed. Won’t happen again.” Proactive transparency builds trust.

n8n or VPS goes down

Immediate: Calls still ring (Vapi handles them), but notifications and logging stop.

Fix: Log into Hetzner console → restart the server. SSH in, run docker-compose up -d. Usually takes 2-5 minutes.

Prevent: Set up UptimeRobot (free, 5-minute checks) to ping your n8n URL. Get email/SMS alerts when it goes down.

Client wants to cancel

Immediate: Call them (don’t text). Ask: “Help me understand what’s not working.” Listen.

Save plays: (1) Offer a free month. (2) Add a free add-on. (3) Reduce to a lower tier instead of full cancel. (4) Pause for 1 month instead of cancel.

If they still cancel: Be gracious. Remove their agent. Send a closing email with their data. Leave the door open: “If things change, we’re here.” They may come back. Or refer someone.

Vapi has an outage

Immediate: Calls should auto-forward to client’s phone (your Twilio fallback). If not set up, configure it NOW.

Communicate: Text affected clients: “Our AI provider is experiencing a brief outage. Calls are forwarding to your phone as a backup. We’ll notify you when it’s restored.”

Monitor: Check status.vapi.ai and Vapi Discord for updates.

A client’s customer complains about “talking to a robot”

Reframe: “Would they prefer to leave a voicemail that never gets returned? The AI ensures every caller gets helped immediately.”

Fix: Listen to the call. Often the issue is a specific phrase or tone. Adjust the prompt to be more natural for that scenario.

Option: Add a “transfer to human” option: “If you’d prefer to speak to someone directly, I can transfer you now.”

Responding to an Angry Client

When a client is upset, follow this 4-step framework:

1. Acknowledge

“I completely understand your frustration. That’s not the experience we want you to have.”

2. Apologize (specifically)

“I’m sorry that [specific thing] happened. That’s on us.”

3. Fix (with a timeline)

“Here’s what I’m doing right now to fix it: [specific action]. It will be resolved by [time].”

4. Follow up (next day)

Text them the next morning: “Hey [Name], just checking in — is everything working well now? Let me know if anything else comes up.”

The Golden Rule of Client Communication

Never let a client hear about a problem from a caller. You should always be the one to tell them first. Proactive transparency builds trust. “Hey, we caught an issue and already fixed it” is 10x better than “My customer told me your AI said something weird.”

Financial Tools & Tracking

Stripe Dashboard: Your real-time revenue tracker. Set up automatic invoicing so you never chase payments manually.

Google Sheets P&L: Simple monthly spreadsheet. Columns: Revenue (setup + recurring), Tool Costs, VA Costs, Profit, Tax Reserve (25%), Take-Home. Update on the 1st of each month.

Mercury or Relay Bank: Free business banking designed for online businesses. Separate from personal accounts. Set up auto-transfers: 25% to tax savings, 75% to operating.

Wise: For paying your Colombian VA. $3 flat fee per transfer. Better rates than PayPal or bank wire.

QuickBooks Self-Employed: $15/mo. Connect to your bank, auto-categorize expenses, generate tax reports. Worth it by month 4+. Your CPA will love you for this.

Stripe Setup & Recurring Billing

Stripe is your payment backbone. Set it up once and every client gets professional invoicing with automatic recurring charges. No chasing checks.

Initial Stripe Configuration

Create Stripe account at stripe.com under Colibri Code LLC. Use your EIN, US business address (registered agent), and Mercury bank for payouts.

Set payout schedule to weekly (Settings → Payouts → Payout Schedule). Daily creates noise; monthly leaves you cash-strapped.

Enable Stripe Tax (Products → Tax). Wyoming has no state income tax, but you still need to track revenue for federal. Stripe auto-generates 1099 data.

Add your branding: Logo, brand color, support email (support@colibricode.com). This shows on all invoices and the customer portal.

Enable the Customer Portal (Settings → Customer Portal). Clients can update their own card info when it expires — saves you a support ticket.

Per-Client Billing Setup

Create a Product for each rung of the pricing ladder: “Founding Client ($497/mo)”, “Starter ($500/mo)”, “Never Miss a Call Bundle ($1,000/mo)”, “Scale ($1,500/mo)”. When you raise prices, create the higher rates ($800 and $1,200) as separate products — never edit an existing product’s price, or you will re-bill every grandfathered client.

Send a one-time Invoice for the setup fee. Invoices → Create Invoice → add client email → add setup fee line item → Send. They pay with a link.

Create a Subscription for the monthly retainer. Subscriptions → Create → select customer → select product → set billing anchor to the 1st of month. Start date = go-live date.

Enable Smart Retries (Settings → Subscriptions → Manage Failed Payments → Smart Retries ON). Stripe will automatically retry failed charges 3 times over 7 days before marking it failed.

Set dunning emails (Settings → Subscriptions → Manage Failed Payments → Send Emails ON). Stripe emails the client automatically when their card fails. This handles 80% of payment issues without you doing anything.

Failed Payment Automation (n8n)

Stripe’s built-in dunning handles most cases, but for clients who still haven’t paid after retries, automate your escalation.

Webhook trigger: In n8n, create a webhook node listening to Stripe event invoice.payment_failed. Stripe sends this every time a charge fails.

Day 1 (auto): Stripe retries + sends dunning email. You do nothing.

Day 5 (n8n): If still unpaid, n8n sends Paola a Slack/SMS alert: “[Client Name] payment failed 5 days ago. Card on file: ending [XXXX]. Action needed.”

Day 10 (Paola): Personal text to client using the late-payment templates from the Client Communications section.

Day 15 (both): Service pause per your contract terms. See the Client Comms templates for exact wording.

Stripe Fees to Know

2.9% + $0.30 per successful charge. On a $1,000/mo client, that’s $29.30/mo to Stripe. On $10K MRR, you’re paying ~$293/mo in processing fees. This is already factored into the P&L projections above. Never eat the fee — it’s a cost of doing business, not a discount to the client.

Monthly Bookkeeping Workflow

A simple monthly financial routine that takes 30 minutes and keeps your business healthy. Do this on the 1st of every month — put it in your calendar as a recurring event.

Step-by-Step Monthly Bookkeeping (1st of Month)

Step 1: Download your Stripe payout report for last month (Stripe → Payments → All Transactions → Export CSV). This is your revenue.

Step 2: Log all tool subscriptions from email receipts — Vapi, Twilio, Hetzner, Smartlead, Google Workspace, Resend, domains, any paid tools. This is your cost.

Step 3: Log any VA payments (Wise transfer receipts).

Step 4: Calculate: Revenue − Tool Costs − VA Costs = Gross Profit.

Step 5: Transfer 25% of gross profit to your tax savings account immediately. Don’t touch this money.

Step 6: Split the remaining 75% between partners per your agreement.

Step 7: Update your P&L spreadsheet (see template below).

5th of Month: Reconciliation

Verify bank balance matches expected amount (Stripe payouts − expenses).

Follow up on any unpaid client invoices. Stripe auto-retries failed payments, but check manually.

Confirm all recurring Stripe subscriptions are active (no failed cards).

Tax Filing Reminders (US LLC)

Quarterly estimated taxes: Due January 15, April 15, June 15, September 15. Pay 25% of the previous quarter’s profit. Use IRS Direct Pay or mail Form 1040-ES.

Annual filing: Form 1065 (partnership) or Schedule C (single-member LLC) due April 15. Use a CPA — it’s worth $300-500 for the peace of mind and deductions they’ll find.

Wyoming annual report: Due on your LLC anniversary month. $60 fee. File online at the Wyoming Secretary of State website.

SOFA note (read Module 2 before relying on this): NATO SOFA Article X exempts Mike’s government salary from German tax — it does not automatically exempt business income. Article X contains an explicit carve-out allowing Germany to tax “any profitable enterprise other than his employment.” Treat agency profit as potentially German-taxable, keep documentation of SOFA status, and get advice from a tax professional who handles both US and German returns before your first profitable year. Do not treat this course — or the shorter note that used to sit here — as tax advice.

Automation Opportunity

By month 4, you can automate most of this: Stripe webhooks → n8n workflow → log transactions to a Google Sheet automatically. The only manual step becomes the bank reconciliation and tax transfer. Build it once, run it forever.

FAQ & Handling Objections

What prospects will ask, and exactly what to say.

"Can the AI handle complex questions?"

"It handles 80-90% of calls perfectly — scheduling, service inquiries, hours, pricing questions. For anything outside its script, it takes a detailed message and sends it to you immediately. It's like having a really reliable receptionist who never misses a call and always takes perfect messages."

"What if the customer wants to talk to a real person?"

"The agent can transfer to your cell phone or any number during business hours. After hours, it lets them know you'll call back first thing in the morning and captures all their info. The key is: instead of getting voicemail and calling your competitor, they get a helpful interaction and a confirmation text."

"That's too expensive."

"I understand. Let me ask — how much is a single HVAC job worth? [$3,000-10,000]. If this saves you even one missed call a month, it pays for itself multiple times over. A part-time receptionist costs $2,000-3,000/month and only works 20 hours. This works 24/7/365 for a fraction of that."

"I need to think about it."

"Totally fair. While you think about it, how many calls do you think you'll miss this week? I ask because every missed call is potentially $3,000+ walking to a competitor. How about this — I'll set up a free 1-week trial so you can see exactly how many calls it captures. If you don't see the value, no hard feelings."

"My customers won't want to talk to an AI."

"That's the most common concern, and here's what we've found: customers prefer getting their problem solved immediately over leaving a voicemail that may or may not get returned. The AI sounds natural, is polite, and most callers don't even realize it's AI — they just know they got helped. Let me call the demo number right now so you can hear for yourself."

"I already have an answering service."

"How much do you pay for that? [Usually $200-500/month]. What do they actually do — just take a message? Our AI does everything they do plus: books appointments directly, sends the customer a confirmation text, follows up if they don't book, and requests a Google review after the job. And it picks up in under a second — no hold music, no transfers, no 'please hold while I find someone.'"

"What if something goes wrong?"

"We monitor every agent 24/7. If anything goes down, we get an alert before you do and fix it immediately. Plus, you can always set a backup: if the AI doesn't answer for any reason, calls automatically forward to your personal phone. You're never worse off than you are today."

"I already have a receptionist."

"That's great — and I'd never replace a good receptionist. But what happens when she's on lunch? On another call? After 5pm? On weekends? Our AI handles the 30-40% of calls your receptionist can't get to. Think of it as backup that never takes a day off. Most of our clients keep their receptionist AND add the AI."

"I don't trust AI / technology."

"I totally get that. Here's the thing — this isn't ChatGPT on a phone. It's a purpose-built agent trained specifically for [HVAC/plumbing]. It knows what a 'no cool' call means. It knows your service area. And if anything ever seems off, calls can instantly forward to your cell phone as a safety net. Zero risk. Want to hear it handle a call right now?"

"I'm too busy to set this up."

"That's literally why you need this — you're so busy you can't answer calls, which means you're losing jobs. Here's the good news: YOU do nothing. We handle 100% of the setup. I just need 5 minutes of your time to fill out a short form — your business hours, services, service area. We do the rest. Your agent is live in 48 hours."

"Can I do this myself?"

"You could, the same way you could do your own taxes or build your own website. The tools exist. But our clients hire us because they're plumbers, not AI engineers. We handle the tech, the maintenance, the monitoring, and the optimization. You focus on running jobs. When was the last time you had free hours to learn a new tech platform?"

"My buddy tried AI phone stuff and it was terrible."

"AI has gotten dramatically better in the last 12 months. The early stuff WAS bad — robotic voices, couldn't handle real conversations. What we use now is a different universe. Rather than take my word for it, call this number right now: [DEMO NUMBER]. Pretend you're a customer with a broken AC. Then tell me if it sounds terrible."

"What happens when my slow season hits and I don't need it?"

"Two things: First, slow season is actually when you need EVERY call — you can't afford to miss any when they're scarce. Second, we're month-to-month. No contracts. If you ever want to pause, just let us know with 30 days notice. But honestly? Our clients who've been through a slow season say the AI paid for itself even more because it caught the calls they desperately needed."

Common Mistakes & Lean Launch Budget

Avoid these pitfalls, and see exactly how lean you can launch.

Common Mistakes New Agency Owners Make

Every new agency makes these. Read this list now, bookmark it, and re-read it monthly.

1. Building for 6 months before selling anything

You’ll never feel “ready.” The agent doesn’t need to be perfect — it needs to be better than voicemail. Start selling in Week 3. Fix issues as they come up. The first client teaches you more than 100 hours of building alone.

2. Underpricing because you feel like a beginner

$500/mo is already cheap compared to alternatives (see the competitor pricing table). Don’t go below $500/mo for the core phone agent. If you charge $200/mo, you need 50 clients to make $10K. At $1,000/mo, you need 10. Price for 10.

3. Spending $500+/month on tools before having clients

You do NOT need GoHighLevel ($97/mo), LinkedIn Sales Navigator ($99/mo), Clay ($149/mo), or PhoneBurner ($149/mo) in Month 1. Start with the ultra-lean stack ($16-46). Add tools only when a specific bottleneck demands it.

4. Trying to serve every industry at once

Pick HVAC + Plumbing. Get 5-10 clients. Build case studies. Then expand to electrical, roofing, etc. A case study saying “we helped 8 HVAC companies” is 10x more powerful than “we serve all businesses.”

5. Not setting boundaries with clients

Contractors will text you at 11pm asking for changes. Set expectations from Day 1: “Support hours are 9am-5pm ET. Emergencies (agent down) = we respond within 1 hour anytime. Feature requests = addressed within 48 hours.” Put this in your contract.

6. Forgetting to ask for referrals and reviews

At the 30-day mark, every happy client should be asked: “Know any other contractors who miss calls?” and “Would you mind leaving us a Google review?” Put these in your calendar as recurring tasks. Referrals are your cheapest client acquisition channel.

7. Not monitoring the first 72 hours obsessively

Listen to EVERY call recording for the first 3 days after a client goes live. The AI will say something weird — guaranteed. Catch it before the client does. After 72 hours of clean calls, you can relax to spot-checking.

8. Getting discouraged after 2 weeks of no responses

Cold outreach is a numbers game. Your first 500 emails might get 5 replies and 0 clients. That’s normal. It takes most agencies 4-8 weeks to close Client #1. Keep going. The emails compound — someone who ignores Email 1 might reply to Email 3. Someone who says “not now” might come back in 60 days. Consistency beats talent.

Internal FAQ (For You Two)

"Do we need an LLC?"

You already have one — Colibri Code LLC. All client contracts and invoices go through it. Consider filing a DBA if you want a separate agency brand name. See the Business Setup section for banking, insurance, and tax details.

"What if n8n or Vapi goes down?"

Set up monitoring (Mike builds this in Week 2). If your VPS goes down, restart it — takes 2 minutes via Hetzner dashboard. If Vapi has an outage, calls forward to the client's personal phone as backup. In 2+ years of operation, major outages are rare. Just have the fallback configured.

"What about client contracts?"

Use a simple service agreement. Google "SaaS service agreement template" and customize. Key terms: month-to-month (no long-term contracts — reduces friction), 30-day cancellation notice, setup fee non-refundable, you own the technology. Keep it to 1-2 pages.

"What if we get more clients than we can handle?"

Good problem. Each new client takes ~4-6 hours to onboard (after your first few). Ongoing maintenance is ~2 hours/client/month. At 20 clients = 40 hours/month of maintenance. That's very manageable for 2 people. Beyond 20, tap into Paola's Colombian VA pipeline — bilingual VAs at $8-15/hr on US Eastern Time. See Advantage 4.

01 — Vapi System Prompt (Production)

Paste this into Vapi → Assistants → System Prompt. Replace the bracketed values with client details.

You are the AI receptionist for [CLIENT_BUSINESS_NAME], a [TRADE_TYPE] company in [CITY, STATE]. IDENTITY: - Your name is [AGENT_NAME] (e.g., "Sarah") - You work for [CLIENT_BUSINESS_NAME] - You sound friendly, professional, and confident — never robotic - You speak English. If the caller speaks Spanish, switch to Spanish seamlessly. CORE TASK: Answer incoming calls, determine what the caller needs, and book an appointment or collect a message. GREETING: "Thanks for calling [CLIENT_BUSINESS_NAME], this is [AGENT_NAME]. How can I help you today?" CALL FLOW: 1. Greet the caller warmly 2. Ask what service they need 3. Collect: caller name, phone number, address, brief description of the issue 4. If EMERGENCY (gas leak, flooding, no heat in winter, electrical fire): - Say: "That sounds urgent. Let me connect you with [OWNER_NAME] right now." - Transfer to [OWNER_PHONE] 5. If ROUTINE (maintenance, quote, non-urgent repair): - Book an appointment using the calendar tool - Confirm date, time, and service needed - Say: "You're all set! [CLIENT_BUSINESS_NAME] will see you on [DATE] at [TIME]." 6. If AFTER-HOURS or no slots available: - Collect their info and say: "I'll have [OWNER_NAME] call you back first thing tomorrow morning." - Save the message via the webhook TRANSFER RULES: - Transfer to [OWNER_PHONE] ONLY for: emergencies, existing customer complaints, price negotiations, or if the caller explicitly asks for a human - Never transfer for: scheduling, general questions, service inquiries, hours/directions INFORMATION YOU KNOW: - Business hours: [HOURS, e.g., "Monday-Friday 7AM-6PM, Saturday 8AM-2PM"] - Services offered: [LIST_SERVICES] - Service area: [COVERAGE_AREA] - Typical response time: [e.g., "same-day for emergencies, 1-2 days for routine"] RULES: - Never make up prices. Say: "Pricing depends on the specific job. We can give you an exact quote at the appointment." - Never diagnose problems. Say: "Our technician will take a look and let you know exactly what's going on." - If asked about competitors, stay neutral: "I can only speak to our services, but I'm happy to help you get scheduled." - Keep responses under 2 sentences when possible. Be concise. - Always confirm the spelling of their name and repeat the phone number back.

03 — Supabase Schema (SQL)

Supabase → SQL Editor → New Query → paste → Run. Creates all tables for multi-tenant call tracking.

-- ============================================= -- Colibri Code Agency — Supabase Schema -- Run this in: Supabase → SQL Editor → New Query -- ============================================= -- Clients table (one row per paying client) CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clients ( id UUID DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY, business_name TEXT NOT NULL, owner_name TEXT NOT NULL, owner_phone TEXT NOT NULL, owner_email TEXT, trade_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'HVAC', twilio_number TEXT, vapi_assistant_id TEXT, plan TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'starter' CHECK (plan IN ('starter','growth','premium')), mrr INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','paused','churned')), onboarded_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() ); -- Calls table (every AI-handled call) CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS calls ( id UUID DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY, client_id UUID REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, caller_phone TEXT NOT NULL, caller_name TEXT, summary TEXT, transcript TEXT, call_duration INTEGER DEFAULT 0, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'completed' CHECK (status IN ('completed','transferred','voicemail','missed','booked','needs_followup')), appointment_date TIMESTAMPTZ, follow_up_sent BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE, vapi_call_id TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() ); -- Messages table (SMS sent/received) CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages ( id UUID DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY, client_id UUID REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, direction TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (direction IN ('inbound','outbound')), to_number TEXT NOT NULL, from_number TEXT NOT NULL, body TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT DEFAULT 'sent', created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() ); -- Monthly reports (auto-generated stats per client) CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS monthly_reports ( id UUID DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY, client_id UUID REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, month DATE NOT NULL, total_calls INTEGER DEFAULT 0, appointments_booked INTEGER DEFAULT 0, calls_transferred INTEGER DEFAULT 0, avg_call_duration INTEGER DEFAULT 0, follow_ups_sent INTEGER DEFAULT 0, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), UNIQUE(client_id, month) ); -- Row Level Security (RLS) — isolate client data ALTER TABLE calls ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ALTER TABLE messages ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ALTER TABLE monthly_reports ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; -- Index for fast lookups CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_calls_client ON calls(client_id, created_at DESC); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_calls_phone ON calls(caller_phone); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_messages_client ON messages(client_id, created_at DESC); -- View: Dashboard stats per client (use in n8n reports) CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW client_stats AS SELECT c.id AS client_id, c.business_name, COUNT(cl.id) AS total_calls, COUNT(CASE WHEN cl.status = 'booked' THEN 1 END) AS appointments, COUNT(CASE WHEN cl.status = 'transferred' THEN 1 END) AS transfers, ROUND(AVG(cl.call_duration)) AS avg_duration_sec FROM clients c LEFT JOIN calls cl ON cl.client_id = c.id AND cl.created_at >= DATE_TRUNC('month', NOW()) GROUP BY c.id, c.business_name;

Knowledge Check Module 8 Quiz

A client's Stripe payment fails. Smart Retries don't recover it after 7 days. What's the correct escalation order?

Right. The graduated approach (friendly → firm → pause) preserves the relationship while protecting your revenue. Jumping to a pause burns trust. Waiting too long teaches clients they can pay whenever. The 5-10-15 cadence is the sweet spot — see the Client Comms section for word-for-word templates.
Immediate pauses damage relationships, and passive waiting trains clients to pay late. The right pattern is a graduated escalation: friendly text (Day 5), firm follow-up (Day 10), then service pause with written notice (Day 15). Each step uses the templates from the Client Communications section.

Common Questions

Do I need technical skills?

No coding required. Everything uses no-code/low-code tools (n8n, Vapi, Supabase). If you can use a spreadsheet, you can do this. We provide copy-paste templates for everything technical.

How much does it cost to get started?

As little as $16/month (domain + VPS + Twilio). The ultra-lean budget in Module 2 shows how to launch for under $20. Full setup with all tools is about $200/month, but you can start lean and upgrade as you get clients.

Can I do this part-time?

The entire plan is designed for part-time (7-10 hours/week). The AI handles calls 24/7 — you just build, sell, and manage. The time zone section in Module 1 shows how to optimize your hours from any location.

What if I'm not bilingual?

Bilingual is a bonus, not a requirement. English-only AI agents are the standard product. You can still target the massive English-speaking contractor market and make great money. The bilingual sections show how to add it later if you hire a Spanish-speaking VA.

How long until I get my first client?

Typical timeline: Week 1-2 setup, Week 3-4 outreach starts, Week 4-8 first client closes. Conservative estimate is 6-8 weeks. Fastest students close in Week 3-4 because the Missed Call Audit creates immediate urgency.

Is the home services market saturated?

There are 3.5+ million home service businesses in the US. Only ~25% of residential contractors use AI at all (ServiceTitan, 2026). The market is barely started. Even in competitive metros, there are thousands of businesses per city with no AI solution. Module 7 covers exactly how to position against competitors.

Glossary of Key Terms

Quick reference for terms used throughout this course. Bookmark this page.

A2P 10DLC

Application-to-Person 10-Digit Long Code. US carrier requirement for business SMS. You must register your brand and campaign before sending texts from a regular phone number.

ARPU

Average Revenue Per User (client). Your monthly revenue divided by number of clients. Target: $800-$1,500/month.

Agentic AI

AI that reasons, plans, and takes multi-step actions autonomously using tools. Unlike reactive AI (responds to input), agentic AI decides what to do next on its own. Premium tier product.

CAC

Customer Acquisition Cost. How much it costs to get one new client. Your target: under $400 hard cost, or under $1,200 once you count your own time at $50/hr (see The Four Numbers in Module 7)

CRM

Customer Relationship Management. Software to track leads and client interactions. You use Supabase (free) or GoHighLevel ($97-$297/mo).

Cold Email Warmup

Process of gradually building reputation for new email domains. Send small volumes of "good" emails for 2 weeks before outreach. Tools: Smartlead auto-warmup.

DBR (Database Reactivation)

AI-powered SMS campaign to a business’s dormant customer list. Re-engages past customers who haven’t booked in 6-12+ months. A zero-risk front-door offer to land new clients. See Database Reactivation.

Discovery Call

A 20-30 minute call with a prospect to understand their business, pain points, and qualify them. This is where you diagnose their problem before prescribing your solution.

GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)

Getting a client’s business recommended by AI search engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews). The 2026 evolution of SEO. See AI Search Visibility.

GHL (GoHighLevel)

All-in-one CRM and marketing platform popular with agencies. $97-$497/mo. Optional — you can start without it using Supabase + n8n. See GHL section and Voice Platforms comparison.

IVR

Interactive Voice Response. The old "Press 1 for sales, press 2 for support" phone trees. What we replace with natural AI conversation.

LTV

Lifetime Value. Total revenue from a client over their entire relationship. At $1,000/mo with 18-month average retention = $18,000 LTV.

MCP (Model Context Protocol)

Open standard (now under Linux Foundation) that lets AI models connect to external tools — databases, APIs, calendars — through a universal interface. Like USB-C for AI. Enables the agentic workflows you sell. See Agentic AI.

MRR

Monthly Recurring Revenue. Your predictable monthly income from all active client subscriptions.

Missed Call Audit

Your proprietary sales tool. Call a prospect's business, let it ring, and use the experience (voicemail, no answer) as proof they need your service. Detailed in Module 5.

n8n

Open-source workflow automation tool (like Zapier, but self-hosted and free). Your central automation hub connecting Vapi, Twilio, Supabase, and everything else.

RLS (Row Level Security)

Supabase/PostgreSQL feature that restricts data access per user. Ensures Client A can't see Client B's data.

SIP Trunk

Session Initiation Protocol trunk. How Vapi connects to Twilio to make/receive calls over the internet instead of traditional phone lines.

SOFA

Status of Forces Agreement. NATO agreement covering US military personnel stationed abroad. Relevant for tax implications if you're military overseas.

Supabase

Open-source Firebase alternative with PostgreSQL database, auth, and APIs. Free tier handles your first 10+ clients easily.

TTS / STT

Text-to-Speech / Speech-to-Text. TTS converts AI responses to spoken audio. STT transcribes caller speech to text. Vapi handles both.

Vapi

Voice AI platform that powers your phone agents. Handles TTS, STT, conversation management, and tool calling. Your core product delivery tool.

Webhook

An HTTP callback — when something happens in one tool, it automatically sends data to another. Example: Vapi call ends → webhook sends call data to n8n.

9

Use AI to build your tools, fill your pipeline, and run your back office — so two part-time people operate like a team of ten.

🚨 The Golden Rule of AI Leverage

AI builds and assists; a human reviews anything that touches money, client call-routing, or credentials. You sell reliability — never let an autonomous agent ship to a client's live phone system unattended, and never hand your Vapi/Twilio/Supabase API keys to a tool you don't fully control. Use AI to go fast on everything except the few things where a mistake reaches a paying client.

Lesson 2: Find & Get Clients with AI

Your ideal customer is unusually easy to find: every home-service business is on Google Maps with a public name, phone, website, category, and — critically — reviews that often complain about missed calls. You do not need expensive databases like ZoomInfo. The winning stack for a tiny team is cheap and mostly automated.

The Pipeline in One Line

Outscraper (pull the list) → Claude (mine reviews for missed-call complaints + write a personalized first line) → Instantly/Smartlead (send + warm up inboxes) → Twilio Missed Call Audit (undeniable proof) → human demo call. All-in: roughly $130–260/month plus pennies per lead.

Lead Data: Where to Get the List

The Best Signal: Reviews That Mention Missed Calls

Reviews are a goldmine. Phrases like "couldn't reach them," "no answer," "didn't call back," "left a voicemail" are direct proof of the exact problem you solve — and a quotable hook for your email. Scrape reviews, then run Claude over them to flag and quote the complaints.

Other high-fit signals you can detect for free

Low review-response rate (owner ignores reviews = understaffed on comms)

No website / no online booking / no listed hours

Hiring a receptionist or dispatcher (job posting = pain + budget)

Running Google Local Services Ads (every missed call wastes ad spend)

Closes at 5pm (misses all evening emergency calls)

High review count but slow responses (busy + overwhelmed)

The Automated Missed Call Audit (Your Sharpest Weapon)

Call a list of prospects, detect whether a human answers vs. voicemail, log the result, then open your outreach with: "We called your main line 3 times last Tuesday — twice it went to voicemail. Here's what that's costing you." This is buildable for pennies with Twilio's Answering Machine Detection (AMD).

  1. n8n triggers Twilio to dial a prospect's main number during business hours.
  2. Twilio AMD classifies the pickup: human, machine_start (voicemail), or no-answer (~94% accuracy, ~$0.0075 per answered call).
  3. Hang up immediately and log the result to Supabase. You never play audio or run a bot — it's a connectivity test, which keeps you clear of robocall rules.
  4. Prospects that missed your calls go to the top of your outreach list with their result quoted in the email.

Auditing 1,000 prospects costs roughly $15 total and produces hyper-specific proof. Respect calling windows (8am–9pm local), don't hammer the same number, and target main business lines, not personal cells.

⚠️ Legal: Do NOT use AI voice to cold-call prospects

In February 2024 the FCC ruled AI-generated voices are "artificial voices" under the TCPA. Cold-calling prospects with an AI voice requires prior written consent you don't have — penalties run $500–$1,500 per call. State "mini-TCPA" laws add more risk. Keep AI voice for inbound (your product) and consented calls only.

Compliant prospecting channels: cold email (legal under CAN-SPAM for B2B with truthful headers, a physical address, and a working opt-out), human-dialed follow-ups to business landlines, and the hang-up Missed Call Audit (measurement only, no message delivered).

Skip the Expensive "AI SDR" Agents

Autonomous "AI SDR" platforms (Artisan's Ava ~$2,000/mo+, 11x's Alice ~$5,000/mo) are built for funded teams, lock you into annual contracts, and reviewers say their personalization reads generic on niche local trades. A hand-tuned Claude + Instantly/Smartlead flow gets ~90% of the value for under $200/mo with full control. Don't buy an AI SDR.

Per-lead cost reality check: the DIY Claude-on-Outscraper-reviews route runs about $0.003–$0.01 per lead. Clay (when you scale) runs ~$0.14–$0.16/lead all-in — and you can cut its AI cost to near zero by plugging in your own Claude API key.

Lesson 4: Autonomous AI Agents — Hermes, OpenClaw & Your Back Office

"Autonomous agents" are AI that don't just chat — they take actions: run commands, read/write files, browse the web, send messages, and call APIs, often triggered from a chat app like Telegram or Slack. In 2026 the two most popular open-source ones are Hermes Agent and OpenClaw. You asked whether they'd help run this business. Here's the honest answer.

Hermes Agent (Nous Research)

Open-source agent released Feb 2026. Runs on a $5 VPS (you already have a Hetzner box), one-line install, works with any model (OpenRouter, Claude, OpenAI, local). Has persistent memory, a self-improving "skills" loop, 40+ built-in tools, and talks to you over Telegram/Slack/WhatsApp/Discord/Signal/Email.

Verdict: Optional — useful as a back-office assistant.

More stable than OpenClaw and built for always-on background tasks. It overlaps with what n8n already does for you, so it's a "nice to have," not required.

OpenClaw

Open-source agent that went viral in early 2026 (most-starred project on GitHub). More powerful on paper — multi-agent, 13,000+ community "skills," runs locally with deep access to your files and OS.

Verdict: Avoid for this business (security).

2026 brought documented incidents: malicious skill packages on "ClawHub," leaked plaintext API keys, the "ClawJacked" hijack, and 20,000+ instances exposed on the open internet. Too risky for a business holding client phone access and PII.

🔐 Security rules if you run ANY autonomous agent

  • • Run it on an isolated VPS, never your main laptop or production server.
  • • Give it scoped, read-mostly access — never your live Vapi/Twilio/Stripe keys or client databases with write access.
  • • Never expose its control port to the internet. Most real-world breaches are misconfiguration, not exotic hacks.
  • • Treat community "skills/plugins" as untrusted code. Don't install random ones.
  • • Keep a human approving anything that contacts a client or moves money.

What an AI Ops Assistant Could Actually Do For You

If you do add Hermes Agent on a cheap VPS, point it at your own internal data only and let it handle low-stakes, repetitive back-office work, pinging you on Telegram:

Nightly health check: "Did every client's AI agent answer test calls today?"

Draft each client's monthly report from Supabase data for your review

Summarize the day's new leads and flag the hottest ones

Watch n8n/Supabase and alert you the moment something breaks

Draft follow-up emails to prospects who went quiet (you approve & send)

Compile a weekly "state of the business" digest

Lesson 5: Copy-Paste AI Prompt Library

Never start from a blank page. Paste these into Claude (or your tool of choice), fill in the brackets, and go. Hit Copy on any block.

1. Turn reviews into personalized cold-email lines

You are writing the personalized first line of a cold email to home-service businesses. I will paste a list of businesses with their Google reviews. For each business, do this: 1. Scan the reviews for any sign of a missed-call, slow-response, or "couldn't reach them" problem. 2. If found, write ONE friendly opening line that references it without being creepy. Example: "Saw a couple of your reviews mention trouble reaching the office after hours —" 3. If no call-related complaint exists, write a neutral opener that compliments their rating. Output a table: Business name | Opening line | Signal found (yes/no). Keep lines under 20 words, natural, never salesy. [PASTE BUSINESS + REVIEW DATA HERE]

2. Research a niche + metro before you target it

Act as a market researcher. I run an AI phone-receptionist agency selling to home-service businesses. Research [TRADE, e.g. HVAC] in [CITY/METRO]: - Roughly how many such businesses operate there - Typical job/ticket value for this trade - How seasonal demand works (peak months) - Whether the market has many Hispanic-owned businesses (bilingual angle) - Any existing AI-receptionist competitors targeting them, and their pricing - The 3 strongest talking points I should lead with for this trade Cite sources. Flag anything uncertain.

3. Build the Missed-Call ROI Calculator (for Claude Artifacts / Lovable)

Build an interactive "Missed Call Revenue Calculator" web app. Inputs: calls/week, % missed (default 30%), avg job value $, close rate (default 40%). Live output: missed calls/month + /year, lost revenue/month + /year, and a bold headline "You're losing about $X/year in missed calls." Add a CTA button "Book a 15-min demo" and an email-capture field "Email me my results." Clean, mobile-first, blue/emerald accents, big numbers.

4. Write a 4-email cold sequence

Write a 4-email cold outreach sequence for [TRADE] businesses in [CITY]. We sell a bilingual (English/Spanish) AI phone receptionist that answers 24/7, books appointments, and texts confirmations, for ~$1,000/mo. Email 1: lead with the missed-call problem + a specific dollar figure they're losing. Email 2: short proof/case-study angle ("an HVAC co. in [city] captured 47 after-hours calls"). Email 3: the bilingual angle + offer a 2-minute demo. Email 4: breakup email. Each under 90 words, plain text, one clear CTA, casual and human (not corporate). Include 3 subject-line options per email.

5. Generate an SOP from messy notes

Turn my rough notes into a clean, numbered Standard Operating Procedure a new VA could follow with zero context. Include: purpose, tools needed, step-by-step instructions, common mistakes to avoid, and a definition-of-done checklist. Format with clear headings. Here are my notes: [PASTE NOTES]

6. Prep for a discovery call (research a prospect)

I have a discovery call with [BUSINESS NAME], a [TRADE] company in [CITY]. Based on the info below, give me: - 3 likely pain points for a business this size - 5 smart discovery questions to ask - The ROI math I should walk them through (estimate their missed-call losses) - 2 likely objections and how to answer them [PASTE WHATEVER YOU KNOW: website text, reviews, size, hours]

7. Spec an n8n workflow for Claude Code to build

I use n8n, Vapi, Twilio, Supabase, and Cal.com. Design a workflow that: when a Vapi call ends, receive the webhook, extract caller name/number/intent, write a row to Supabase 'calls' table, and if an appointment was requested, create a Cal.com booking and send a confirmation SMS via Twilio. List the nodes in order, the data mapping between them, and any edge cases I should handle (missing fields, duplicate calls, after-hours).

Pro move

Save these as saved prompts / a Claude Project so Paola and Mike both reuse the exact same wording. Consistency is what makes a 2-person team feel like a system.

The 2026 Trends Radar: What to Sell, Watch, and Ignore

The AI agency space reinvents itself every six months. The skill isn't chasing every trend — it's knowing which ones make you money this quarter, which to watch, and which are noise. Here's the radar as of mid-2026, plus the ritual for keeping it current yourself.

Sell Now: "AI Employee" Positioning

The biggest shift of 2026 isn't a tool — it's the framing. Winning agencies stopped selling "automation software" and started selling headcount replacement. GoHighLevel literally sells a product called "AI Employee." The reframe changes your price anchor entirely:

Old FramingAI Employee Framing
"AI phone answering software, $497/mo""A front-desk employee who never sleeps. A human receptionist runs $2,800-3,600/mo all-in — yours is $497."
"The system books appointments""Meet Ava. She answers every call, speaks Spanish, and texts you each booking." Named agents get owner buy-in and fewer cancellation conversations.
Compared against $149/mo DIY toolsCompared against a salary. You're not the expensive option anymore — you're 85% cheaper than the alternative they understand.

Rename the offer in your proposals: "Your AI Front Desk Employee" instead of "AI receptionist service"

Give every client's agent a name and a one-line "job description" in the onboarding doc

Anchor every pitch against the cost of the human equivalent, never against software

Sell Now: The Trend Service Lines Already in This Playbook

AI Search Visibility (GEO) — the fastest-growing line item in local marketing, and almost no local agency offers it yet. Full playbook: AI Search Visibility.

Database Reactivation — the 2026 evolution is two-way AI conversation instead of dumb SMS blasts, and always-on retainers instead of one-off campaigns. Full playbook: Database Reactivation.

Speed-to-Lead — still underexploited; lead costs on Angi/Thumbtack keep rising, which makes the pitch stronger every year. Full playbook: Speed-to-Lead.

Watch: MCP and the Agent Infrastructure Wave

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the USB port of the agent era — an open standard (now under the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation) that lets any AI model plug into any tool. Adoption exploded to tens of millions of SDK downloads a month, and ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot all speak it. What it means for you, practically:

n8n is now an agent-orchestration platform (n8n 2.0 added 70+ AI nodes and persistent agent memory) — your existing stack ages well; no migration needed

When a client asks "can your AI check our inventory system / CRM / QuickBooks?", the honest 2026 answer is increasingly "yes, via MCP" — this unlocks the agentic premium tier for bigger clients

Computer-use agents (Claude computer use, ChatGPT agent mode) are real but still slow and brittle — fine for your own back-office research, not yet something to sell SMBs as a product. Revisit every 6 months.

Watch: The Compliance Wave (This One's Mandatory)

RuleWhat It SaysWhat You Do
FCC: AI voices = TCPA "artificial voices"Outbound AI voice calls need prior express consent. $500-1,500 per call in statutory damages.Inbound answering: low risk. Outbound AI calls: only to people who submitted a request or replied YES. Never to cold lists.
FCC revocation rule (Apr 2025)Consumers can revoke consent by any reasonable phrase ("stop," "cancel," "no more"); honor within 10 days.Your n8n STOP-handling should catch variants, not just "STOP." Claude classifies opt-out intent on every inbound reply.
State AI disclosure laws (Utah safe harbor; CA AB 2905 for AI voice)Utah: self-identify as AI at the outset = safe harbor. CA AB 2905: outbound AI-voice calls must disclose the artificial voice up front. (Companion-bot laws like CA SB 243 / WA / OR generally don't apply to a receptionist.)Your agents already self-identify as AI assistants — keep it that way, in every script, in both languages. Make "the AI always says it's an AI" a selling point: compliance done-for-you.

Turn compliance into revenue: most DIY owners and cheap competitors have never heard of any of this. A "compliance-included" line in your proposal beats a $149/mo DIY tool that leaves the owner holding TCPA liability.

The Vendor-Risk Lesson (Learn It Cheap)

Two cautionary tales from the last 12 months: Bland restructured its entire pricing into tiers overnight, and OpenAI announced it's sunsetting its Agent Builder barely a year after launch. Agencies that had built their whole delivery on one vendor's proprietary tooling had to rebuild mid-contract. Your protections:

Own the client relationship and the phone number — clients sign with Colibri Code, numbers live in your Twilio, and any vendor underneath is swappable

Keep prompts, workflows, and data portable — agent scripts in your repo, workflows in n8n (self-hosted), data in Supabase. Migrating voice platforms is then a 1-2 day job, not a crisis

Re-check the platform comparison quarterly (Voice Platform Showdown) — per-minute pricing moved meaningfully three times in 18 months

Pick at most ONE new thing to test on your own agency before selling it to anyone

Check your three platforms' pricing pages (Vapi, Twilio, Anthropic) for changes — reprice add-ons if your costs moved >20%

Ask your best client: "What are other vendors pitching you lately?" — the cheapest competitive intelligence that exists

Anything that threatens my core offer (e.g., platforms selling direct to SMBs, big players entering local AI) For each: what it is, why it matters to a 2-person agency, and a one-line recommended action. Rank by revenue impact. Cite sources.

The Meta-Rule

Every trend above passes the same filter: does it use the stack we already run, and does it attack money the client can already see leaking? AI Employee framing, GEO, DBR, and Speed-to-Lead all pass. Crypto-adjacent AI, "autonomous business" hype, and tools without a clear SMB pain point all fail. When something new appears, apply the filter before the excitement.

Knowledge Check Module 9: AI Leverage

You want to fill your pipeline fast. Which approach is both effective AND legally safe for prospecting US home-service businesses?

Correct! Cheap, effective, and compliant. AI cold-calling violates the TCPA (AI = "artificial voice"), AI SDRs are overpriced for a tiny shop, and handing live keys to OpenClaw is a security disaster. The data-to-email pipeline wins.
Not safe. AI voice cold-calling breaks the TCPA ($500–$1,500/call), AI SDRs are overpriced and generic, and giving an autonomous agent your live credentials is a security risk. The safe play: Outscraper → Claude on reviews → Twilio hang-up audit → compliant cold email.

Scale & Income Streams

Turn one service into a revenue stack: nine income streams, productized delivery, a hiring ladder, acquisition-channel economics, cheat sheets, the master tool directory, and your exit options

4 hours Advanced 7 Lessons
What You'll Learn
  • Stack nine income streams in the right order (and when each unlocks)
  • Productize delivery so one operator can run 15-20 clients

The Revenue Stack: Nine Income Streams, One Asset Base

A single-service agency is fragile: one churn wave or one platform price change and your month is ruined. A scalable agency layers income streams that all reuse the same assets — your prospect list, your Vapi templates, your n8n workflows, your client relationships. Nothing here requires building a second business. Each stream is the same business, monetized again.

The two rules of stacking: (1) Never add a stream until the previous one runs without you thinking about it — a half-systemized stream is a liability, not income. (2) Every new stream must reuse an asset you already have. If it needs a new audience, new tooling, AND new skills, it's a different business wearing your logo.
